section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which agency handles driver licensing and permits in Maine?
options: a:Maine DMV,b:Maine Bureau of Motor Vehicles (BMV),c:Maine DOT,d:Maine Secretary of State
note: Maine's Bureau of Motor Vehicles (BMV), part of the Secretary of State's office, handles driver licensing, vehicle registration, and permits. If you need a permit or license in Maine, visit a BMV office.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum age to apply for a Maine learner's permit?
options: a:14,b:15,c:16,d:15 and a half
note: Maine allows teens to apply for a learner's permit at age 15. The permit allows supervised driving practice as the first step in Maine's GDL program.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Maine's real BMV knowledge test has exactly 30 questions. How many must you answer correctly to pass?
note: Maine's BMV knowledge test has 30 questions and requires 24 correct answers — an 80% passing threshold. You can miss up to 6 questions. Missing 7 or more means you fail and must wait to retake the test.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal BAC limit for a Maine driver age 21 or older?
note: Maine sets the OUI (Operating Under the Influence) limit at 0.08% BAC for drivers 21 and older. Maine uses the term OUI rather than DUI. Commercial drivers face a stricter 0.04% limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Maine uses the term 'OUI' for drunk driving. What does OUI stand for?
options: a:Operating Under Influence,b:Offense Under Intoxication,c:Operating Unlawfully Impaired,d:Operating Under Intoxicants
note: Maine uses the term OUI — Operating Under the Influence — rather than DUI or DWI. The concept is the same: operating a motor vehicle while impaired by alcohol or drugs, or with a BAC of 0.08% or higher.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What BAC level triggers Maine's zero tolerance law for drivers under 21?
note: Maine sets the underage OUI threshold at 0.02% BAC for drivers under 21. This is effectively zero — any measurable alcohol is prohibited for underage drivers in Maine.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Maine's GDL program, how many hours of supervised driving must a permit holder complete?
options: a:30 hours (no night requirement),b:70 hours (including 10 at night),c:30 hours (5 at night),d:No minimum hour requirement
note: Maine requires 70 hours of supervised driving practice — one of the highest requirements in the country — with at least 10 hours driven at night. The supervising driver must be a licensed adult age 20 or older. These hours must be logged and certified before advancing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit on Maine urban streets when no sign is posted?
options: a:25 mph,b:30 mph,c:35 mph,d:45 mph
note: Maine sets the default speed limit in urban and business areas at 30 mph when no sign is posted. On rural roads, the default is 45 mph — lower than many states. Always check for posted signs, and use these defaults when no sign is visible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is notable about Maine's default rural road speed limit compared to most other states?
options: a:Maine has the highest rural default at 65 mph,b:Maine's rural default is 45 mph — lower than the 55 mph used by most states,c:Maine has no default — all roads must be posted,d:Maine's rural default is 55 mph, the same as most states
note: Maine's default speed limit on rural roads is 45 mph — lower than the 55 mph default used by most other states. This reflects Maine's road conditions, wildlife hazards, and narrower rural roads. Always look for posted signs, but the default is 45 mph on unposted rural roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You approach a school bus stopped on an undivided road with flashing red lights. What must you do?
options: a:Stop only if you are behind the bus,b:Stop in both directions at least 25 feet from the bus,c:Slow to 15 mph and pass carefully,d:Stop only if children are visible outside
note: Maine law requires all vehicles in both directions on an undivided road to stop at least 25 feet from a school bus displaying flashing red lights. Wait until the stop arm retracts and the lights stop before proceeding. On a divided highway, only traffic behind the bus must stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Maine's Move Over law requires you to do what when approaching a stationary emergency vehicle with flashing lights?
options: a:Slow to 20 mph,b:Move one lane away if safe, or reduce speed if a lane change is not possible,c:Stop completely behind the vehicle,d:Only required for police — not tow trucks
note: Maine's Move Over law requires drivers to move one lane away from stationary emergency, law enforcement, utility, or tow vehicles with flashing lights. If a safe lane change is not possible, reduce speed significantly. The law applies to all such vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must Maine drivers use their headlights?
options: a:Only from sunset to sunrise,b:From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, and when visibility is under 500 feet,c:Only in rain and fog,d:Only between 10 PM and 5 AM
note: Maine requires headlights from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise, and anytime visibility is less than 500 feet due to weather. This includes rain, fog, snow, and other conditions reducing visibility — not just complete darkness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum recommended following distance in Maine under normal conditions?
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: Maine recommends a minimum 3-second following distance under normal conditions. In Maine's challenging weather — rain, snow, ice, and fog — increase following distance to 6 seconds or more. The 3-second rule provides the bare minimum reaction time to stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution,b:Yield to cross traffic and proceed,c:Come to a complete stop, yield to all traffic, and proceed when safe,d:Continue at the posted speed
note: A flashing red signal in Maine is treated like a stop sign. Make a complete stop, yield to all traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when the way is clear. A flashing yellow means caution — slow down but a full stop is not required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane road in Maine, when may you legally cross a solid yellow line on your side?
options: a:When the road ahead is visible for at least 500 feet,b:You may never cross a solid yellow line on your side to pass,c:When the vehicle ahead is going well below the speed limit,d:When you signal at least 200 feet in advance
note: A solid yellow line on your side is an absolute prohibition on crossing the center line to pass. No exceptions. Only when the yellow line on your side is broken (dashed) may you pass when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Maine seatbelt law requires which vehicle occupants to wear a seatbelt?
options: a:Driver and front-seat passengers only,b:All occupants in the vehicle,c:Only those under 18,d:Driver only
note: Maine requires all vehicle occupants — in all seating positions — to wear a seatbelt. Maine has primary enforcement. Children under 40 pounds or under age 2 must be in a rear-facing child safety seat; children under 8 or under 80 pounds must use a booster seat.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches from behind, you must:
options: a:Speed up to the next intersection and pull over,b:Pull to the right edge of the road and stop,c:Slow to 10 mph and stay in your lane,d:Move to the center of the road
note: Maine law requires you to immediately pull to the right edge of the road and stop when an emergency vehicle with active lights and siren approaches. Remain stopped until the vehicle has passed. If you are in an intersection, clear it first, then pull to the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Can you make a right turn on a red light in Maine?
options: a:No, right turns on red are prohibited statewide,b:Yes, after a complete stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, unless a sign prohibits it,c:Yes, without stopping if the turn is clear,d:Only during daytime
note: Right turns on red are permitted in Maine after a complete stop, yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic, and only when no 'No Turn on Red' sign is posted. Always make a full stop — rolling through on red while turning right is illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Maine is known for severe winters. When driving on snow or ice in Maine, what should you do first?
options: a:Maintain the posted speed limit to keep up with traffic,b:Significantly reduce speed and increase following distance,c:Use hazard flashers and maintain speed,d:Use high beams to see further ahead
note: In Maine's severe winter conditions — snow, ice, and sleet — significantly reduce your speed well below the posted limit and increase your following distance to 8–10 seconds or more. Stopping distances on ice can be 10 times longer than on dry pavement. Slow down and allow extra space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit on Maine rural interstate highways?
options: a:55 mph,b:60 mph,c:65 mph,d:70 mph
note: Maine's maximum speed limit on rural interstate highways is 65 mph for passenger vehicles. This is lower than many other states, reflecting Maine's road conditions and terrain. Some sections may have lower posted limits. Always check posted signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Maine, what does a flashing yellow arrow traffic signal indicate?
options: a:You must stop before turning in the arrow direction,b:You may turn in the arrow direction but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians,c:You have a protected turn — oncoming traffic is stopped,d:The signal is malfunctioning — proceed with caution
note: A flashing yellow arrow is a permissive turn signal. You may turn in the arrow direction but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. This differs from a solid green arrow (protected turn) where oncoming traffic is held by a red light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Maine law requires drivers to signal before turning or changing lanes at least how far in advance?
options: a:50 feet,b:100 feet,c:200 feet,d:300 feet
note: Maine law requires drivers to signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes. On higher-speed roads, signaling even earlier is advisable to give other drivers sufficient warning time to adjust.

question: Is it true that every motor vehicle in Maine must have liability insurance?
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only trucks must have insurance.
note: Maine law requires that any motor vehicle operated on public roads be covered by liability insurance. This insurance helps pay for injuries or damage you may cause to others in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving in heavy rain in Maine. Maine law requires headlights when:
options: a:Visibility drops below 200 feet only,b:Windshield wipers are in use due to precipitation,c:Only after sunset regardless of rain,d:Only when driving on highways in the rain
note: Maine law requires headlights to be on whenever windshield wipers are in use due to precipitation. This 'wipers on, lights on' rule ensures your vehicle is visible to other drivers in wet conditions — even during daylight hours when you might otherwise not think to turn on lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in fog in Maine, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beams for maximum visibility,b:Low beams or fog lights,c:Hazard flashers only,d:No lights — they reflect off fog
note: In Maine's frequent coastal and morning fog, use low beams or dedicated fog lights. High beams reflect off fog particles, creating glare. Fog lights have a lower, wider beam pattern that cuts under fog layers for improved visibility. Also reduce speed significantly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Maine, what happens to your license if you refuse a chemical test after being lawfully stopped for OUI?
options: a:No penalty — refusal is a protected right,b:275-day license suspension for a first offense refusal,c:Minor fine only,d:You lose your license only if convicted of OUI
note: Maine's implied consent law means refusing a chemical test after an OUI stop results in a 275-day license suspension for a first offense — separate from any OUI conviction. Refusal can also be used against you in court. It is rarely in a driver's best interest to refuse.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian is crossing in a marked crosswalk. You must:
options: a:Proceed if you have the right of way,b:Slow to 20 mph and pass carefully,c:Stop and yield until the pedestrian has completely cleared the roadway,d:Yield only if the pedestrian is directly in your path
note: Maine law requires drivers to stop and yield to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk. You must remain stopped until the pedestrian has completely cleared the roadway — not just your lane. Pedestrian right-of-way in a crosswalk is absolute.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Maine requires permit holders to log 70 hours of supervised driving — what makes this notable?
options: a:70 hours is the national average,b:70 hours is among the highest supervised driving requirements in the country,c:Most states require more than 70 hours,d:Maine recently reduced the requirement from 100 hours to 70
note: Maine's 70-hour supervised driving requirement is among the highest in the United States. Most states require 40–50 hours. Maine's higher requirement reflects the state's challenging driving conditions — severe winters, rural roads, and wildlife hazards — that demand extensive preparation before independent driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the shape and color of a standard 'No Passing Zone' sign in Maine?
options: a:Diamond, yellow,b:Rectangle, white,c:Pennant (triangle), yellow — placed on the left side of the road,d:Circle, yellow with an X
note: The No Passing Zone sign is a yellow pennant (triangle) shape, always placed on the left side of the road at the beginning of a no-passing zone. It is the only pennant-shaped sign in the U.S. road sign system — making it unique and instantly recognizable as a passing restriction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as a vehicle to your right. Who has priority?
options: a:You do — you are both there at the same time,b:The vehicle on your right has the right of way,c:Whoever is going straight has priority,d:The driver who arrived from the main road goes first
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at a 4-way stop, yield to the vehicle on the right. This is the universal tie-breaking rule at all-way stops. If you arrived clearly before the other driver, you proceed first regardless of direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when you see a yellow diamond-shaped sign near a railroad crossing?
options: a:Stop immediately at the tracks,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching,c:Proceed at normal speed — it is just an advisory sign,d:Turn around — trains have the absolute right of way
note: A yellow diamond-shaped railroad crossing warning sign advises you to slow down and be prepared to stop. The sign is typically placed 500 feet before the crossing to give you advance warning. Approach all railroad crossings with caution and be prepared to stop if signals activate.

question: Which of the following is NOT a factor in determining stopping distance?
options: a:Braking distance.,b:Reaction distance.,c:Steering ability.
note: Total stopping distance is how far your vehicle travels from the moment you see a hazard until you come to a complete stop. It includes perception time, reaction distance (how far you travel while moving your foot to the brake), and braking distance (how far you travel while the brakes slow the car). Steering ability does not directly determine stopping distance.

question: If you encounter a flooded roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Drive through slowly and carefully.,b:Turn around and find another route.,c:Drive until the water looks too deep.
note: If a road is flooded, do not try to judge the depth or drive through it. Even shallow water can hide hazards, stall your vehicle, or sweep it away. The safest choice is to turn around and find another route.

question: What helps you avoid having to make emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Looking far ahead and maintaining a safe following distance.,b:Honk to get drivers ahead to move faster.,c:Drive only in the right lane.,d:Constantly weaving between lanes.
note: Looking well ahead and keeping a safe following distance gives you time to see problems early and slow or change lanes smoothly, instead of slamming on the brakes for an emergency stop.

question: How can drivers adjust their behavior to travel more safely in winter weather?
options: a:Increase their following distances.,b:Operate at slower speeds.,c:Stop and turn more gently.,d:All of the above.
note: Winter conditions reduce traction and increase stopping distance. To stay safe, you should slow down, increase your following distance, and brake, accelerate, and turn more gently so you are less likely to skid.

question: If you see pedestrians close to the road where you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and pass with caution.,b:Sound your horn and maintain your speed.,c:Speed up to clear the area quickly.
note: When pedestrians are near the road, you should slow down, be prepared to stop, and pass with extra caution. Use your horn only if needed to prevent a collision, not to force pedestrians to hurry or to keep your speed.

question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:At all times when pedestrians are in the crosswalk.,b:Only when pedestrians are waving you on.,c:Only if the pedestrian is not distracted.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are in a marked or unmarked crosswalk. Slow or stop as needed and allow them to cross completely and safely before you proceed.

question: What is the only medically proven method to reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Give your body time.,c:Breathe in fresh air.
note: Time is the only thing that lowers your blood alcohol concentration. Your body must metabolize the alcohol, and nothing speeds this up—not coffee, cold showers, food, or fresh air. Until enough time passes, you remain impaired.

question: While driving down a long or steep hill, what should you be especially alert to?
options: a:Assume all traffic is maintaining a consistent speed.,b:Watch over your shoulder for traffic behind you.,c:Check your mirrors and be prepared for vehicles gaining speed behind you.
note: On long or steep hills, vehicles often pick up speed, and some drivers may ride their brakes or lose control. You should check your mirrors regularly so you can spot fast‑approaching traffic from behind and adjust your speed or lane position early to avoid conflicts.

question: If the driver ahead is distracted (driving with one hand, talking to a passenger), you should:
options: a:Follow their example more closely.,b:Attempt to pass immediately.,c:Give the vehicle extra space.
note: A distracted driver is more likely to drift, brake suddenly, or miss traffic signals. By giving them extra space, you create a safety buffer so you have more time and room to react if they make a mistake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Adjust your mirrors.,c:You may proceed through the intersection if it is clear.
note: A steady green light means you may go if the intersection is clear, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection. Green never means to speed up or ignore other road users.

question: True or false: Solid pavement lines separating lanes indicate a no-passing zone.
options: a:False,b:True (for solid center lines that control passing zones between opposing directions of traffic)
note: A solid center line on your side of the road means you must not cross it to pass because visibility or road conditions make passing unsafe. A dashed center line on your side means you may pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?
options: a:Alcohol has no effect on nighttime driving.,b:If you can walk a straight line,c:Alcohol impairs judgment required for safe driving.,d:If you are below the legal BAC limit
note: Alcohol slows reaction time and impairs judgment, coordination, and vision. Even small amounts can affect your ability to make safe driving decisions, especially at night. You should never assume you are safe to drive just because you feel okay or are under the legal BAC limit.

question: If you want to pass a pedestrian and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, what should you do first?
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.,b:Maintain steady speed and pass the pedestrian immediately.,c:Honk to get the pedestrian to move, then pass.,d:Drive onto the shoulder to pass the pedestrian.
note: When you face multiple hazards, deal with them one at a time. If a pedestrian is ahead and a vehicle is coming toward you, slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first. Once the lane is clear and it is safe, then pass the pedestrian while giving plenty of space and driving at a safe speed.

question: What should you do first when visibility is reduced?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Turn on your windshield wipers only.,c:Turn on your high beam headlights.,d:Turn on your low beam headlights and hazard lights.
note: When visibility drops due to fog, heavy rain, snow, or darkness, your first response should be to slow down. Reducing speed gives you more time to see and react to hazards. After slowing, you can use appropriate lights and wipers as needed, but speed reduction is the primary safety step.

question: When backing your vehicle, what is the correct visual technique?
options: a:Put your head out the driver's side window.,b:Only use a backup camera and no visual checks.,c:Rely only on your mirrors.,d:Look over your shoulder and out the rear window.
note: When backing, turn your body and look over your right shoulder through the rear window so you can directly see the path behind you. Use mirrors and cameras only as supplements. Back slowly and be prepared to stop if you lose sight of any area you are moving into.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are you ever allowed to drive off the road onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Yes, whenever you are in a hurry.,b:No, you must stay on the paved roadway when passing.,c:Only if the vehicle ahead is turning left and the shoulder is paved and open to traffic.,d:Only on freeways.
note: You must stay on the paved roadway when passing. Driving onto the shoulder to pass is illegal in most situations and very dangerous because shoulders are for emergencies and may hide pedestrians, cyclists, or stopped vehicles. If you cannot safely pass in your lane, wait until conditions improve.

question: A diamond-shaped road sign is used to indicate what?
options: a:Interstate route marker.,b:School crossing sign.,c:Warning or road hazard ahead.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are standard warning signs. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards or changes in road conditions, such as curves, merging traffic, or pedestrian crossings, so you can adjust speed and be prepared.

question: When parallel parking between two vehicles, what should you do first?
options: a:Pull up even with the vehicle in front of the desired space.,b:Turn your wheels sharply to the left immediately.,c:Turn your wheels sharply to the right immediately.
note: For parallel parking, after you choose a space and check traffic, you first pull up parallel and even with the vehicle in front of the space. From this position you can then back slowly while turning the wheel to angle your car into the space.

question: At a railroad crossing that lacks signals, what should you do as you approach?
options: a:Assume crossings always have signals so no special action is needed.,b:Always come to a full stop whether you see a train or not.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop while checking for trains.
note: At a railroad crossing without gates or lights, you must slow down, look and listen for trains in both directions, and be ready to stop. Never assume the tracks are clear; only proceed when you are sure no train is coming.

question: As blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, you become:
options: a:Less likely to be detected.,b:More intoxicated and more impaired.,c:More sober.,d:More coordinated.
note: As BAC increases, alcohol affects your brain more, reducing judgment, slowing reaction time, and harming coordination. Even small increases in BAC make you more impaired and less able to drive safely.

question: Which of these affects braking distance?
options: a:All of the above.,b:The condition of your brakes and tires.,c:The speed your vehicle is traveling.,d:The condition of the pavement.
note: Braking distance increases with higher speed and is also affected by how well your brakes and tires work and how good or bad the road surface is. Worn brakes or tires and wet or icy pavement all make it take longer to stop.

question: To improve visibility reduced by rain or fog, which lights should drivers use?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:Fog lights only regardless of conditions.,c:High beam headlights.,d:Low beam headlights.
note: In rain, fog, snow, or sleet, you should use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and improve your ability to see and be seen by others.

question: When should you allow extra space in front of your vehicle because of the vehicle ahead?
options: a:When following a compact hatchback.,b:When following a small passenger car.,c:When following a motorcycle.,d:When following a bicycle on the shoulder.
note: You should allow extra following distance behind motorcycles because they are smaller and harder to see, and they can stop or swerve more quickly than larger vehicles. Extra space gives you more time to react if the motorcycle slows or stops suddenly.

question: Drowsiness while driving, like alcohol or drugs, can:
options: a:Improve concentration.,b:Make you a better driver.,c:Impair judgment,d:Have no impact on driving safety.
note: Drowsiness slows your reaction time, narrows your attention, and impairs judgment, much like alcohol or drugs. Driving while very tired can be as dangerous as driving while intoxicated because you may react too slowly or make poor decisions.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?
options: a:They alert drivers to potential tire problems.,b:They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,c:They warn drivers through vibration and sound that they are leaving the lane or approaching a hazard.
note: Rumble strips are raised or grooved patterns on the road that create vibration and noise when you drive over them. This alerts drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are drifting out of their lane or approaching a hazard, such as a stop sign, toll plaza, or work zone.

question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:
options: a:Increase the effects of both and make driving more dangerous.,b:Decrease the effects of both.,c:Help relieve your illness.,d:Have no effect on impairment.
note: Combining alcohol with many prescription, over‑the‑counter, or illegal drugs can greatly increase impairment. The substances can interact and intensify each other’s effects, making you much less alert and more likely to lose control of the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why should you signal continuously while making a turn?
options: a:It lets other road users know your intentions.,b:Because it is always unsafe to turn off a signal early.,c:Because it is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.
note: Signaling gives drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians advance notice of your intended action, reducing the chance of conflicts.

question: When near a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog you should:
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Take the right-of-way.,c:Proceed at normal speed.
note: When you see a blind pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog, you must slow down, be prepared to stop, and always yield the right‑of‑way. Blind pedestrians may be listening for traffic sounds to decide when it is safe to cross, so sudden movements or failing to yield can be especially dangerous. Never try to assert your right‑of‑way around a blind pedestrian.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If stopped by a police officer, you should:
options: a:Get your paperwork out before the officer reaches your car.,b:Unbuckle and get out immediately.,c:Stay in your vehicle with your hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
note: If you are stopped by a police officer, stay in your vehicle unless the officer instructs you otherwise. Keep your hands visible, usually on the steering wheel, and wait for directions. Do not start reaching for your license, registration, or other documents until the officer asks you to; sudden movements can cause concern for the officer’s safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and its stop arm extended, you must:
options: a:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are visible.,b:Slow and continue while watching for children.,c:Stop and remain stopped until signals are withdrawn.
note: When you approach a school bus with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. This rule protects children who may be crossing the road and might not be easily seen. In most situations, traffic in both directions must stop unless a specific state law and a physical median or barrier provide an exception.

question: What do round road signs typically indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones.,c:Upcoming railroad crossings.
note: Round traffic signs are used for railroad crossing warnings. When you see a round yellow sign with a black X and the letters “RR,” it means you are approaching a railroad crossing and should slow down, look, and listen for trains. Other shapes, such as pennant‑shaped signs, are used for no‑passing zones, and pentagon‑shaped signs are used for school zones.

question: Blind spots are:
options: a:Areas around your vehicle that cannot be seen in the vehicle's mirrors.,b:Spots in your vision caused by fatigue.,c:Traffic control devices.
note: Blind spots are the areas around your vehicle that you cannot see using your mirrors alone. To check them, you must quickly glance over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging, so you don’t miss vehicles, motorcycles, bicycles, or pedestrians traveling beside you.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly in an emergency, what is the correct technique?
options: a:Hold down the brake pedal without releasing.,b:Lightly tap the brakes.,c:Firmly pump your brakes.
note: In a vehicle without ABS, you should use the "pump" or threshold braking technique in an emergency stop: apply firm pressure to the brake pedal just short of wheel lockup, then release slightly and reapply. This helps you slow quickly while still being able to steer and avoid skidding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is parking prohibited among these options?
options: a:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a hill.
note: You may not park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane because these areas must remain clear for pedestrians and cyclists. Parking on a hill is allowed if it is not otherwise prohibited and you park legally: set the parking brake, turn your wheels correctly, and follow any posted signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers turning left must yield to:
options: a:Only vehicles turning left,b:Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.,c:No one in particular.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, and also to pedestrians crossing the street you are turning into. Only turn when there is a safe gap and the way is clear.

question: Who may park in spaces reserved for persons with disabilities?
options: a:Only vehicles displaying valid disabled plates or placards and transporting a person with a disability.,b:Any vehicle with a driver who intends to stop only briefly.
note: Parking in spaces reserved for persons with disabilities is only allowed for vehicles displaying valid disabled license plates or placards issued to a person with a disability. The person with the disability must be using the vehicle, either as a driver or passenger.

question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:You are moving faster than the bicycle.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:You must give bicycles extra space because they may swerve or be hard to see, and oncoming traffic may not expect you to pull out to pass.
note: You must be cautious when passing a bicycle because they are vulnerable road users and may need to swerve suddenly to avoid potholes, debris, or opening car doors. Oncoming traffic may also not expect you to move out to pass, so you must check carefully before pulling out and give the cyclist plenty of space.

question: Why should drivers be extra alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They can be difficult to see in traffic.,b:They always have different traffic laws.,c:They always have the right-of-way.
note: Smaller road users like motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians are harder to see, especially in blind spots, at night, or in heavy traffic. Because they are less protected, drivers must scan carefully, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield when required to avoid serious collisions.

question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection with working signals, you should:
options: a:Always obey the traffic light instead of the officer.,b:Follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic signal.,c:Honk to get the officer's attention.
note: When a police officer is directing traffic, their hand signals and directions override traffic lights and signs. You must follow the officer’s instructions, even if they conflict with the traffic signal, to keep traffic moving safely and avoid confusion.

question: When is turning or stopping most hazardous during rainy conditions?
options: a:After it has been raining all day.,b:One half hour after it stops raining.,c:During the first half hour of rain.
note: The first part of a rainstorm is usually the most dangerous. Oil and residue on the road mix with the first rain and create a very slippery surface, especially during the first 20–30 minutes. Use extra caution when turning or stopping during this time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light, you should:
options: a:Obey the red light instead of the officer.,b:Follow what the vehicle ahead of you does.,c:Stop and wait for the light to change.,d:Follow the officer's directions and proceed.
note: A police officer’s directions always override traffic signals and signs. If an officer tells you to go through a red light, you must follow the officer’s instructions, proceeding carefully as directed, because they are managing traffic for safety.

question: On major highways you should:
options: a:Drive the same speed regardless of conditions.,b:Stay alert,c:Look at one point ahead to focus.
note: Staying alert and continuously scanning the road is essential on highways to avoid highway hypnosis and to spot hazards early. Your speed and following distance should always be adjusted to traffic, weather, and road conditions.

question: What type of signs use an orange background?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:General destination signs.,c:Construction and maintenance warning signs.
note: Orange signs are temporary warning signs used in construction and maintenance zones. They alert drivers to road work, lane shifts, workers, and equipment so you can slow down and proceed with extra caution.

question: If you have had several beers, how will the effects of alcohol be reduced?
options: a:By taking a cold shower.,b:By waiting several hours.,c:By drinking several cups of coffee.
note: Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol. Cold showers, coffee, or exercise may make you feel more awake, but they do not lower your blood alcohol concentration. Plan ahead and allow several hours—or avoid drinking if you will need to drive.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:Whenever it may help prevent a collision.,b:To express frustration with a slow driver.,c:To get other drivers moving in a traffic jam.,d:To greet friends on the roadside.
note: Use your horn only to help prevent a collision or to alert other road users to your presence when necessary. Do not use it to express anger, impatience, or to greet people, as unnecessary honking can startle others and create unsafe situations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up and get through the intersection.,b:Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.,c:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right. Slowing down and letting that driver go first helps prevent confusion and collisions.

question: When driving past parked cars you should:
options: a:Honk to warn pedestrians,b:Assume others will yield to you.,c:Be prepared for people or vehicles to unexpectedly enter your lane.
note: When driving past parked cars, you should slow slightly and be ready for doors to open, cars to pull out, or pedestrians to step from between vehicles. Keeping extra space and being prepared to brake or steer safely helps you avoid sudden hazards.

question: You must stop at a railroad crossing in which of these situations?
options: a:Only if gates are present.,b:Only when there is a stop sign.,c:When directed to do so by a flagger.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing any time a flagger directs you to stop, when there is a stop sign requiring a stop, or when warning devices such as flashing red lights or gates are activated. Always obey all signals, signs, and instructions at railroad crossings, and never proceed until you are sure the tracks are clear and it is safe.

question: How close to a crosswalk may you not park?
options: a:10 feet,b:Five feet,c:15 feet
note: Many states prohibit parking within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection to keep sight lines clear for both drivers and pedestrians. Always check your state’s specific distance requirement, but remember that parking too close to a crosswalk makes it harder to see people entering the street and increases the risk of a collision.

question: In traffic flowing 50–55 mph, how are you least likely to be involved in a crash?
options: a:Drive a few miles per hour slower than most vehicles.,b:Drive a few miles per hour faster than most vehicles.,c:Stay within the common speed range of the traffic.
note: You are least likely to be involved in a crash when you travel at a speed similar to surrounding traffic, as long as it is within the posted speed limit and safe for conditions. Large speed differences—either faster or slower—force more lane changes and passing, which increases the chance of conflicts and collisions.

question: When you become too drowsy to drive safely, the best action is to:
options: a:Open all windows and crank the A/C.,b:Drink a large energy drink and continue driving.,c:Exit the roadway and rest.
note: Fatigue impairs reactions and judgment; the safest option is to stop and rest before continuing.

question: The first driving ability impaired by alcohol is:
options: a:Judgment,b:Vision,c:Balance
note: Alcohol affects the parts of the brain that control judgment and decision‑making before it noticeably affects coordination or vision. This means a driver may feel confident and take risks—such as speeding, tailgating, or unsafe passing—before realizing their abilities are reduced.

question: Under-21 drivers can have their license suspended for driving with what blood alcohol level?
options: a:Any detectable amount of alcohol.,b:0.08 percent or more.,c:0.15 percent or more.,d:Only if breath test confirms impairment.
note: Maine enforces a zero-tolerance law for drivers under 21: any detectable alcohol can result in penalties including license suspension.

question: After making an emergency roadside stop, is applying the parking brake optional?
options: a:False — you should set your parking brake during an emergency roadside stop.,b:True — the parking brake is not necessary.,c:Only apply it on hills.,d:Only use it if you plan to leave the vehicle.
note: When you make an emergency roadside stop, you should secure the vehicle by setting the parking brake and turning on your emergency flashers. The parking brake helps prevent the vehicle from rolling if it is bumped or if the ground is uneven, improving safety for you and other road users.

question: When you approach an octagonal sign, you must:
options: a:Turn immediately.,b:Come to a complete stop and yield to traffic and pedestrians.,c:Ignore it if no other cars are present.,d:Slow down and proceed without stopping.
note: An octagonal sign is always a STOP sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then yield to pedestrians and other traffic already in or close to the intersection before proceeding when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but there is no gap in traffic, you should:
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.,b:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Force other drivers to make room by maintaining speed.
note: You must not enter the freeway unless you can merge safely. If there is no gap in traffic by the time you reach the end of the ramp, you must stop (if necessary) and wait for a safe opening, then accelerate and merge. Never force your way in or expect other drivers to brake suddenly to let you in.

question: If a traffic light shows a green arrow and a red light, it means:
options: a:You must wait for a solid green light to go.,b:You may proceed only in the direction of the green arrow.,c:You may only drive straight ahead.
note: A green arrow with a red light means you may go only in the direction of the arrow, and only if the intersection is clear. The red light still applies to all other movements, so you must stop for any direction not indicated by the arrow.

question: Why must you use extra caution when you see a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:They are deaf and cannot hear your horn.,b:They are always police officers.,c:They may be blind and need the right-of-way.
note: A pedestrian with a white cane or a guide dog is likely blind or visually impaired. You must yield the right-of-way, be prepared to stop, and allow them to cross safely before proceeding.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights, where should you look?
options: a:Down at your dashboard and speedometer.,b:Directly at the headlights to signal them.,c:Toward the center of the roadway.,d:Toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, look toward the right edge of your lane, using the right side of the road as a guide. This reduces glare while still letting you see the roadway and stay in your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic on the freeway is merging into your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Always maintain your position.,b:Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.,c:Make room for the merging traffic if possible.
note: When traffic is merging into your lane on a freeway, you should, when safe, adjust your speed or change lanes to create space. Cooperating with merging traffic helps prevent sudden braking and reduces the risk of collisions.

question: The amount of alcohol in the blood is called:
options: a:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).,b:Implied consent (IC).,c:Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC).
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is the amount of alcohol in a person’s bloodstream. It is used by law enforcement to determine legal impairment and DUI violations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Never,b:Only at uncontrolled intersections.,c:Whenever yielding will help prevent a collision.
note: Drivers must be prepared to give up their legal right-of-way whenever it helps avoid a collision. You cannot rely on other road users to obey the rules perfectly, so if insisting on your right-of-way would create a risk, you should yield to keep everyone safe.

question: What is ''highway hypnosis'' and what causes it?
options: a:A condition that can be prevented by staying alert and taking regular breaks.,b:A result of getting too much sleep the night before driving.,c:A drowsy, trance-like state caused by fatigue and staring ahead for long periods without active scanning.
note: Highway hypnosis is a drowsy, trance-like state that can occur after driving long distances at steady speeds, especially on monotonous roads. It is caused by fatigue and staring straight ahead without actively scanning, which reduces alertness and makes it easier to miss hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The correct way to use a freeway exit ramp is to:
options: a:Reduce speed sharply before entering the ramp.,b:Maintain highway speed while on the ramp.,c:Slow down once you are on the exit ramp.
note: On a freeway, maintain a safe speed in the travel lane until you are actually on the exit ramp. Once on the ramp, slow down to the posted exit speed or to a safe speed for the curve. Slowing sharply while still on the freeway can surprise drivers behind you and cause rear-end collisions.

question: What colors are used for signs that indicate the distance to the next highway exit?
options: a:Blue with white letters.,b:Red with white letters.,c:Green with white letters.,d:Yellow with black letters.
note: Guide signs that show destinations and distances on highways are green with white letters or symbols. These signs help drivers know how far it is to upcoming exits, cities, and routes.

question: What must a driver do regarding pedestrians, even if the pedestrian is crossing improperly?
options: a:Flash headlights to make them move faster.,b:Stop only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,c:Yield the right-of-way and do everything to avoid striking them.,d:Ignore the pedestrian since they are wrong.
note: Drivers must always do everything reasonably possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, even if the pedestrian is crossing illegally or unsafely. You must slow down, yield, or stop if needed to prevent a collision, because protecting human life is more important than who has the right-of-way.

question: A red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection or any marked crosswalk or stop line.,b:Stop only if pedestrians are present.,c:Slow down and proceed if the road looks clear.
note: A steady red traffic signal means you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection, crosswalk, or at the stop line, and remain stopped until the light turns green or you are otherwise legally allowed to proceed (such as a permitted right turn on red where allowed).

question: What is the shape of a stop sign?
options: a:Octagon,b:Square,c:Circle,d:Rectangle
note: A stop sign is always an octagon (eight-sided). This unique shape helps drivers recognize it quickly, even if visibility is poor or the sign is partially blocked.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid out of control, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Apply the brakes lightly.,c:Stay off the brakes.
note: When your vehicle begins to skid, you should stay off the brakes. Braking hard can lock the wheels and make the skid worse. Instead, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. Once you regain traction and control, you can brake gently if needed.

question: A stopped school bus ahead in your lane displays flashing red lights. What must you do?
options: a:Stop for as long as the red lights are flashing.,b:Stop and proceed when you think all children have exited the bus.,c:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.
note: When a school bus in your lane (or on an undivided road in either direction) has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the bus moves or the driver signals you to proceed. The main exception is when you are on the opposite side of a divided highway with a physical median.

question: On a road without sidewalks, pedestrians should walk on:
options: a:The same side as vehicle traffic.,b:The side with the lightest traffic.,c:The side facing oncoming traffic.
note: On roads without sidewalks, pedestrians should walk facing oncoming traffic. This allows them to see approaching vehicles and react if a driver drifts toward the edge of the road.

question: A lane-use control signal displaying a solid yellow X means what?
options: a:Drivers may use the lane only to make left turns.,b:The lane signal is about to change to a red X; clear the lane.,c:The signal is about to change to a green arrow.
note: A solid yellow X over a lane means the lane is about to close to traffic in your direction. You should prepare to leave that lane and move to an adjacent open lane as soon as it is safe, because the signal will soon change to a red X.

question: Wearing both a lap belt and shoulder strap during a collision increases your chances of survival by three to four times. True or false?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Wearing both the lap belt and shoulder strap keeps your body properly restrained so you are less likely to be thrown forward or ejected in a crash. This greatly increases your chances of surviving a collision compared with wearing no belt or only part of the belt system.

question: If you encounter a flooded roadway ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed if the water looks shallow enough.,b:Drive in the center of the roadway only.,c:Turn around and find another route; do not drive through the flood.,d:Slam on the brakes and stop immediately in the water.
note: You should never drive through a flooded roadway because you cannot accurately judge the depth, current, or hidden hazards like washed‑out pavement. Turn around and find another route, even if the water appears shallow.

question: Road surfaces tend to freeze more quickly when they are:
options: a:Curvy sections exposed to wind.,b:Recently repaved sections only.,c:In shaded areas (for example, under trees or bridges).,d:Flat open areas in full sun.
note: Shaded areas of the road freeze sooner and stay icy longer because they receive less sunlight to melt ice and snow. Be especially cautious on bridges, overpasses, and shaded curves, where black ice can form even when other parts of the road look clear.

question: While driving in the rain, what headlight setting should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: In rain, use low beam headlights. Low beams help you see the road and make your vehicle more visible to others without causing glare or reflecting too much light back at you from the raindrops, which can happen with high beams.

question: When should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,b:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,c:When parked on a level roadside with no curb.
note: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light, you should keep your wheels pointed straight ahead until you actually begin the turn. If your wheels are turned and you are hit from behind, your vehicle can be pushed into oncoming traffic. When parked on a hill or sloping driveway, you should turn your wheels so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

question: A distraction while driving is:
options: a:Something that makes you pay more attention to driving.,b:Only things inside the car.,c:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
note: Anything that takes your eyes, mind, or hands away from the driving task is a distraction. This includes things both inside and outside the vehicle, such as texting, adjusting controls, eating, or looking at roadside activity.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you start driving.,b:Whenever you notice a vehicle behind you.,c:After you begin moving the car.,d:Only during long trips.
note: Adjust your seat and then your mirrors before you start driving so you have a clear view around your vehicle without needing to lean. Making these adjustments while moving takes attention away from the road and is unsafe.

question: Do yellow pavement markings indicate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions or mark the left edge of divided highways and one-way roads. White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and mark the right edge of the roadway.

question: When backing up, you should:
options: a:Close your eyes and estimate distance.,b:Press the accelerator to move quickly.,c:Rely solely on your rearview mirror.,d:Look through the rear window over your right shoulder and back up slowly.
note: When backing up, turn your head and look through the rear window over your right shoulder so you can see directly behind you, and move slowly. Mirrors and cameras can help but should not be relied on alone, and you should never back quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.,b:Where there is a red traffic light.,c:Both of the above.
note: You must always stop when directed by a police officer and at steady or flashing red traffic lights. Traffic officers’ directions override signals and signs, and red lights always require a complete stop before proceeding when allowed.

question: Motorcycles are entitled to:
options: a:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,b:Only half the lane width.,c:Use of the bicycle lane at all times.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full use of a lane, just like any other motor vehicle. Other drivers should not crowd them or share the lane side‑by‑side, because motorcycles need space to maneuver and maintain stability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two lanes move in your direction and you're in the left lane with faster drivers behind, you should:
options: a:Drive onto the left shoulder to let others pass.,b:Speed up to prevent others from passing on the right.,c:Stay in the left lane regardless of traffic behind you.,d:Move into the right lane when it is safe so traffic can pass.
note: On multi‑lane roads, you should generally travel in the right lane if you are moving slower than other traffic. If faster vehicles are behind you in the left lane, move safely to the right lane when possible so traffic can flow smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: There are situations when driving 10 mph might still be too fast. True or false?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You must always adjust your speed to conditions. In heavy traffic, bad weather, poor visibility, or near hazards, even 10 mph can be too fast. The safe speed is the one that allows you to stop and avoid hazards in the distance you can see.

question: If you are already within an intersection when a green light changes to yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Stop.,b:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,c:Increase your speed to clear the intersection.
note: If the light turns yellow after you have entered the intersection, continue through and clear it safely. Stopping suddenly in the intersection can cause rear‑end collisions and block cross traffic.

question: Which action helps prevent crashes by improving communication with other road users?
options: a:Drive only on side streets and back roads.,b:Ignore other drivers on the road.,c:Use signals
note: Using your turn signals is a key way to communicate your intentions to other road users so they can anticipate your actions and adjust safely. Signals, along with brake lights, horn, and lane position, help reduce surprises and prevent crashes.

question: A large truck turning right onto a multi-lane street may:
options: a:Need to swing wide to complete the right turn.,b:Always stay strictly in the right lane while turning.,c:Complete the turn in either of the two right lanes without swinging wide.
note: Large trucks have a much wider turning radius and their rear wheels track inside the path of the front wheels. When turning right, they often must swing wide to avoid hitting the curb, parked cars, or pedestrians, so you should never try to squeeze between a turning truck and the curb.

question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Speeding is not dangerous if you are skilled.,b:Speeding can kill.,c:Driving too slowly is always safe.
note: Speeding increases both the chance of a crash and how severe injuries will be if a crash occurs. The faster you go, the longer it takes to stop and the harder you hit, which is why speeding is a major factor in fatal collisions.

question: What does a steady yellow arrow mean to drivers?
options: a:Merge into a lane in the arrow's direction immediately.,b:Slow to a stop if it is safe to do so because a red arrow is imminent.,c:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A steady yellow arrow means the protected turn phase is ending and a red arrow is about to appear. You should slow and stop if you can do so safely; if you are too close to stop safely, you may carefully complete the turn before the light turns red.

question: Driving more slowly than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:Recommended anytime weather is bad.,b:Appropriate if you are unsure of the posted limit.,c:Often a hazard because other drivers may attempt risky passes.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can cause other drivers to brake suddenly or make risky passing maneuvers, increasing the chance of a crash. You should generally travel at the speed of traffic, up to but not over the posted speed limit, and adjust for conditions.

question: Who must wear a seat belt in a motor vehicle?
options: a:Only adult passengers.,b:Only the driver.,c:Passengers under 18 years of age and the driver.
note: In most U.S. states, the driver and all passengers are required to wear seat belts, with especially strict rules for children and teens. The safest and generally lawful rule to follow is that every person in the vehicle should be properly restrained, regardless of age or seating position. This greatly reduces the risk of serious injury or death in a crash.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the red, what should you do?
options: a:Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.,b:Honk your horn.,c:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
note: Even if you have a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the crosswalk or intersection, even when they are crossing against the signal. Slow down and stop if necessary so they can cross safely. Never try to force them out of the way by honking or driving toward them.

question: Does using a cell phone to talk or text while driving significantly increase your crash risk?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Talking or texting on a cell phone while driving is a major distraction. It takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, and your attention away from driving. This greatly increases your risk of being involved in a crash, which is why many states restrict or ban phone use while driving.

question: If a pedestrian is crossing your lane where there is no marked crosswalk, how should you respond?
options: a:Stop and allow the pedestrian to finish crossing.,b:Make eye contact then pass the pedestrian.,c:Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks and should stop to allow them to cross safely.

question: Which statement about large trucks is correct?
options: a:They require a longer distance to stop than passenger vehicles.,b:They are more maneuverable than cars.,c:All large trucks stop quickly because of air brakes.,d:They always stop within the same distance as cars at the same speed.
note: Large trucks are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need a longer distance to stop, even with air brakes. Air brakes do not make trucks stop instantly; in fact, the weight and size of the truck mean you should never cut in front of them or assume they can stop as quickly as a car.

question: Alcohol consumption impairs which of the following driver abilities?
options: a:Perception.,b:Emotional control.,c:All of the above.
note: Alcohol affects multiple critical driving abilities, including perception, emotional control, and judgment. Impaired perception makes it harder to see hazards and judge distances or speeds. Reduced emotional control can lead to risk‑taking, aggression, or overconfidence. Poor judgment affects decisions such as when to turn, pass, or stop. Because alcohol impairs all of these, any amount can make driving unsafe.

question: What best ensures safety when you are backing your vehicle?
options: a:Walk behind the vehicle to check for obstacles before getting in and backing up.,b:Check only your rearview mirrors after getting in.,c:Honk your horn immediately before shifting into reverse.
note: The safest way to back up is to know exactly what is behind your vehicle before you move. Walking behind the vehicle lets you check for children, pedestrians, pets, and low objects that mirrors or cameras may miss. After checking, back up slowly while looking over your shoulder and using mirrors and cameras as aids.

question: What should drivers know about large trucks?
options: a:They require less room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.,b:They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:They have large blind spots and require more room to maneuver and stop.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots on all sides, especially directly behind and along the sides near the cab. They also need more space to turn and a longer distance to stop because of their size and weight. Give trucks extra room, avoid lingering in their blind spots, and never cut closely in front of them.

question: If someone behind you is driving aggressively, you should:
options: a:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,b:Stare at the driver as they pass.,c:Get out of their way and avoid eye contact.
note: When someone behind you is driving aggressively, your goal is to avoid a confrontation and reduce risk. Safely move to another lane or gradually slow so they can pass, and avoid eye contact or gestures that could escalate the situation. Do not speed up or block them, as this increases danger for everyone.

question: If confronted by an aggressive driver, you should:
options: a:Retaliate by tailgating.,b:Cut them off to slow them down.,c:Avoid eye contact, stay calm, and create distance when safe.
note: If you encounter an aggressive driver, stay calm and do not engage. Avoid eye contact, gestures, or any response that could be seen as a challenge. Increase your following distance, let them pass when safe, and focus on creating space around your vehicle. If you feel threatened, drive to a safe, public place and consider contacting law enforcement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in a business or residential area?
options: a:25 mph.,b:15 mph.,c:35 mph.,d:30 mph.
note: In many states, including Maine, the default speed limit in business or residential districts is 25 mph unless signs show a different limit. Always check for posted signs, but if none are present in these areas, 25 mph is the standard.

question: When is the proper time to adjust your mirrors?
options: a:While backing out of your driveway.,b:Before starting the engine.,c:After you begin driving.,d:Only when approaching highway speeds.
note: Mirrors should be adjusted before you start the engine and move the vehicle so you have a clear view behind and to the sides without needing to lean. Adjusting them while driving takes attention away from the road and is unsafe.

question: A single dashed yellow line between opposing lanes means:
options: a:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,b:Drivers may pass if it is safe.,c:Drivers may not pass at any time.
note: A single dashed (broken) yellow line between opposing lanes marks a two-way road where passing is allowed in either direction when it is safe and legal. You must still check for oncoming traffic, adequate space, and no passing-zone signs.

question: Which light indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution at an intersection?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A flashing red light.,c:A steady yellow light.,d:A steady green arrow.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, yielding as necessary. It does not require a full stop unless needed for safety or other traffic.

question: Which of these can impair a person's driving ability?
options: a:Only alcohol and not prescription medication.,b:Alcohol,c:None of the above.,d:Only illegal drugs.
note: Driving can be impaired by alcohol, prescription and over-the-counter medications, illegal drugs, and even fatigue. Any substance that affects your judgment, reaction time, or coordination can make driving unsafe, so you must be cautious with all drugs, not just alcohol or illegal substances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking next to a curb, you should signal:
options: a:When pulling next to or away from the curb.,b:Only when pulling away from the curb.,c:Only when pulling next to the curb.
note: You must signal any time you change your vehicle’s position on the road. That includes both pulling toward the curb to park and pulling away from the curb to re-enter traffic so others can anticipate your movement.

question: If you're angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Drive quickly on the highway to let off steam.,b:Loudly play music so you won't think about it while driving.,c:Begin driving immediately to get home sooner.,d:Take a few minutes to calm down before operating your vehicle.
note: Strong emotions like anger reduce your attention and judgment. Before driving, take time to calm down so you can focus fully on the road and make safe decisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow light you must:
options: a:Proceed without slowing down.,b:Slow down and cross carefully.,c:Stop and wait for a green light.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. Slow down, scan for traffic and pedestrians, and continue through the intersection only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,b:Drivers must make hand motions to communicate.,c:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
note: At a four-way stop where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The vehicle on the right goes first when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, what actions should you take to ensure it is safe?
options: a:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.,b:Check the inside rearview mirror only.,c:Slow down before changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then look over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to clear your blind spot. Only move over when the lane is open and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp should:
options: a:Yield to vehicles already on the interstate and merge when safe.,b:Force their way because they are entering traffic.,c:Always stop at the end of the ramp before merging.,d:Expect drivers to change lanes for them.
note: On entrance or acceleration ramps, you must adjust your speed to match interstate traffic and yield to vehicles already on the highway. Do not force your way in or expect others to move; merge only when there is a safe gap.

question: How should you prepare for anything coming up on the road ahead?
options: a:Drive with your foot resting on the brake at all times.,b:Continually scan the entire road and roadsides.,c:Only look as you approach intersections.,d:Stare straight ahead at a single point.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan ahead and to the sides to spot hazards early. By continually checking the whole roadway and roadsides, you have more time to react to changing conditions and avoid sudden emergencies.

question: If your vehicle's suspension is worn out, what problem can result?
options: a:Vehicle control problems.,b:Squealing brakes.,c:Slack in the steering.,d:Uneven tire wear.
note: A worn suspension system reduces your vehicle’s stability, especially when turning, braking, or driving over bumps. This can cause poor traction, excessive body roll, and loss of control, increasing the risk of skids and crashes.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, you should:
options: a:Use only the lap belt.,b:Use only the shoulder belt.,c:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
note: Two-part belt systems are designed to work as a unit. The lap belt keeps your lower body secure, and the shoulder belt keeps your upper body from striking the steering wheel, dashboard, or windshield. Using both together gives the best protection.

question: If you experience a sudden tire blowout, you should:
options: a:Tap or pump the brakes repeatedly.,b:Slow down gradually and apply the brakes lightly.,c:Apply the brakes firmly and immediately.
note: In a tire blowout, hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Once you have control and your speed has dropped, apply the brakes lightly and move to a safe place off the road.

question: When planning to pass another vehicle, what assumption should you avoid?
options: a:Assuming the other driver will maintain a constant speed.,b:Assuming the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.,c:Assuming they will let you pass if you signal.
note: When passing, you must plan the entire maneuver so you can move out, pass, and return to your lane using only the space you can clearly see is available. Never assume other drivers will slow down or create a gap for you; instead, wait until you already have enough clear distance and space to complete the pass safely on your own.

question: Does a driver need to allow as much following distance when behind a motorcycle as behind a car?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You should allow at least the same following distance behind a motorcycle as you would behind a car, and often more. Motorcycles can stop and maneuver very quickly, so a 3–4 second following distance gives you enough time to react if the rider brakes or swerves suddenly.

question: If you encounter a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Honk to alert the pedestrian of your presence.,b:You must yield the right-of-way to the pedestrian.,c:The pedestrian must yield to vehicles.
note: A pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog is blind or visually impaired and always has the right-of-way. You must slow down or stop as needed and yield, giving them plenty of time and space to cross safely. Never honk or try to force them to hurry or yield to you.

question: When meeting an oncoming vehicle using high beams that blind you, what should you do?
options: a:Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.,b:Use your bright lights until the other vehicle dims theirs.,c:Look away from the headlights and toward the right side of the road until the vehicle passes.
note: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams and they are blinding you, do not stare into the lights or speed up. Instead, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the road edge or lane line as a guide while you slow slightly if needed. This helps you stay in your lane and maintain control until the vehicle passes.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: a:You must not pass other vehicles.,b:Reduce your speed immediately.,c:A traffic light is ahead.,d:You may pass if no oncoming traffic is visible.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline marks a no-passing zone for traffic in your direction. You may not cross this line to pass another vehicle, even if the road ahead looks clear. You may cross it only when turning left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe.

question: What must you do when you hear a siren from an emergency vehicle approaching from behind?
options: a:Stop immediately where you are and turn off the engine.,b:Speed up to get out of its way.,c:Pull over to the right and stop to allow it to pass.
note: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle approaching from behind, you must, if safe, move to the right side of the road and stop until it has passed. In heavy traffic, keep moving slowly until you can safely pull over; do not stop in the middle of a lane and block traffic.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:
options: a:Flash your headlights and retaliate.,b:Attempt to speed up and race them.,c:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
note: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm, create space, and let them go ahead. Do not make eye contact, gesture, or try to race or block them. Avoiding confrontation greatly reduces the risk of a crash or road‑rage incident.

question: To reduce the chance of losing traction on wet roads you should:
options: a:Make abrupt turns to clear water quickly.,b:Slow down.,c:Apply the brakes firmly to test grip.
note: On wet roads, slowing down is the best way to reduce the risk of hydroplaning and losing traction. Gentle steering, smooth braking, and maintaining good following distance help your tires maintain grip on the wet surface.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, at what speed should you be traveling?
options: a:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,b:Five to ten mph slower than freeway traffic.,c:The posted speed limit only, regardless of traffic speed.
note: When merging onto a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of traffic, as long as it is safe and not above the speed limit. Matching traffic speed allows you to merge smoothly without forcing other drivers to brake suddenly.

question: Which behavior best describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Watching the vehicle directly in front only.,b:Frequently checking mirrors and surroundings.,c:Keeping eyes on the road while adjusting radio.,d:Staring off the roadway or daydreaming while driving.
note: An inattentive driver is mentally or visually distracted from the driving task, such as staring off the roadway or daydreaming. Safe drivers keep their attention on the road, scan ahead, check mirrors regularly, and avoid distractions like phones, passengers, or adjusting controls for long periods.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How are fines for moving violations in school zones typically different?
options: a:Fines are reduced in school zones.,b:Fines are unchanged in school zones.,c:Fines are doubled in school zones.,d:Fines are waived during school hours.
note: In many states, including Maine, fines for moving violations are increased in school zones, often doubled. This is to encourage drivers to slow down and use extra caution where children are present.

question: Why should you avoid making a sudden stop in front of a large truck or bus?
options: a:Because large trucks and buses travel at higher speeds.,b:Because small vehicle drivers cannot see trucks in their rearview mirrors.,c:Because large trucks and buses require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks and buses are heavier and need a much longer distance to stop than smaller vehicles. If you brake suddenly in front of them, they may not be able to stop in time, increasing the risk of a rear-end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver whose left arm and hand are extended downward is signaling what?
options: a:Turn left.,b:Turn right.,c:Stop or slow down.
note: Hand signals use the left arm: straight out means a left turn, arm bent up means a right turn, and arm extended downward means you are slowing or stopping.

question: When approached by an emergency vehicle using its siren and/or flashing lights, what must a driver do?
options: a:Pull to the right and stop.,b:Pull to the right and slow down.,c:Pull to the right and turn on their vehicle's four-way flashers.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights and/or siren, you must move to the right side of the road and stop until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by law enforcement.

question: What headlight setting should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.
