note: In fog, use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and can shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the correct immediate response?
options: a:Ease up on the gas pedal.,b:Brake as hard as possible.,c:Turn off the ignition.
note: When a vehicle begins to skid, you should smoothly ease off the accelerator (and off the brake if you were braking) so the tires can regain traction. As traction returns, steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. Sudden braking or jerking the wheel can make the skid worse.

question: What should you do first before stopping your vehicle at a signal or sign?
options: a:Set the parking brake.,b:Press down hard on the accelerator.,c:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.
note: Before slowing or stopping, check your mirrors so you know where traffic is around you, especially behind you. This helps you brake smoothly, avoid being rear‑ended, and adjust your braking if a vehicle behind is too close.

question: Why should motorists give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:They are larger and easier to see than adults.,b:Children are less predictable and can be harder to see.,c:Children can stop more quickly than adults.,d:Children always follow the rules perfectly.
note: Motorists should give extra space to children on bicycles because children are less predictable, have less experience judging traffic, and can be harder to see. They may suddenly swerve, stop, or enter the roadway without warning, so drivers must slow down and allow a wide safety margin.

question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally do what?
options: a:Require a smaller turning radius than passenger vehicles do.,b:Require less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles.,c:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
note: Large trucks are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need a longer distance to stop, especially at higher speeds or on downgrades. When driving near trucks, avoid cutting in front of them and allow extra space so the driver has enough room to stop safely.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what steps should you take?
options: a:Slam on your brakes immediately.,b:Keep driving at the same speed and try to get to a service area.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly to keep the vehicle straight, ease your foot off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Do not slam on the brakes. When you have control and your speed has dropped, carefully steer to the side of the road and stop in a safe place.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are in the left lane and want to move into the right lane. What should you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Check mirrors,b:Look in mirrors,c:Check rear view
note: Before changing lanes, you must check your mirrors, signal, and then quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot on the side you are moving toward. Relying only on the rearview mirror is unsafe because it does not show vehicles in your blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver begins to pass you, how can you help them re-enter your lane?
options: a:Signal the other driver aggressively to speed up.,b:Pull off the road immediately.,c:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.
note: When another driver is passing you, stay in your lane and maintain a steady speed, or slightly adjust your speed if needed, so they have enough space and time to pass and return safely. Do not speed up or make sudden moves that could trap them beside oncoming traffic.

question: Is it lawful to share a lane side-by-side with a motorcycle?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other vehicle. You must not crowd or share the same lane side‑by‑side with a motorcycle because they need space to maneuver and maintain balance safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, you should look for a gap of how many seconds?
options: a:Three seconds,b:Four seconds,c:One to two seconds
note: When entering a freeway, use the on‑ramp to match the speed of traffic and look for a gap of about four seconds. A four‑second gap gives you enough space to merge smoothly and maintain a safe following distance from the vehicle ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should not pass:
options: a:Only when a police officer is present.,b:Whenever a car in front is driving under the speed limit.,c:On a hill or curve,d:Only during daylight hours.
note: You must never pass on a hill or curve where you cannot see far enough ahead to be sure the lane is clear. Limited visibility makes it impossible to judge whether oncoming traffic is approaching, which can lead to head‑on collisions.

question: What is the correct general action when roads are slippery?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Drive the posted speed with caution.,c:Drive more quickly.
note: On slippery roads you must reduce speed, often to well below the posted limit. Rain, snow, or ice greatly reduce traction, so slowing down gives you more time to react and helps prevent skids.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You always have the right-of-way at railroad crossings.,b:You must stop when directed by a flagger or stop sign.,c:Use cruise control to maintain speed over tracks.
note: At railroad crossings, you must obey all traffic control devices and any flagger directing traffic. If a stop sign, signal, or flagger tells you to stop, you must stop and proceed only when it is clearly safe.

question: If your vehicle begins to lose traction because of water (hydroplaning), you should:
options: a:Accelerate to regain traction.,b:Slow down gradually and avoid braking.,c:Apply firm braking immediately.
note: When your vehicle hydroplanes, the tires lose contact with the road and you cannot steer or brake effectively. Ease off the accelerator and slow down gradually without braking hard or making sudden moves. This allows the tires to regain traction safely.

question: When you drive through an area where children are playing, you should expect them to:
options: a:Stop at the curb before crossing.,b:Always know when it is safe to cross.,c:Possibly run into the street without looking.
note: Children often do not judge traffic well and may suddenly run into the street without looking. In areas where children are present, slow down, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop at any moment.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Have done as much as you can and leave.,b:Must stay until the police arrive regardless of circumstances.,c:Leave a written notice with your name and contact information, and report the collision if required by law.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner, you must leave a written note with your name, contact information, and a brief description of the collision in a secure, visible place on the vehicle. You must also report the collision to law enforcement if required by state law.

question: What must you do when approaching an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution without stopping.,b:Come to a complete stop,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the light turns green.
note: A flashing red light is treated exactly like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. After stopping, yield to any pedestrians and other vehicles that have the right‑of‑way, then proceed only when it is safe.

question: Alcohol consumption causes which of the following?
options: a:Loss of concentration.,b:All of the above.,c:Slower judgment.,d:Poor coordination.
note: Alcohol affects many parts of your driving ability at the same time. It reduces concentration, slows and distorts judgment, and harms coordination and balance. Because it causes all of these effects together, any amount of drinking can make you an unsafe driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead,b:Right, toward the side of the road,c:Left, toward the center of the road
note: When parking downhill on a two‑way road with no curb, turn your front wheels to the right, toward the edge of the road or shoulder. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the roadway instead of into oncoming traffic.

question: Which action can help reduce incidents of road rage?
options: a:Always signal your intention when changing lanes.,b:Use your horn frequently to warn others.,c:Text or talk on your phone to stay calm.
note: To help prevent road rage, drive predictably and courteously. Always signal before changing lanes or turning so others know what you plan to do, obey speed limits, avoid tailgating, and do not respond to aggressive drivers. Using your horn aggressively or being distracted by a phone can increase tension and risk.

question: What does a flashing red traffic signal mean?
options: a:You do not have to stop if the way is clear.,b:The traffic signal is broken and can be ignored.,c:The same as a stop sign; come to a full stop before proceeding.
note: A flashing red traffic signal means you must stop completely, just as you would at a stop sign. Stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then look in all directions and proceed only when the way is clear and it is your turn to go.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is correct?
options: a:You should always make sure all passengers are using a seat belt or appropriate child restraint.,b:You should never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.,c:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child even in a low-speed collision.
note: All three statements are correct safety practices. Drivers should always ensure every passenger is properly buckled, infants and small children should not be placed in the front seat with an active airbag, and airbags can seriously injure infants or small children even in low‑speed crashes. However, the safest and most emphasized rule is to keep infants and small children out of the front seat when there is an active airbag, because a deploying airbag can be fatal to a child in a rear‑facing seat.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When the car in front of you is disabled.,b:When doing so would interfere with traffic.,c:When turning left into a driveway.
note: You may cross a single broken line to change lanes or pass only when it is safe and legal. If crossing the line would interfere with other traffic—such as forcing another driver to brake or swerve—you must not cross. Always wait until you have enough clear space and time to complete your maneuver without affecting other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss the exit you wanted to take off a freeway, you should:
options: a:Cross the median and turn around.,b:Pull onto the shoulder and back to the exit.,c:Go on to the next exit.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, stay calm and continue to the next exit. It is illegal and extremely dangerous to stop on the freeway, back up on the shoulder, or cross the median to reach a missed exit. Use the next exit to safely leave the freeway and then return to your intended route.

question: When you approach a heavy truck from behind on an uphill, you should be aware that:
options: a:You can always safely pass the truck on the hill.,b:It is legal to pass on a hill with limited visibility.,c:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.
note: Heavy trucks often slow down on uphill grades because of their weight and engine limits, so they may travel well below the posted speed limit. You must be prepared for this speed difference and only pass when it is legal and you have clear visibility and enough space; passing on a hill with limited sight distance is unsafe and often illegal.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing you should:
options: a:Slow down, look for a train, and be prepared to stop.,b:Always speed up to clear the tracks quickly.,c:Ignore gates and proceed if no train is visible.
note: Approach every railroad crossing with caution: slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. If lights are flashing, a train is visible, or gates are down, you must stop at a safe distance—typically 15 to 50 feet from the nearest rail—and remain stopped until it is clearly safe to proceed. Never speed up to beat a train or go around lowered gates.

question: A flashing yellow traffic signal tells you to:
options: a:Drive with caution.,b:Yield to oncoming traffic only.,c:Stop before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you must slow down and proceed with extra caution, watching carefully for other vehicles and pedestrians. It does not require a full stop unless needed for safety or to yield to others who have the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Yellow centerlines on the road separate what type of traffic?
options: a:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,b:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,c:All carpool lanes from regular lanes.
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads. They mark the center of the roadway and help drivers stay on the correct side of the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is a likely result of driving much slower than the speed limit?
options: a:Always has the right-of-way.,b:Is a very safe driver.,c:May create a hazard and you may need to let others pass.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because it can cause sudden braking, lane changes, and backups. If your slow speed is holding up traffic, you may need to move to the right or pull off when safe and let others pass.

question: Which driving habit helps conserve gasoline?
options: a:Constantly switching between gears.,b:Accelerating quickly at each green light.,c:Idling in your driveway with the engine running.,d:Slowing down gradually and avoiding unnecessary stops.
note: To conserve fuel, avoid rapid starts and hard braking. Looking ahead and slowing down gradually so you avoid unnecessary stops helps your vehicle use less gasoline.

question: If there are two adjacent railroad tracks, what must you do after one train passes?
options: a:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,b:Look for another train on the other track before proceeding.,c:It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
note: When there are multiple railroad tracks, another train may be coming on a different track, sometimes hidden by the first train. After one train passes, you must look and listen carefully and be sure all tracks are clear before crossing.

question: On which side(s) of your vehicle should you maintain a space cushion?
options: a:All around your vehicle—front, back, left, and right,b:Only to the front of the vehicle,c:Only to the back of the vehicle
note: You should maintain a space cushion on all sides of your vehicle—front, back, left, and right. Extra space gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake, if you need to stop suddenly, or if road conditions change.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you should:
options: a:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead and slow down.,b:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.,c:Speed up because a lane ends ahead.
note: Orange construction signs and cones warn of a work zone ahead. You must be prepared for workers, equipment, lane shifts, or lane closures. Reduce your speed, increase following distance, and follow any posted instructions or flagger directions.

question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, you should NOT:
options: a:Brace yourself against the seatback.,b:Press your head against the head restraint.,c:Release your seat belt.
note: If you are about to be hit from the rear, keep your seat belt fastened. Press your head firmly against the head restraint and brace yourself against the seatback to reduce the risk of whiplash. Never release your seat belt in a collision situation.

question: On long trips, preventing drowsiness is achieved by:
options: a:Stopping at regular intervals for rest and stretching.,b:Turning the radio on loudly.,c:Slowing down to conserve energy.
note: On long trips, stop at regular intervals to rest, walk, and stretch. Short breaks help you stay alert and prevent drowsiness. Loud music or simply slowing down does not effectively prevent fatigue and can give a false sense of alertness.

question: To reduce the chance of skidding on slippery surfaces, what should you do before entering a curve or intersection?
options: a:Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.,b:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,c:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
note: To reduce the chance of skidding on slippery surfaces, slow down before you enter a curve or intersection. Braking or making sudden speed changes while turning can cause your tires to lose traction and lead to a skid.

question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing red light, you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed if clear.,b:Come to a complete stop, check traffic, and go when safe.,c:Drive through without stopping if no other vehicles are present.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield to anyone with the right-of-way, and then proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a transit vehicle signals to re-enter the roadway after stopping, what must you do?
options: a:Honk to let them know you’re there.,b:Move to the left lane.,c:Yield to allow safe re-entry.
note: When a transit or city bus signals that it is pulling away from a stop, you must yield and allow it to re-enter traffic when it is safe. This may mean slowing, changing lanes, or briefly stopping so the bus can merge safely. You should not honk at the bus; your responsibility is to help avoid conflicts and give it space to rejoin the flow of traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?
options: a:Turn without checking for pedestrians if the light is green.,b:Stop before turning even if no one is present.,c:Yield to pedestrians and any other traffic with the right-of-way.,d:Maintain your normal speed and complete the turn.
note: A green light allows you to turn, but it does not give you the right to ignore others. Before turning right, you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in or entering the intersection with the right-of-way. Make the turn only when the path is clear and safe.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:
options: a:Grip the wheel, ease off the accelerator, and slow gradually without braking hard.,b:Press the brake pedal as hard as possible immediately.,c:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.
note: If a tire blows out or goes flat, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and stay off the brakes at first. Ease off the accelerator and let the vehicle slow down gradually so you don’t lose control. Once you have slowed and the vehicle is stable, steer to a safe place off the road and brake gently to stop.

question: When should you allow extra following distance behind another vehicle?
options: a:Only when following a small passenger car.,b:Never; following distance is constant.,c:When behind a compact sedan.,d:When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle (like a truck with blind spots)
note: You should leave extra following distance behind large vehicles, such as trucks and buses, because their drivers may not see you directly behind them and they can block your view of the road ahead. More space gives you extra time to react if they slow, stop, or need to make wide turns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit indicates:
options: a:Only a suggested safe speed.,b:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions.,c:The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed you may drive in ideal conditions. You must slow down below that limit when conditions are poor (rain, fog, heavy traffic, sharp curves) so that your speed is safe for the situation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a crowded freeway, what steps should you take to merge safely?
options: a:Always stop before entering the highway.,b:Use your mirrors and check blind spots; use the acceleration lane to match traffic speed; yield to traffic already on the freeway.,c:Merge across two lanes at once.
note: When entering a freeway, use the entrance/acceleration lane to reach about the same speed as traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and merge when there is a safe gap. You must yield to vehicles already on the freeway and never stop in the acceleration lane unless absolutely necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing red signal, you must:
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the light turns green.,b:Proceed as if the signal were a flashing yellow.,c:Slow down and pass through if clear.,d:Come to a complete stop, then proceed when it is safe after yielding as needed.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, then yield to any pedestrians or vehicles in or approaching the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe. You do not have to wait for the light to change; you may go after stopping and yielding.

question: If you approach an accident scene, when should you stop?
options: a:Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived.,b:Always stop to look, even if you are not involved.,c:Keep moving and ignore the scene completely.,d:Park nearby and take photos.
note: You must stop if you are involved in a crash or if emergency help has not yet arrived and you can safely offer assistance or call 911. If emergency vehicles and responders are already on scene and you are not involved, keep moving, slow as needed, and focus on driving so you do not create additional hazards or slow traffic unnecessarily.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Yellow and white
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and also mark the right edge of the roadway.

question: Highway signs that warn of potentially hazardous conditions are called:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Warning signs are usually yellow and black and are used to alert drivers to upcoming hazards, changes in road conditions, or special situations ahead so you can adjust your driving in time.

question: Drivers should be most alert for deer and moose at what times?
options: a:Only during the night.,b:At dusk and dawn.,c:Only at midday.
note: Deer and many other large animals are most active and likely to cross roads around dawn and dusk, so drivers should be especially alert and reduce speed in areas where wildlife may be present at those times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle uses sirens and lights, it:
options: a:Has no different rights than other traffic.,b:Has the right-of-way and you must yield to it.,c:Should be followed closely by other vehicles.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using sirens and flashing lights, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling to the right and stopping when safe, and follow any directions given by emergency personnel.

question: Under low visibility due to fog, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your high beam headlights to see farther.,b:Increase your speed to get out of the fog quickly.,c:Slow down and use low beam headlights.
note: Fog reflects high beams and makes it harder to see, so you should slow down, use low beam headlights, and if visibility becomes extremely poor, pull completely off the road to a safe place until conditions improve.

question: When driving in dense fog, which of these is correct?
options: a:Keep your normal speed to avoid causing delays.,b:Use high beam headlights to see farther.,c:Use low beam headlights and drive cautiously at reduced speeds.
note: In dense fog, always use low beam headlights because high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility; drive at a reduced speed and be prepared to stop, pulling off the roadway to a safe location if you cannot see well enough to continue.

question: Regarding curves, the most important rule is to:
options: a:Accelerate through the curve for better traction.,b:Slow down before entering the curve.,c:Maintain posted speed until the sharpest part
note: You should always slow down before entering a curve so you can steer smoothly and avoid being pushed outward by inertia. Entering too fast makes it harder to stay in your lane and to react to hazards you may not see until you are in the curve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a curve you should:
options: a:Brake hard while in the curve.,b:Activate your turn signal.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: Reduce your speed before you enter a curve so the vehicle is stable and under control as you turn. Braking hard while already in the curve can cause skidding, especially on wet or loose surfaces, and signaling is not required for a simple curve in the road.

question: How often must motor vehicles bearing a Maine registration be inspected?
options: a:Once every two years.,b:Once every four years.,c:Once a year.
note: In Maine, most registered motor vehicles must pass a safety inspection once every year at an official inspection station before being driven on public roads. This helps ensure that brakes, lights, tires, and other key systems are in safe working order.

question: When driving in bad weather, what should drivers do?
options: a:Decrease their following distance.,b:Increase their following distance.,c:Increase their speed to reach their destination faster.
note: In bad weather, such as rain, snow, or fog, you should increase your following distance so you have more time and space to react. Slippery or low‑visibility conditions lengthen stopping distances and make sudden maneuvers more dangerous.

question: Distracted driving is:
options: a:Extremely risky behavior that greatly increases crash risk.,b:Very uncommon and not a major concern.,c:Always acceptable if you are an experienced driver.,d:Only an issue for new drivers.
note: Distracted driving is extremely dangerous because it takes your eyes, mind, or hands away from the driving task, greatly increasing the chance of a crash. It is unsafe for all drivers, regardless of age or experience.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must yield to emergency vehicles when:
options: a:Only when other vehicles yield.,b:You see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You must always yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using a siren and/or flashing red or blue lights. Move to the right side of the road and stop, if possible, so they can pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you are waiting in the intersection to complete a left turn, how should your wheels be positioned?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.,b:Signal and keep your wheels straight.,c:Flash your headlights so drivers will let you through.
note: When waiting in an intersection to turn left, keep your wheels straight and your turn signal on. If you are hit from behind, straight wheels help prevent your vehicle from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: When can you legally go around or under a railroad crossing gate that is lowered?
options: a:When you can clearly see in both directions.,b:When the warning lights are not flashing.,c:Never.
note: You must never drive around or under a lowered railroad gate. Stay stopped until the gates are fully raised and the warning lights and bells have stopped.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A two-lane road divided by a broken yellow line indicates:
options: a:It is a one-way road.,b:The road is under repair and temporary markings apply.,c:It is a two-way road where passing is allowed when safe.
note: A broken yellow centerline means two-way traffic and passing is allowed in both directions when it is safe and legal. Always check for oncoming traffic and enough clear distance before passing.

question: When you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Firmly apply your brakes.,b:Apply your parking brake.,c:Take your foot off the gas pedal.
note: On a slippery road, first ease off the gas so the car slows down gradually. If you need to slow more, brake gently and steadily to avoid skidding.

question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, what should you always do?
options: a:Slowly pass stopped vehicles without checking.,b:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,c:Only look straight ahead.,d:Ignore pedestrians if you have the right-of-way.
note: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you must scan to the sides as well as ahead because people, bicycles, or vehicles can enter your path from either direction. Looking left and right before proceeding helps you spot hazards early and gives you time to stop or yield.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under which condition may you legally pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:On a narrow bridge if traffic is slow.,b:Whenever there is space on the right shoulder to pass.,c:When the vehicle ahead is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane on the right.
note: You may pass on the right only when it can be done safely and without leaving the paved roadway, such as when the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is a marked lane or sufficient legal lane space on the right. You must never pass on the right by driving on the shoulder, off the pavement, or in a narrow space not intended as a travel lane.

question: If a driver accumulates how many points in one year will their license be suspended?
options: a:12 points,b:18 points,c:20 points
note: In Maine, accumulating 12 or more points within a 12-month period can result in a license suspension.

question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.,b:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted.,c:You become more alert.
note: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your reflexes and reaction time, reduces alertness, and distorts your judgment of speed, distance, and risk. It does not make you more alert; even small amounts of alcohol can impair your ability to drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes you should do which of the following?
options: a:Check side and rearview mirrors, then glance over your shoulder for blind spots.,b:Quickly turn your head without checking mirrors.,c:Only check your side view mirror.,d:Only rely on a backup camera.
note: Before changing lanes, first check your rearview and side mirrors to see traffic around you, then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you’re moving to check your blind spot. Mirrors alone cannot show vehicles in blind spots, so the shoulder check is essential for a safe lane change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your lane after passing another vehicle, you should:
options: a:Flash your headlights.,b:Sound your horn.,c:See the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: Before moving back into your original lane after passing, you should not cut closely in front of the vehicle you passed. A good safety rule is to wait until you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your inside rearview mirror, then check your mirrors and blind spot, signal, and return smoothly.

question: If you are about to be struck from the rear, which action should you NOT take?
options: a:Let go of the steering wheel.,b:Press your head firmly against the head restraint.,c:Be ready to apply the brakes.
note: If you are about to be hit from behind, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel so you can maintain control of the vehicle. Press your head firmly against the head restraint and be ready to apply the brakes so you are less likely to be pushed into another vehicle ahead of you.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings and signs?
options: a:They are usually not important.,b:They are only found in construction zones.,c:They provide information and guidance for drivers.
note: Highway signs and pavement markings are critical safety tools. They guide lane use, indicate passing and no‑passing zones, show where you must stop or yield, warn of hazards, and provide directions and other information so drivers can travel safely and predictably.

question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag.,b:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,c:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.
note: You should never follow a large truck or bus closely to “draft” or reduce wind drag. Large vehicles have big blind spots directly behind them and need more room to stop. Stay out of their blind spots, avoid lingering alongside them, and give them extra space on curves and hills where their view and maneuverability are limited.

question: Are drivers required to yield to children playing in the streets?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Drivers must always exercise extreme caution around children, slowing down and being prepared to stop, especially in residential areas, near playgrounds, and in school zones. However, the law does not give children playing in the street an automatic legal right‑of‑way over vehicles; drivers must avoid collisions but are not formally required to yield to unlawful street play.

question: If someone is tailgating you on a two-lane road and you cannot change lanes, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Speed up to increase distance.,b:Slow down gradually to encourage the tailgater to pass.,c:Apply your brakes and then resume original speed.
note: If a driver is following too closely and you cannot safely change lanes, gradually slow down to increase your following distance and encourage the tailgater to pass when it is safe. Avoid suddenly braking or speeding up, as these actions can increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead.,b:Toward the center of the road (left).,c:Toward the edge of the road (to the right).
note: On an uphill road with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road (to the right). If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll backward and the front wheels will guide it off the roadway instead of into oncoming traffic.

question: If you drink socially, what helps ensure safe driving afterwards?
options: a:Take a cold shower,b:Wait 10 minutes and then drive if you feel fine.,c:Drink coffee before driving to sober up.,d:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
note: The only safe choice after drinking is not to drive. A sober driver, taxi, rideshare, or public transportation should be used. Coffee, cold showers, or waiting a few minutes do not reduce your blood alcohol concentration or restore safe driving ability.

question: When an authorized emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights approaches, you should pull to the right-hand edge and wait for it to pass. True or false?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When an authorized emergency vehicle approaches using sirens and flashing lights, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as close as safely possible to the right-hand edge of the road and stopping until the vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by a police officer.

question: What should you do when it begins to rain while you are driving?
options: a:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.,b:Slow down.,c:Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
note: When it begins to rain, the road becomes especially slippery, and visibility often decreases. You should slow down, increase your following distance, and turn on your headlights so you can see and be seen more easily. Driving at or above the speed limit in rain can greatly increase your risk of skidding or hydroplaning.

question: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is NOT affected by which of the following?
options: a:Your body weight.,b:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.,c:How much time passes between drinks.
note: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is determined mainly by how much alcohol you consume, how quickly you drink it, your body weight, and how fast your body processes alcohol. The specific type of alcoholic beverage does not change BAC by itself; what matters is the total amount of pure alcohol you take in and the time over which you drink it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you plan to turn left at the upcoming corner, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Pedestrians who are in or entering the crosswalk with the right-of-way.,b:Oncoming vehicles that are going straight or close enough to be a hazard.,c:All approaching road users who have the right-of-way and would be affected by your turn.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians who are in or entering the crosswalk with the right-of-way. You do not yield to pedestrians who are merely waiting on the sidewalk for a Walk signal, and you do not yield to oncoming vehicles that are also turning left if you have a protected green arrow. In general, you yield to any approaching vehicles that have the right-of-way and would be affected by your turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging from an entrance ramp onto a highway, you should generally:
options: a:Accelerate to match the speed of traffic and merge when safe.,b:Stop at the ramp end and wait for a large gap.,c:Slow down significantly to avoid merging conflicts.
note: On highway entrance ramps, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of traffic, signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge when there is a safe gap. Stopping at the end of the ramp or slowing far below traffic speed makes merging more dangerous and can cause rear-end collisions.

question: As your speed increases, what must you do to stay safe?
options: a:Look well ahead of your vehicle.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Change lanes frequently.
note: At higher speeds, your stopping distance and the distance you travel while reacting both increase. To stay safe, you must look well ahead of your vehicle so you can spot hazards early, adjust your speed, and change lanes smoothly if needed. Simply turning on headlights or changing lanes often does not address the increased stopping distance.

question: Is it acceptable to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates under any circumstances?
options: a:When directed by another driver.,b:Yes — if the train has passed recently.,c:No — under no circumstances should you drive around a lowered gate.,d:Only when flashing lights have stopped.
note: You must never drive around or under lowered railroad crossing gates. A train may be closer or moving faster than it appears, or another train may be coming on a different track. You must wait until the lights stop flashing, the gates are fully raised, and it is clearly safe before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:The light is about to turn green.,b:Stop only if other cars are present.,c:The same as a stop sign—you must stop and proceed when safe.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, yield the right‑of‑way as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view to the side is blocked at an intersection, how should you proceed?
options: a:Maintain your speed and look both ways.,b:Slow down and look both ways.,c:Stop.
note: If your side view is blocked at an intersection, you should slow down and be prepared to stop, then move forward carefully until you can see clearly in both directions. A complete stop is required only if there is a stop sign, signal, or other legal requirement to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it acceptable to begin a pass in a passing zone if you cannot complete it before the zone ends?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You may not start a pass if you cannot finish it before reaching a no-passing zone; it is unsafe to be mid-pass when the zone ends.

question: When should you stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:Only in cities with frequent trains.,b:Only if you are transporting two or more young children.,c:If there isn’t room on the other side for you to completely clear the tracks.
note: You must never enter railroad tracks unless there is enough space on the far side for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks. Stopping on the tracks or where you could be trapped by traffic or a signal is extremely dangerous and illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.,b:When driving so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic.,c:Only when driving in rural areas.
note: Driving significantly below the posted speed limit can be illegal if you unnecessarily slow or block normal traffic flow. You should adjust your speed to conditions, but not drive so slowly that you create a hazard or impede other drivers without a good reason.

question: Which of the following may be used on some highways to guide drivers into proper turning lanes?
options: a:Arrows and lane-control signals such as flashing yellow arrow indicators.,b:White lines on the side of the road only.,c:Flashing red lights only.
note: Lane-use arrows painted on the pavement and lane-control signals with arrow indications are commonly used on multi-lane roads to show which lanes are for turning and which are for going straight. Drivers should follow these arrows and signals to be in the correct lane before reaching an intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal is green but an officer signals for you to stop, you should:
options: a:Follow the green light instead of the officer.,b:Obey the officer's directions and stop.,c:Slow and then proceed if clear.,d:Follow what the vehicle ahead does.
note: A police officer’s hand signals or verbal directions always override traffic lights and signs. If the light is green but an officer tells you to stop, you must stop and follow the officer’s instructions, even if it conflicts with the signal.

question: Any amount of alcohol in the bloodstream can affect what aspects of a driver?
options: a:Knowledge only.,b:Right-of-way privileges.,c:Judgment and physical coordination.
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect the brain, reducing judgment, slowing reaction time, and harming coordination. These changes make it harder to steer, brake, and respond to traffic situations safely, even when the driver does not feel very impaired.

question: Is alcohol a major factor in fatal motor vehicle crashes?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Alcohol is a major contributing factor in many fatal crashes. It reduces a driver’s ability to see clearly, judge distances and speeds, and react quickly, which greatly increases the risk of severe or deadly collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a steady red light, drivers should:
options: a:Drive through if no cross traffic is visible.,b:Only stop if a police officer is present.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the light turns green, except when making a permitted turn on red after stopping and yielding.
note: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or stop line and remain stopped until the light turns green, unless you are making a permitted turn on red after stopping and yielding. You may turn right on red (and left from a one-way onto a one-way) only where it is allowed and only after stopping and yielding to traffic and pedestrians.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Pump the brakes rapidly.,b:Grip the steering wheel firmly,c:Brake very hard and sharply steer to the right.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, stay off the brakes at first, and gently ease off the accelerator. Steer straight, let the vehicle slow down gradually, then carefully move to the side of the road when you have control and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstances may you legally block an intersection?
options: a:During rush hour traffic.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If you entered the intersection on a green light.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless there is enough space to completely clear it, even if the light is green. Blocking an intersection can impede cross traffic and emergency vehicles and may result in a citation. Always wait until you can fully get through before entering.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
options: a:All of the above.,b:Alertness and concentration.,c:Reaction time and coordination.
note: Alcohol and many drugs affect multiple driving skills at the same time. They reduce alertness and concentration, slow your reaction time, and impair coordination. Because all of these abilities are critical for safe driving, any impairment greatly increases your crash risk.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:Only when involved in a collision.,b:Whenever stopped for a citation or involved in a collision.,c:Only when stopped and cited.
note: Drivers must carry proof of insurance and show it to law enforcement when requested, such as when stopped for a traffic violation or involved in a collision. This demonstrates you have the required financial responsibility to cover potential damages.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Merge to the right lane immediately.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Wait for a police officer to direct traffic.,d:Stop
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield the right-of-way as needed, and proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:You do not need to yield when turning.,b:Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.,c:The turn is protected and you may proceed without caution.,d:Prepare to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic before turning.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected green arrow phase is ending. You should prepare to stop if it is safe to do so and be ready to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning. If you are already in the intersection when it appears, complete the turn carefully while yielding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, you must:
options: a:Expect oncoming traffic to yield to you.,b:Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before completing the turn.,c:Turn immediately when the signal changes regardless of oncoming traffic.,d:Never yield under any circumstances.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right, and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Only begin your turn when there is a safe gap and you will not force others to slow or stop suddenly.

question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers may pass with caution.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass.
note: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line between lanes means lane changes and passing are discouraged or prohibited; you should stay in your lane unless necessary and legal to move. Center lines between opposite directions of travel are yellow, not white.

question: Road rage and aggressive driving may be reduced by:
options: a:Refusing to signal.,b:Driving faster than other vehicles to get ahead.,c:Allowing extra travel time, obeying speed limits, and using turn signals.
note: To reduce road rage and aggressive driving, give yourself extra time so you are not rushed, obey the speed limit, and drive courteously. Using your turn signals, keeping a safe following distance, and avoiding confrontations all help keep emotions under control and traffic safer.

question: To reduce fatigue on a long trip, it is a good idea to:
options: a:Do arm exercises every hour.,b:Drive with one eye open at a time.,c:Stop and rest every two hours.
note: On long trips, stop about every two hours to rest, stretch, and get some fresh air. Regular breaks help prevent drowsiness, keep you alert, and reduce the risk of falling asleep or losing focus while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns green, you should:
options: a:Back up slowly if you misjudged timing.,b:Yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection.,c:Accelerate as quickly as possible.
note: Even when the light turns green, you must first check the intersection and yield to any pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles that are still clearing the intersection. A green light means you may go only when it is safe and the way is clear.

question: Are posters, signs, or window decals on vehicle windows permitted?
options: a:Allowed only if they do not block or significantly reduce your view.,b:They are a fun way to personalize your car.,c:They are generally prohibited on the windshield and front side windows except for items required by law.
note: Window obstructions are prohibited unless the item is specifically required by law. Do not place signs or stickers that block visibility.

question: When a school bus ahead on your side of the road has its red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Slow to a speed no faster than 10 mph.,b:Stop until the lights stop flashing.,c:Change lanes and pass cautiously.
note: When a school bus on your side of the road has its red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. Passing or driving slowly past the bus is illegal and extremely dangerous to children who may be crossing.

question: Where should you allow a larger space cushion than usual when stopped?
options: a:When stopped on an uphill slope.,b:At a stop sign in a flat area.,c:At a traffic circle.,d:On a straight, level road.
note: On an uphill slope, the vehicle ahead of you may roll backward when the driver releases the brake to move forward. Leaving extra space when stopped on a hill gives you time and room to react if the vehicle in front rolls back unexpectedly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection but opposing traffic blocks your view, you should:
options: a:Accelerate quickly once the first lane is clear.,b:Rely on an oncoming driver to wave you through.,c:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before turning.
note: When turning left across multiple lanes of oncoming traffic, you must not start your turn until you can clearly see that every lane you must cross is free of approaching vehicles. Never rely on another driver waving you through or try to dart out as soon as one lane looks open.

question: When weather changes suddenly, what should you do?
options: a:Ignore vehicles behind you since they should adapt.,b:Maintain your previous speed regardless of conditions.,c:Only worry about weather when it snows heavily.,d:Adjust your driving to the new conditions
note: Adjusting your driving to match changing weather is essential for safety. When rain, fog, snow, or wind begins, you should reduce speed, increase following distance, and drive more cautiously so you have enough time to react and can maintain control of the vehicle.

question: You should remove snow, frost, and ice from which parts of your vehicle before driving?
options: a:Only the windshield.,b:All windows.,c:Only the windshield and passenger window.
note: Before driving in winter conditions, you must clear snow, frost, and ice from all windows so you have an unobstructed view in every direction. You should also clear mirrors and lights so you can see and be seen by others, reducing the risk of collisions.

question: If you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights on the roadside, what must you do if safe to do so?
options: a:Continue in your lane at the posted speed.,b:Drive to the right side of the road and stop.,c:Change lanes away from the stopped vehicle if safe and slow down; if you cannot change lanes safely, slow down well below the speed limit and pass with caution.
note: Move over a lane away from stopped emergency, roadside assistance, or tow vehicles when it is safe; otherwise slow to below the posted speed limit and proceed with caution.

question: A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02 percent:
options: a:Has no effect on driving.,b:Only affects very inexperienced drivers.,c:Nearly doubles the risk of being in a fatal crash.
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect driving ability. Research shows that even a BAC as low as 0.02% can measurably impair judgment and reaction time, and each 0.02% increase in BAC is associated with a large increase in crash risk. You should never assume a low BAC has no effect on your driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic backs up behind you on a two-lane road, you should:
options: a:Pull off the road at the first safe opportunity to let traffic pass.,b:Keep driving at the same speed until a passing zone appears.,c:Increase your speed abruptly to clear the backup.,d:Stay in lane and prevent others from passing.
note: If you are traveling so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane road, you are required in many states to pull off at the first safe place and let other vehicles pass. This keeps traffic flowing smoothly and reduces the chance of risky passing maneuvers by impatient drivers.

question: Does an octagonal sign always require drivers to stop?
options: a:False,b:True
note: A red octagonal sign is reserved exclusively for STOP signs in the U.S. When you see this shape and color, you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move onto the shoulder.,b:Stay as far right as possible because the motorcycle is small.,c:Allow the motorcycle a full lane and be entirely in the left lane while passing.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other vehicle. When passing, move completely into the left lane, give them the full width of their lane, and pass as you would a car. Do not crowd or share the lane with a motorcycle.

question: Before entering an intersection, what order should you scan traffic?
options: a:Left only.,b:Left, then right, then left again.,c:Right only.
note: Before entering an intersection, scan left, then right, then left again. Traffic from the left is usually closer to you and reaches the intersection first, so you check that side twice to be sure it is safe before you proceed.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, you should first:
options: a:Turn back onto the roadway immediately and sharply.,b:Stop where you are and remain in the vehicle.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, firmly hold the steering wheel, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gradually. Once the vehicle is under control and traffic allows, gently steer back onto the pavement—do not jerk the wheel sharply, which can cause you to lose control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing on a multilane highway you should:
options: a:Ensure the passing lane is clear.,b:Always pass only on the right.,c:Ignore other traffic's speed.
note: Before passing on a multilane highway, make sure the lane you will use is clear, check your mirrors and blind spots, and signal before moving over. Adjust your speed safely to pass and return to your lane only when you can do so without cutting off another driver.

question: Must drivers yield to pedestrians in the street even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly?
options: a:Only if the pedestrian follows signals.,b:Yes — drivers must yield and take steps to avoid hitting them.,c:No — only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.
note: Drivers must always exercise due care to avoid colliding with pedestrians, even when pedestrians are careless or crossing improperly. You must slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield to pedestrians already in the roadway to prevent a crash.

question: You must yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:
options: a:Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.,b:Only if a crossing guard is present.,c:At all times.
note: A pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog is visually impaired and must always be given the right-of-way. You must stop and remain stopped until the person has safely crossed, and never honk or try to hurry them.

question: What does a red arrow displayed on a traffic signal instruct drivers to do?
options: a:Stop then proceed when clear,b:Stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to a green light or green arrow.,c:Slow and proceed carefully through the intersection.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped. You may not turn in the direction of the arrow until it changes to green or a green arrow, unless a specific sign at that intersection allows a turn on red after stopping and yielding.

question: If you see an animal on the road, you should:
options: a:Sound your horn and speed past.,b:Take no special action.,c:Pass slowly and cautiously to avoid frightening it.
note: When animals are on or near the road, slow down and pass cautiously. Sudden movements, loud horns, or speeding can startle animals and cause them to move unpredictably into your path, increasing the risk of a collision.

question: Which types of drugs may affect your ability to drive safely?
options: a:Illegal drugs only.,b:Illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over‑the‑counter medicines.,c:Only prescription medications.
note: Any drug that affects your mind or body can impair driving, including illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over‑the‑counter medicines. Some prescriptions and common cold or allergy medicines can cause drowsiness, blurred vision, or slowed reaction time. Always read labels and follow medical advice before driving.

question: Should you always drive more slowly than other traffic?
options: a:Yes,b:You yes,c:No — driving too slowly can block traffic and may be illegal.
note: You should drive at a safe speed for conditions, not simply slower than everyone else. Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can cause sudden braking and lane changes by other drivers, which increases crash risk and may be illegal if you unnecessarily block or impede traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, which action is prohibited?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and find an alternate route.,b:Proceed to the next exit.,c:Back up on the road or shoulder to reach the exit.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, you must never back up on the travel lanes or the shoulder. Backing on a freeway is extremely dangerous and illegal. Instead, continue to the next exit, leave the freeway safely, and then find a route that takes you back to your intended destination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers may not pass from either direction across which centerline marking?
options: a:Double solid yellow centerline.,b:Combination solid and broken yellow centerline.,c:Single broken yellow centerline.
note: A double solid yellow centerline on a two‑way road means vehicles in both directions are prohibited from crossing the line to pass. A combination of solid and broken yellow means only the side with the broken line may pass when safe, and a single broken yellow generally allows passing in both directions when it can be done safely.

question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light, how should you proceed?
options: a:Drive carefully through the intersection.,b:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,c:Stop and wait for the light to change.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. Slow down, be prepared to yield, and carefully check for cross traffic and pedestrians before entering the intersection. You do not have to stop unless needed for safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, it is safe to move back into the right lane when:
options: a:About three seconds have passed.,b:You can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,c:You have finished signaling for at least one second.,d:You can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, don’t move back into the right lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead and reduces the risk of cutting off the other driver.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A rectangular red sign.,b:A diamond-shaped yellow sign.,c:A reflective orange triangle.,d:A circular green sign.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle with a red border, mounted on the rear of vehicles that travel 25 mph or less, such as farm equipment. This alerts faster traffic to use extra caution and be prepared to slow down.

question: If your turn signals stop working, how should you indicate a turn?
options: a:Use your horn.,b:Use your headlights.,c:Use hand signals.
note: If your turn signals fail, you must use standard hand and arm signals to indicate turns and stops so other drivers know your intentions and can react safely.

question: Driving while impaired by medication is:
options: a:Allowed if you don't feel drowsy.,b:Allowed if prescribed by a doctor.,c:Never permitted.
note: Driving is illegal and unsafe if any medication or drug impairs your ability to operate a vehicle, even if it is prescribed. Always read labels and follow medical advice about driving while using medication.

question: Work zone signs indicate:
options: a:There are less-than-ideal driving conditions ahead and to use caution.,b:It is summer and conditions are normal.,c:You must immediately stop and back up.
note: Orange work zone signs warn that road work or maintenance is ahead and that conditions may be changing or hazardous. You should slow down, stay alert, and be prepared for lane shifts, workers, and equipment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings?
options: a:You only follow them if other traffic is present.,b:They are merely suggestions.,c:They apply only during daylight.,d:They must always be obeyed.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings are legal controls that regulate, warn, and guide drivers. They must be obeyed at all times, regardless of traffic or time of day.

question: At dusk or on overcast days you should:
options: a:Drive with your four-way flashers on.,b:Use only your parking lights.,c:Turn on your headlights.
note: Headlights must be used at dusk, dawn, and any time visibility is reduced, such as on overcast days. Use your low-beam headlights so other drivers can see you; parking lights or hazard flashers alone are not sufficient or legal substitutes for headlights while driving.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Brake lightly.,b:Stay off the brakes.,c:Brake abruptly.
note: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should stay off the brakes and off the accelerator. Braking, even lightly, can make the skid worse because it reduces traction and can cause the wheels to lock. Instead, look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go, and once you regain control, brake gently if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When using a roundabout, what should entering drivers do?
options: a:Enter and keep right of the central island.,b:Drive clockwise around the central island.,c:Yield to traffic already circulating in the roundabout.
note: Traffic in a roundabout always moves counterclockwise, and vehicles already in the roundabout have the right-of-way. When entering, you must slow down, yield to traffic already circulating and to pedestrians in crosswalks, then enter when it is safe and keep to the right of the central island.

question: If you stop along the roadway at night, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Use only your parking lights or hazard flashers.,b:Turn off all your lights.,c:Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beam headlights on.
note: If you must stop along the roadway at night, you should move as far off the road as possible and use your parking lights or hazard flashers so others can see your parked vehicle. You should not leave your headlights on while parked facing traffic, because they can blind approaching drivers and make it harder for them to see your vehicle’s position.

question: It is unlawful for a car to share a single lane with a motorcycle.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a lane, just like any other vehicle. A car must not share the same lane side-by-side with a motorcycle because it leaves the rider too little space and time to react. Always allow a motorcycle a full lane and follow at a safe distance.

question: Is it safe to stop on a railroad track if you are moving with a stream of vehicles?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Never stop on railroad tracks, even if traffic is moving slowly. Before you start across, make sure there is enough space on the far side of the tracks for your entire vehicle so you can clear the tracks without stopping.

question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving are likely to:
options: a:Be better drivers because they are not hungry.,b:Have trouble staying in their lane and controlling the vehicle.,c:Make no driving errors.
note: Eating or drinking while driving is a form of distracted driving. It takes at least one hand off the wheel and your attention away from the road, making it harder to stay in your lane and control the vehicle. This increases the chance of making mistakes or being involved in a crash.

question: When you see a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line in the center of the road, what does that mean?
options: a:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,b:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass; those next to the solid line may not.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions and neither may pass.,d:Passing is permitted from the side next to the solid line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. Vehicles on the side with the broken line may pass when it is safe. Vehicles on the side with the solid line must not cross it to pass.

question: Is it ever legal to drive through, around, or under a lowered railroad gate or barrier?
options: a:False — never drive through or under a lowered gate.,b:True — if the train has passed.,c:Only if directed by a railroad employee or law enforcement officer.,d:Only at night when visibility is reduced.
note: You must never drive through, around, or under a lowered railroad gate. The only exception is when a properly identified railroad employee or law enforcement officer is directing you to proceed because they know it is safe. Otherwise, always stop and wait until the gates are fully raised and the lights stop flashing.

question: How should a lap belt fit when properly adjusted?
options: a:Hidden under the seat cushion.,b:Crossing only the upper chest.,c:Snugly across your hip bones and upper thighs.,d:Loose and comfortable across your stomach.
note: A lap belt should be worn low and snug across the hip bones and touching the upper thighs, not across the soft part of the stomach. This positioning helps the strong bones of the pelvis absorb crash forces and reduces the risk of internal injuries.

question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches?
options: a:Try to reach your destination before it catches up.,b:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.,c:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right‑of‑way. Safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed. If you are in an intersection, continue through it and then pull over as soon as it is safe. Never try to outrun or race an emergency vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when should you move back into your lane?
options: a:After you are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.,b:As soon as you clear the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,c:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: Return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror, ensuring you have enough room.

question: If a traffic light changes from green to solid yellow as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.,b:Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue through.,c:Stop immediately regardless of distance.
note: A solid yellow light warns the signal will soon turn red; stop before entering if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed with caution.

question: To check blind spots and see vehicles not visible in mirrors, you should:
options: a:Check only inside rearview mirror.,b:Check only outside mirrors.,c:Look over your shoulders.
note: Blind spots are outside mirror coverage areas; a quick shoulder check is necessary before lane changes.

question: You must obey directions from a flagger in a construction zone.
options: a:True,b:False
note: In construction and work zones, flaggers have the same authority as traffic signals and signs. You must follow their directions, even if they differ from posted signs, because they are managing traffic around workers, equipment, and lane closures. Ignoring a flagger’s instructions is illegal and can be very dangerous.

question: How can you stay aware of traffic behind you?
options: a:Turn and look out your back window every few seconds.,b:Rely solely on the side mirrors.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots by tailgating.,d:Frequently check your rearview mirror.
note: Frequently checking your rearview mirror is the correct way to stay aware of traffic behind you. Glancing at it every few seconds helps you know where vehicles are and how fast they are approaching, so you can react safely. You should not turn around while driving, rely only on side mirrors, or tailgate to manage blind spots.

question: True or False: Roads are most dangerous at the start of a light rain when oils mix with water.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Roads are especially slippery at the beginning of a light rain because oil and residue on the pavement mix with the water and rise to the surface. This creates a slick, greasy layer that reduces traction. As rain continues, much of this buildup washes away and traction usually improves, though heavy rain can still be hazardous.

question: What color are signs that indicate areas of public recreation or historical sites?
options: a:Orange.,b:Blue.,c:Red.,d:Brown.
note: Brown traffic signs are used for guidance to recreational areas, parks, campgrounds, and points of cultural or historical interest. Recognizing brown signs helps you quickly identify locations related to outdoor activities and historic sites while driving.

question: Is failing an alcohol test the only way to be convicted of an OUI?
options: a:Only if there is DNA evidence.,b:Only if there is a breath test result.,c:True — conviction requires a failed test.,d:False — you can be convicted even if you refuse testing or based on officer testimony.
note: You can be convicted of Operating Under the Influence even without a failed breath or blood test. Officers can use observations such as driving behavior, field sobriety tests, and other evidence to show impairment. Refusing a test can also be used against you in court and usually leads to separate license penalties under implied consent laws.

question: If you plan to slow where other drivers may not expect it, what should you do before slowing?
options: a:Release the accelerator and drift to a stop.,b:Quickly tap your brakes three or four times to alert drivers behind you.,c:Slam on your brakes.
note: If you need to slow or stop where others might not expect it, quickly tapping your brakes several times turns your brake lights on and off, warning drivers behind you. This gives them extra time to react and helps prevent rear-end collisions. Avoid slamming on the brakes unless it is an emergency stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:
options: a:Assume they have the right-of-way.,b:Force their way into traffic if needed.,c:Yield to drivers already on the public road.
note: When entering a public road from a driveway or private road, you must always yield to traffic and pedestrians already on the public roadway. Vehicles on the public road have the right-of-way, and you may proceed only when it is safe and will not cause other road users to slow or stop suddenly.

question: What do downward-facing triangular signs typically indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:Yield.,c:Construction zones.
note: A downward-facing triangle is the standard shape for a yield sign. It tells you to slow down, be prepared to stop if necessary, and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection or roadway you are entering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A broken yellow centerline next to your lane means:
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is never permitted.,c:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline next to your lane means you may cross it to pass another vehicle if it is safe and legal to do so. You must ensure there is enough clear distance ahead, no oncoming traffic that would be affected, and no signs or conditions that prohibit passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is unlawful regarding passing?
options: a:Passing over or within 100 feet of a railroad crossing.,b:Passing another vehicle in any marked no-passing zone or where a sign prohibits it.,c:Passing when the centerline is broken and it's safe.,d:Passing when there is no oncoming traffic regardless of markings.
note: Passing is unlawful in any marked no-passing zone or where signs prohibit it, even if you do not see oncoming traffic. It is also illegal to pass at railroad crossings, on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, and in other specifically restricted areas. Always obey pavement markings and signs, and only pass where it is both permitted and safe.

question: What blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Slowing down to look at a collision scene (rubbernecking).,b:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,c:Using public transportation instead of a car.
note: Slowing down just to look at a collision or roadside incident, known as rubbernecking, disrupts the smooth flow of traffic. It can cause sudden slowdowns, traffic jams, and even additional crashes. Keep your attention on the road ahead and maintain a safe, steady speed unless you are required to stop or slow for safety or traffic control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, you should:
options: a:Get off at the next exit and return to the missed exit.,b:Stop and make a U-turn on the shoulder.,c:Roll down your window and ask another driver for directions.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, continue driving to the next exit, then safely get off and return using the proper ramps. Never stop, back up, or make a U‑turn on the highway or shoulder, as this is illegal and extremely dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How close may you legally follow an emergency vehicle that is using its alarm?
options: a:One mile,b:500 feet,c:250 feet
note: You must not follow an emergency vehicle that is responding to an emergency closer than about 500 feet. Staying back gives the emergency vehicle room to maneuver and prevents you from interfering with their response.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should drive the maximum posted speed limit only under which conditions?
options: a:During the night.,b:During the day.,c:Under ideal conditions.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum speed allowed under ideal conditions. You must slow down when visibility, traffic, road surface, or weather conditions are poor, even if that means driving well below the posted limit.

question: If you must drive in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights or hazard (four-way) flashers only.
