note: In fog, use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off water droplets in the fog and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams help you see the road and help others see you without increasing glare.

question: At a school crossing sign you should:
options: a:Always sound your horn to warn children.,b:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.,c:Always stop whether there is a stop sign or not.
note: At a school crossing sign, slow down, watch carefully for children, and be prepared to stop. Children may enter the road unexpectedly, so you must be especially alert and ready to yield to them.

question: If your vehicle with ABS begins to lose traction on a slippery road, what should you do?
options: a:Press and hold the gas pedal.,b:Pump the brakes.,c:Press and hold the brake pedal.
note: With ABS (anti-lock braking system), you should press and hold the brake pedal firmly and let the system work. ABS automatically pumps the brakes to help prevent wheel lockup and maintain steering control, so you should not pump the brakes yourself.

question: If your vehicle becomes disabled on a highway, you should:
options: a:Park with all four wheels off the traveled portion of the highway, if possible.,b:Stop in the right travel lane and leave hazard lights off.,c:Leave your vehicle where it stopped and stand in traffic to warn others.
note: If your vehicle becomes disabled on a highway, move it as far off the traveled portion of the road as possible, ideally with all four wheels off the roadway. Turn on your hazard lights and use warning devices if available, then stay in a safe place away from traffic.

question: Is it safe to drive beside a large truck inside a roundabout?
options: a:Only if the truck is turning left.,b:True — it's fine as long as you signal.,c:Only at speeds below 10 mph.,d:False — you should not attempt to drive next to a large truck in a roundabout.
note: You should not drive beside a large truck in a roundabout. Large trucks often need extra space and may swing wide or use more than one lane to turn, creating a serious squeeze risk for smaller vehicles alongside them.

question: Before changing lanes or attempting to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Signal your intention before changing lanes.,b:Check your blind spots and mirrors.,c:All of the above.
note: Before changing lanes or passing, you should always signal, check your mirrors, and quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Using all three steps helps ensure the lane is clear and other drivers are aware of your intentions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you must:
options: a:Slow and drive around the gates cautiously.,b:Come to a complete stop well back of the gates and wait until they lift.,c:Drive around the gates if you can't see a train.
note: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you must stop at a safe distance from the gates and wait. Do not drive around or under the gates; proceed only after the lights stop flashing and the gates are fully raised and the tracks are clear.

question: Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:
options: a:25 miles per hour.,b:45 miles per hour.,c:40 miles per hour.,d:35 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride up on a film of water and lose contact with the road. This can begin around 35 mph, especially with worn tires or deeper water, so you must slow down in heavy rain and drive with good tires and proper inflation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space you need to cross traffic safely depends on which factors?
options: a:Use of your turn signals.,b:Road and weather conditions and the speed and distance of oncoming traffic.,c:Presence of a stop sign.
note: The space you need to cross or enter traffic depends mainly on how fast other vehicles are going, how far away they are, and the road and weather conditions. On faster or slippery roads, you need a larger gap to cross safely. Turn signals and the presence of a stop sign do not change the actual space needed; they only control who must stop or indicate your intentions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and vehicles to your right and left arrive at an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your left.,b:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.,c:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right. This rule helps decide who goes first when there are no signs or signals. If you are to the left of another vehicle, you should let that vehicle proceed first.

question: When a red light is showing but a green arrow points in the direction you want to go, when may you proceed?
options: a:Only after the main light changes from red.,b:If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.,c:After first coming to a complete stop.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow. You may proceed if you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles already in the intersection. The red circular light does not apply to the movement allowed by the green arrow.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver on the road, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to assert yourself.,b:Challenge them.,c:Get out of their way.
note: When you encounter an aggressive driver, do not race, block, or challenge them. The safest response is to stay calm, avoid eye contact, and safely move out of their way when possible. This reduces the risk of a crash and prevents the situation from escalating.

question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:
options: a:Drive carefully, avoid slowing to stare, and obey posted directions.,b:Stop to watch the workers.,c:Decrease following distance to move through faster.,d:Pass without changing speed if you think it's safe.
note: In construction zones you must drive carefully, follow all posted signs and flagger directions, and avoid slowing down just to look at the work. This helps keep workers and drivers safe and keeps traffic flowing smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching, you should:
options: a:Stop immediately anywhere you are,b:Continue driving slowly and let it pass.,c:Drive as far to the right as is safe and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, you must move as far to the right as is safe and stop until it has passed. Do not stop in an intersection or keep driving alongside it, because that can block its path and delay its response.

question: If you exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill, what should you do before entering the curve?
options: a:Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.,b:Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.,c:Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
note: On a downhill, curved exit ramp you should slow to a safe speed before you enter the curve. Braking hard while already in the curve can cause skidding or loss of control, especially on a downgrade.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn from a one-way street, which lane should you be in?
options: a:The lane nearest the right curb.,b:The lane nearest the center of the street.,c:The lane nearest the left curb.
note: When turning left from a one‑way street, you must start from the lane nearest the left curb. You begin your turn from the lane closest to the direction you are turning to keep the turn short and to avoid cutting across other lanes.

question: Why does driving at night require extra caution?
options: a:Traffic is always faster at night.,b:Road rules change after dark.,c:Drivers cannot see as well at night,d:There are more pedestrians at night.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous because you cannot see as far or as clearly, making it harder to spot hazards in time. Headlights are required from about one‑half hour after sunset to one‑half hour before sunrise, or whenever visibility is reduced, to help you see and be seen.

question: Alcohol consumption negatively affects which abilities?
options: a:All of the above,b:Alertness,c:Coordination and reaction time
note: Alcohol affects multiple driving abilities at the same time. It reduces alertness, slows reaction time, and harms coordination, making it harder to notice hazards and respond in time. Because it impairs all of these abilities, any amount of drinking can increase your risk of a crash.

question: On slick roads, you should:
options: a:Accelerate rapidly out of turns.,b:Change lanes quickly.,c:Take turns more slowly than usual.
note: On slick roads, your tires have less traction, so it is easier to skid. You should slow down and take turns more slowly than usual so your tires can grip the road. Avoid sudden acceleration, braking, or quick lane changes, because these can cause you to lose control.

question: An aggressive driver may be identified by:
options: a:Erratic or improper lane changes.,b:Having many passengers in the car.,c:Driving consistently below the speed limit.
note: Aggressive drivers often show unsafe, hostile behaviors such as erratic or improper lane changes, tailgating, speeding, and failing to yield. These actions increase crash risk and reduce the time other drivers have to react. The number of passengers or simply driving slowly does not by itself indicate aggressive driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing for a right turn, your vehicle must be:
options: a:As close to the right side of the road as practicable.,b:Near the center of the street.,c:Close to the left side of the street.,d:At the lane's centerline.
note: When turning right, you should be positioned as close to the right curb or edge of the roadway as is safe and practicable. This position shortens the turn, keeps you out of oncoming traffic, and makes your path more predictable to other road users.

question: Does how fast you drive affect the distance your vehicle travels after you brake?
options: a: ,b:TRUE,c:FALSE
note: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop. At higher speeds, your vehicle travels farther during your reaction time and also needs more distance for the brakes to slow and stop the car. Doubling your speed can more than double your total stopping distance.

question: Which substances can impair driving and lead to DUII charges?
options: a:Beer,b:All of the above,c:Controlled substances (illegal drugs or prescriptions)
note: Driving can be impaired by any alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many prescription or over‑the‑counter medicines. DUI/DUII laws apply to alcohol and to controlled or other impairing substances, not just beer. You must never drive after using anything that affects your ability to think clearly, react quickly, or control your vehicle.

question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:
options: a:Pay attention, obey signals, and look both ways before crossing tracks.,b:Assume no trains will come if no gates are down.,c:Drive around lowered gates if traffic is heavy.,d:Focus only on automobile traffic and ignore rail signals.
note: At light rail crossings, you must obey all signals and signs, look carefully both ways along the tracks, and only cross when it is clearly safe. Never drive around lowered gates or ignore rail signals, even if you do not immediately see a train.

question: An octagonal traffic sign always indicates what?
options: a:A speed limit sign.,b:A hospital sign.,c:A stop sign.
note: An octagon-shaped sign is used only for STOP signs. When you see this shape, you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:
options: a:Pull to the right curb and stop.,b:Keep driving in your lane at the same speed.,c:Slow down but remain in your lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and siren, you must yield the right of way by pulling as close as safely possible to the right edge or curb and stopping until it has passed. Do not stop in an intersection; clear the intersection first, then pull over.

question: Is it safe to pull in front of a large truck that is slowing or stopping?
options: a:It is safe as long as you signal first.,b:True,c:False
note: It is not safe to pull in front of a large truck that is slowing or stopping. Large vehicles need much more distance to stop because of their size and weight. Cutting in front of them reduces their stopping space and can cause a rear‑end collision if they cannot brake in time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may a driver pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder?
options: a:When traffic is moving slowly.,b:When the shoulder is paved.,c:Never; passing on the shoulder is prohibited.,d:If the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is a clearly marked lane or space to pass on the right (not the shoulder).
note: Passing on the shoulder is unsafe and not permitted under any circumstances.

question: Can sudden wind gusts on highways create problems for all vehicles?
options: a:Only cause visibility problems.,b:Only affect the movement of large vehicles.,c:Can cause problems for all vehicles.
note: Strong or sudden wind gusts can push any vehicle sideways, making it harder to stay in your lane. While large vehicles, trailers, and motorcycles are especially vulnerable, all drivers must be prepared to steer smoothly and reduce speed when winds are strong, because both vehicle control and visibility can be affected.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered a distraction?
options: a:It can distract your attention from the driving task.,b:It occupies the driver's hands, eyes, or mind and diverts attention from driving.,c:It makes other drivers pay attention to you.
note: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it takes your attention away from the road. It can occupy your hands, eyes, and mind, which slows your reaction time and makes it easier to miss hazards. Any activity that diverts your focus from driving increases your risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you start across an intersection if you know you'll block it when the light turns red?
options: a:Only if you entered on a green light.,b:Only if you entered on a yellow light.,c:Never.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it, regardless of the signal color when you enter. If you move into the intersection and then have to stop and block cross traffic when the light changes, you can be cited and you create a traffic hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever permissible to exceed the speed limit to complete a pass?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Speed limits apply even when you are passing. You must complete any passing maneuver without exceeding the posted speed limit. If you cannot safely pass without speeding, you should wait for a better opportunity rather than increase your speed beyond the legal limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting a highway you should slow down:
options: a:On the main road just before the exit lane.,b:Only when you see a toll booth.,c:After you have moved into the exit lane.
note: On highways, maintain the mainline speed until you are safely in the exit (deceleration) lane. Once in the exit lane, then slow down to the posted exit or ramp speed. Slowing on the main road before entering the exit lane can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: When driving on snow or ice, you should:
options: a:Drive exactly as you would in normal conditions.,b:Use cruise control to keep steady speed.,c:Make speed and directional changes more gradually than usual.
note: On snow or ice, reduce speed and make all changes—speed, steering, and braking—more gradually than usual to avoid skids. Sudden moves can cause loss of traction. Never use cruise control on slippery surfaces because it can cause your wheels to spin and you may lose control.

question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is true?
options: a:They can stay alert by opening a window or turning up the radio.,b:Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly they may appear to be drunk.,c:Drinking strong black coffee is enough to make them safe to drive.
note: Drowsy driving can impair judgment, reaction time, and lane control so severely that the driver may appear drunk. Tricks like opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee do not reliably restore alertness. The only safe solution is to rest before driving or stop and take a real break if you become drowsy.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrived last.,b:Drivers who do not stop.,c:The driver who arrived first.
note: At a four-way stop, the vehicle that arrives first has the right-of-way and proceeds first after stopping. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. All drivers must come to a complete stop before proceeding.

question: When another vehicle approaches from the opposite direction at night, what should your headlights be set to?
options: a:High beam setting.,b:Off; use parking lights only.,c:Alternate between high and low beams rapidly.,d:Low beam setting.
note: When another vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction at night, use your low-beam headlights. High beams can blind or dazzle the other driver, creating a serious hazard. Switch to low beams within the distance specified by your state (commonly about 500 feet) to ensure safe visibility for everyone.

question: Which of the following should you NOT do when changing lanes?
options: a:Signal your intention before changing lanes.,b:Fail to check your side and rearview mirrors and blind spot.,c:Check for drivers moving into the same lane.,d:Look over your shoulder to confirm the lane is clear.
note: When changing lanes, you must always signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. The unsafe action is failing to check mirrors and blind spots, because you may not see a vehicle next to you and could sideswipe it.

question: If you approach an intersection and the light turns yellow, what should you generally do?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.,b:Speed up to cross before it turns red.,c:Slow down and proceed through without caution.
note: A solid yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through with caution rather than speeding up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when meeting an oncoming vehicle, what must you allow the other vehicle?
options: a:Demand the other vehicle pull over.,b:Pull completely off the road and stop.,c:At least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.
note: On narrow roads, each driver must allow the other at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the roadway. This ensures both vehicles have enough space to pass safely without forcing the other driver off the road.

question: If it begins to snow or sleet while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Approach other vehicles more quickly.,b:Ignore conditions and maintain usual distance.,c:Keep windshield and mirrors clear and allow extra following distance.
note: Snow and sleet reduce traction and visibility, so you need more time and space to react. Keep your windshield and mirrors clear and increase your following distance so you have a longer stopping distance on slippery roads.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, you should look:
options: a:Toward the right side of the road to avoid glare.,b:Toward the left edge of your lane.,c:Directly at the headlights to signal them.
note: Bright high beams from oncoming traffic can temporarily blind you. To reduce glare, glance toward the right side of the road and use the edge line as a guide, rather than looking directly at the headlights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:When you are on a hill or curve.,b:When you are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.,c:When you are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.
note: You may only pass when the line next to your lane is broken and you have enough clear distance to do so safely. Passing is not allowed when there is a solid line next to your lane or when your view is blocked, such as on hills or curves, because you cannot see oncoming traffic well enough to pass safely.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always sound your horn when you see children.,b:Always stop,c:Watch for children and be ready to stop.
note: A school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing the road. You should slow down, watch carefully for children who may enter the street unexpectedly, and be ready to stop if needed. You are not required to stop every time you see the sign, only when children or a crossing guard are present or when otherwise required by law or signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should a driver do when a traffic control signal is not operating?
options: a:Speed through to clear the intersection quickly.,b:Proceed through if the intersection appears clear without stopping.,c:Treat the intersection as an all-way stop and come to a full stop.
note: When a traffic signal is completely out, you must treat the intersection as an all-way stop. Come to a full stop at the intersection, then proceed in the order of arrival, yielding to any vehicle already in the intersection and to pedestrians. Do not assume it is safe to go just because it looks clear.

question: If your wheels slip off the pavement edge, you should:
options: a:Speed up to regain control.,b:Slam on the brakes immediately.,c:Gradually reduce speed,d:Jerk the wheel to force back onto the road quickly.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, keep a firm grip on the wheel, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gradually while staying on the shoulder. Once you have the vehicle under control and your speed is reduced, gently steer back onto the pavement when it is safe. Sudden braking, jerking the wheel, or speeding up can cause you to lose control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to exceed the posted speed limit when passing another vehicle?
options: a:True,b:False,c:Not sure
note: You must never drive faster than the posted speed limit, even when passing another vehicle. When passing, you should only move into the passing lane if you can complete the maneuver without exceeding the speed limit and with enough clear distance to return safely to your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You have the right-of-way when turning left on which traffic signal?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A steady yellow light.,c:A green arrow pointing left.,d:A solid red light with a left-turn sign.
note: A green left arrow means you have a protected left turn: oncoming traffic and pedestrians facing the signal are stopped, so you have the right‑of‑way to turn. Still check the intersection before turning, but you do not need to yield to oncoming vehicles when the green arrow is on.

question: To whom must you yield the right-of-way when a pedestrian is present?
options: a:Only pedestrians in marked crosswalks.,b:Any pedestrian crossing any street.,c:Pedestrians only when the light is red.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks and must use due care to avoid hitting any pedestrian in the roadway. Even outside crosswalks, if a pedestrian is in the street and you can safely yield, you must slow or stop to let them pass.

question: Where are stop lines typically painted on the roadway?
options: a:Next to churches and schools only.,b:Only in curves and on hills.,c:Across traffic lanes at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and at pedestrian crosswalks. They show where you must stop at a stop sign or red light so that you stay clear of crosswalks and the intersection.

question: If you are in an intersection and hear an emergency vehicle using siren and lights, you should:
options: a:Pull to the right of the intersection and stop immediately.,b:Continue through the intersection.,c:Stop immediately in the intersection.
note: If you are already in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, drive through and clear the intersection first. Then, as soon as it is safe, pull to the right side of the road and stop to let the emergency vehicle pass. Never stop in the middle of an intersection.

question: Should you use low beam headlights when driving in fog?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Use low beam headlights in fog because high beams reflect off the water droplets in the air and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and improve visibility in foggy conditions.

question: How can you reduce the risk of rear-end collisions?
options: a:Always stop abruptly to signal following drivers.,b:Avoid sudden stops and let your vehicle slow before braking.,c:Never check mirrors before stopping.
note: Gradually slowing before braking gives drivers behind you more time to react. Ease off the accelerator first, then apply steady pressure to the brakes so your brake lights come on early and predictably. Avoid sudden, hard stops whenever possible, because they increase the chance that a following driver will not have enough time or distance to avoid hitting you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before moving from the right lane into the left lane on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Check mirrors and look over your left shoulder for a blind spot, then signal.,b:Only check your rearview mirror for traffic before moving.,c:Signal after you begin moving into the lane.,d:Assume no vehicles are in the other lane if mirrors look clear.
note: Before changing lanes, you must check traffic using your mirrors and then turn your head to quickly look over your shoulder to check the blind spot in the direction you’re moving. Signal before you start moving into the lane so other drivers know your intention. Never rely only on mirrors, and never start moving first and signal later.

question: When you hear the siren of a fire engine behind you, you must:
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.,b:Slow down and continue driving.,c:Turn on your flashers and continue at the same speed.,d:Drive to the nearest exit and stop there.
note: When an emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights approaches from behind, you must immediately yield the right-of-way by pulling as close as safely possible to the right edge or curb and stopping. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed and it is safe to reenter traffic. Do not continue driving alongside or in front of the emergency vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In traffic it is safest to:
options: a:Drive faster than the flow to get ahead.,b:Drive slower than everyone else to be safe.,c:Drive with the flow of traffic within posted limits.
note: It is safest to drive at a speed that matches the flow of traffic while staying within the posted speed limit and adjusting for conditions. Driving much faster than other traffic increases the chance of collisions at intersections and lane changes, while driving much slower can cause other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly, also raising crash risk.

question: Before backing your vehicle, what steps should you take?
options: a:Depend only on your mirrors.,b:Walk completely around the vehicle and check for obstacles before backing.,c:Back quickly to minimize time spent reversing.
note: Before backing, walk around your vehicle if needed to check for children, pedestrians, and obstacles that may be hard to see from the driver’s seat. Once inside, look in all directions and turn your head to look out the rear window while backing; use your mirrors only as a supplement. Back slowly and be prepared to stop if you lose sight of any area behind you.

question: Does safe passing depend on the cooperation of both drivers?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Safe passing does depend on cooperation from both drivers. The passing driver must only pass when it is legal and safe, and the driver being passed should not speed up and should allow enough space for the passing vehicle to return to the lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: After being stopped by police, a driver should immediately exit the vehicle and approach the officer's cruiser.
options: a:False,b:True
note: When stopped by police, you should stay inside your vehicle, keep your hands visible on the steering wheel, and wait for the officer’s instructions. Exiting your vehicle or walking toward the officer’s car can be unsafe and is generally discouraged unless the officer specifically directs you to do so.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is in your vicinity, what is your responsibility?
options: a:Speed up to avoid interaction.,b:Make every effort to give it a clear path of travel by pulling to the side when safe.,c:Stop your vehicle immediately and block the lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely pull to the right side of the road and stop, if possible, so the emergency vehicle has a clear path to pass. Do not speed up or block the lane.

question: When entering a roundabout you should slow and:
options: a:Signal and enter without yielding to pedestrians.,b:Yield only to vehicles in the roundabout.,c:Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists and to traffic already in the roundabout.
note: When approaching a roundabout, slow down and yield to pedestrians and bicyclists at the crosswalks, and also yield to traffic already in the roundabout. Enter only when there is a safe gap in circulating traffic.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing without gates or flashing signals, you should:
options: a:Cross immediately and quickly without looking.,b:Always stop before crossing regardless of conditions.,c:Prepare to yield to any approaching train and ensure your vehicle can clear the tracks completely.
note: At a railroad crossing without gates or flashing signals, slow down, look and listen for trains in both directions, and be prepared to stop. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks without stopping on them.

question: Before making a turn you should:
options: a:Turn on hazard lights instead of signaling.,b:Activate your turn signal several seconds before turning.,c:Increase speed to complete the turn faster.,d:Begin turning the wheel immediately without signaling.
note: You must signal before turning so other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know what you plan to do. Turn on your turn signal at least several seconds before you begin the turn, not as you turn the wheel. This gives others time to react and helps prevent collisions.

question: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning on wet pavement, you should:
options: a:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.,b:Use cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,c:Slow down.,d:Drive in the tracks of the vehicle ahead to help your tires contact the road.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road, usually at higher speeds on wet pavement. The best way to reduce the risk is to slow down, especially when it first starts to rain or when water is pooling on the road. Avoid sudden steering or braking and make sure your tires are in good condition.

question: Why must you be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:They rarely use headlights.,b:Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers than other motorists.,c:They are smaller and more difficult to see than cars.,d:They are not required to obey traffic laws.
note: Motorcycles are much smaller than cars and can be easily hidden in blind spots or behind other vehicles. Because of their size, it is harder to judge their speed and distance, and they can appear suddenly in your path. Always check mirrors and blind spots carefully, use extra caution when turning or changing lanes, and give motorcycles a full lane and plenty of space.

question: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is:
options: a:A distracting activity that can reduce attention and control.,b:Beneficial for driver alertness.,c:Irrelevant to driving performance.,d:A required break activity on long trips.
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is a distraction. It takes at least one hand off the wheel and part of your attention away from the road while you handle lighters, cigarettes, or ashes. Any activity that divides your focus or reduces your control of the vehicle increases your risk of a crash and should be avoided while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady yellow light at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,b:Stop immediately, even if you are already in the intersection.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.,d:Proceed through the intersection without checking for cross traffic.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already too close to the intersection to stop safely when the light turns yellow, continue through with caution. Never speed up to beat the red light.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline on a two-lane road mean?
options: a:A construction zone is ahead.,b:Passing is never permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from either direction when it is safe to do so.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line is broken, vehicles in either direction may cross it to pass if the lane is clear and it is safe and legal to do so. You must be sure there is no oncoming traffic and enough space to complete the pass without speeding or cutting back too sharply.

question: When may you cross a solid yellow centerline?
options: a:Only to make a turn into or out of a driveway or street.,b:At any time to pass other vehicles.,c:During daylight hours only.
note: Solid yellow lines generally should not be crossed except to turn into driveways or side roads where permitted.

question: Do ramps and bridges freeze before other road surfaces in cold weather?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Ramps and bridges often freeze before the rest of the road because they are exposed to cold air from above and below. This allows ice to form even when nearby road surfaces may still appear just wet. Approach bridges, overpasses, and ramps with extra caution in cold or near-freezing temperatures, and reduce speed to avoid skidding.

question: When driving at night, what is a recommended safety measure?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.
note: At night your visibility is reduced, so you should increase your following distance to give yourself more time to see hazards and stop safely. Use low beams when following other vehicles or when there is oncoming traffic, and use high beams only when they will not blind other drivers. Avoid looking directly into oncoming headlights; instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane to reduce glare while staying in your lane.

question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:Because following too closely will get you caught in the vehicle's slipstream.,b:To better see around the sides of the vehicle.,c:Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles.
note: Large vehicles such as trucks and buses block your view of the road ahead and have larger blind spots. By increasing your following distance, you can see farther down the road around the sides of the vehicle and have more time to react to slowing or stopped traffic. This extra space also makes it easier for the truck driver to see you and reduces the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: On possibly slippery roads you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed and avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.,b:Use cruise control to maintain speed.,c:Always drive at the maximum posted speed.
note: On slippery roads, you are more likely to lose traction when you brake, accelerate, or steer suddenly. Reduce your speed and make all changes in speed or direction gradually. Do not use cruise control on slippery surfaces because it can cause the vehicle to accelerate or maintain speed when you actually need to slow down.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and diagonal slash mean?
options: a:That drivers should come to a complete stop.,b:That an action is forbidden.,c:That some drivers should yield to other drivers.
note: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a diagonal slash over a symbol means that the action shown is prohibited. For example, a left-turn arrow with a red circle and slash means no left turn. These signs tell you what you must not do, not what you must do.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your shoulder.,b:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:After about three seconds.
note: After passing, you should not move back into the right lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This helps ensure you have enough space and are not cutting the other driver off. After confirming this, check your blind spot and signal before returning to the lane.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right, you should:
options: a:Quickly turn in front of the truck to beat it.,b:Try to squeeze between the vehicle and the curb.,c:Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.
note: Large trucks and buses often need extra room to make right turns and may swing wide to the left before turning right. Never try to squeeze between the vehicle and the curb or cut in front of it. Stay behind and wait until the truck or bus has fully completed the turn before you make your right turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road you must:
options: a:Flash your lights to warn oncoming traffic.,b:Use the shoulder to pass.,c:Move into the lane belonging to oncoming traffic and pass only when it is safe and legal to do so.
note: On a two-lane, two-way road, you must move into the lane used by oncoming traffic to pass a slower vehicle. Only do this where passing is legal (for example, with a broken center line on your side) and when you have enough clear distance ahead to pass safely without interfering with oncoming traffic. Never use the shoulder to pass.

question: Why is night driving especially hazardous?
options: a:There are more cars on the road at night.,b:You cannot see as far as during daytime,c:Headlights make it easier to judge speed.,d:The speed limit is always higher at night.
note: Night driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as far ahead as in daylight. Headlights limit how much of the road, hazards, and other vehicles you can see, and reduced visibility makes it harder to judge distance and speed. This means you must drive more cautiously and often at a lower speed than in daytime.

question: A green traffic arrow controlling a turn means:
options: a:Traffic in the indicated lane may proceed only in the arrow's direction and has the right-of-way.,b:The arrow is equivalent to a circular green and you may go any direction.,c:You may proceed only if a circular green light also appears.,d:The arrow applies only on one-way streets.
note: A green arrow means you may proceed only in the direction the arrow points, and turning traffic generally has the right-of-way over oncoming traffic and pedestrians that face a red signal. You must still watch for any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection, but the arrow gives you a protected turn in that direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection instructs drivers to:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop until a green light appears.,c:Continue at normal speed without change.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must slow down, look carefully for cross traffic and pedestrians, and be prepared to yield if necessary. Treat it as a warning that conditions at or near the intersection require extra attention.

question: If you see heavy smoke covering the roadway ahead, you should:
options: a:Turn on high beams and drive through.,b:Turn on four-way flashers and continue slowly.,c:Reduce speed, move as far right as possible, and stop if you cannot see the road ahead clearly.
note: If heavy smoke or fog is covering the roadway and you cannot see clearly, you should immediately reduce speed, turn on your low-beam headlights and hazard flashers, and move as far right as you safely can. If visibility is severely reduced, pull completely off the roadway, stop, and wait until conditions improve. Driving into thick smoke at normal speed is extremely dangerous because you may not see stopped vehicles, debris, or other hazards in time to avoid a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Continuously passing slower vehicles on a two-lane two-way road will:
options: a:Always be legal if you signal.,b:Help prevent traffic congestion.,c:Increase your risk of a collision.,d:Get you to your destination much more safely and quickly.
note: Frequently passing slower vehicles on a two-lane, two-way road greatly increases your collision risk. Each pass requires you to enter the oncoming lane, judge the speed and distance of approaching traffic, and complete the maneuver quickly. The more often you do this, the more chances there are for misjudgment or an unexpected hazard, so you should pass only when necessary and clearly safe.

question: If a school bus is stopped on the opposite side of a multilane highway separated by a median, what must you do?
options: a:Must stop until the school bus begins moving.,b:May continue driving because the median separates traffic.,c:Must stop and wait for the flashing lights to stop.
note: When a divided highway has a median or physical barrier, traffic on the far side need not stop for a stopped school bus; otherwise all directions must stop.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Reach down and try to pull the accelerator up.,b:Turn off your headlights and continue driving slowly.,c:Shift the vehicle into neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.,d:Shift into park immediately.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift the transmission into neutral, and apply steady, firm pressure on the brakes. Steer to a safe location off the roadway, then once stopped, turn off the engine. Do not reach down to pull up the pedal while moving, and do not shift into park until the vehicle is fully stopped, as this can damage the transmission or cause loss of control.

question: If you drink alcohol while taking medication, the result may be:
options: a:One negates the other.,b:The combination could multiply the impairing effects.,c:Alcohol helps the medicine work better.
note: Combining alcohol with prescription or over‑the‑counter medications can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment more than either substance alone. The effects often multiply, making driving extremely dangerous. Never assume alcohol and medicine cancel each other out or improve how either works; always read labels and follow medical advice before driving.

question: When driving through a work zone, you should:
options: a:Pass other vehicles as soon as possible.,b:Avoid tailgating and maintain a safe following distance.,c:Follow the vehicle ahead closely.
note: In work zones, traffic may slow or stop unexpectedly, and workers and equipment can be close to the roadway. Maintain a larger following distance than usual so you have time to react, and never tailgate. Follow posted work‑zone speed limits, obey flaggers, and be prepared for sudden lane shifts or stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the best mindset regarding right-of-way rules?
options: a:Assume most drivers obey the rules so you can proceed quickly.,b:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way to avoid collisions.,c:Assume all drivers will obey right-of-way rules.
note: Right‑of‑way rules do not give you an absolute right to proceed; they tell you when you must yield. To avoid collisions, always be prepared to yield even when you are legally entitled to go first. Never assume other drivers will follow the rules—drive defensively and be willing to give up your right‑of‑way if it prevents a crash.

question: What important action should you take before making a turn?
options: a:Speed up to complete the turn quickly.,b:Check traffic in all directions.,c:Close your windows.,d:Always move into the left lane before turning.
note: Before turning, you must check traffic in all directions—ahead, behind, and to both sides—to be sure the way is clear and it is safe to turn. As you check, adjust your speed so you can make a smooth, controlled turn without surprising other drivers or pedestrians.

question: How should small children ride in a vehicle to be safe?
options: a:Stand on the floor in the back of the vehicle.,b:Be safely held by a strong adult.,c:Be secured in an appropriate child safety seat.,d:Sit on an adult's lap with a seat belt around both.
note: Small children must always be secured in a properly installed, age‑ and size‑appropriate child safety seat or booster seat. Adult seat belts alone do not fit young children correctly, and holding a child in your arms is extremely dangerous in a crash because you cannot restrain them against the force of impact.

question: When following another vehicle at night, what headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights until you are 10 feet behind.,c:Turn off headlights and use parking lights.,d:Alternate between high and low beams.
note: When you are following another vehicle at night, use low beam headlights. High beams can reflect in the other driver’s mirrors and cause glare, making it harder for them to see and increasing the risk of a collision.

question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol’s effects from your body?
options: a:Take a cold shower.,b:Wait.,c:Drink strong coffee.
note: Only time allows the body to eliminate alcohol; coffee, showers, or exercise do not reduce blood alcohol concentration.

question: Before you enter an intersection, in what sequence should you look?
options: a:Down at your speedometer then forward.,b:Left, right, then left again.,c:Only to the left.,d:Only to the right.
note: Before entering an intersection, scan for hazards by looking left, then right, then left again. Traffic coming from your left reaches you first, so you check that side twice to be sure it is still clear before you proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different highways at the same time, which must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,b:Either one.,c:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
note: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions by giving priority to the vehicle on the right.

question: What is the effect of taking drugs together with alcohol?
options: a:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,b:It lessens alcohol's effect on driving ability.,c:It increases the risk of causing a crash and may multiply impairment.
note: Alcohol and many drugs both affect the brain and nervous system. When taken together, their effects can combine or multiply, causing much greater impairment than either one alone. This greatly increases the risk of a crash, even if each substance is taken in a small amount.

question: When bad weather reduces visibility, you should:
options: a:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,b:Speed up to get past bad weather quickly.,c:Increase following distance.
note: In bad weather with reduced visibility, you need more time and space to see hazards and react safely. Increasing your following distance gives you extra room to stop or maneuver if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A yellow left-turn arrow that is steady indicates:
options: a:The protected left turn is ending and drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.,b:You have unlimited time to complete the turn.,c:Left turns remain protected until the green arrow returns.
note: A steady yellow left‑turn arrow means the protected left‑turn phase is ending. You should prepare to stop if you have not yet entered the intersection, and be ready to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians as the signal changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line indicates what?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line, and only when it is safe. Vehicles next to the solid yellow line are not allowed to cross it to pass.

question: Before you switch on the ignition, what should you do?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt.,b:Both of the above.,c:Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.
note: Before starting the vehicle, you should make it a habit to buckle your own safety belt and ensure that all passengers are properly buckled. The driver is responsible for making sure everyone is restrained before the vehicle moves.

question: Refusing to submit to a chemical test when requested by a police officer in Maine will:
options: a:Only result in a warning the first time.,b:Result in immediate suspension of your driver's license.,c:Be encouraged if you are unsure about sobriety.,d:Have no consequences if you decline.
note: Maine’s implied consent law means that by driving, you agree to take a chemical test if lawfully requested by an officer. Refusing the test results in an immediate license suspension and can bring additional penalties, even if you are not convicted of OUI.

question: What is the best way to handle being tailgated?
options: a:Change lanes or gradually slow to encourage the tailgater to pass.,b:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.,c:Slam on your brakes to get the driver to back off.
note: If someone is following too closely, avoid sudden braking or speeding up. Instead, maintain a steady speed, gradually slow if needed, and change lanes or create a safe opportunity for the tailgater to pass. This reduces the risk of a rear-end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the interstate, you should check for a traffic gap, match the speed of traffic, signal, and:
options: a:Merge carefully into the gap.,b:Expect oncoming drivers to yield to you.,c:Wait for the entire lane to clear until merging.
note: When using an entrance ramp, use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, signal, check your mirrors and blind spot, find a safe gap, and then merge carefully. Do not assume other drivers will move or slow down for you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required at an intersection and there is no stop line or crosswalk marked, where should you stop?
options: a:Only where you can see at least 200 feet on either side,b:At the point nearest to the intersecting roadway where you can get a view of approaching traffic.,c:Is not required to stop.
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, you must stop before entering the intersection at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can clearly see approaching traffic. Do not pull into the intersection to gain a better view before stopping.

question: When may you cross a dashed white line?
options: a:Only during daylight hours.,b:At any time regardless of traffic.,c:When it is safe to change lanes.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross them when you are changing lanes or merging, but only after checking mirrors and blind spots and ensuring it is safe to move.

question: Double solid yellow lines down the center of the road mean:
options: a:Railroad crossing ahead.,b:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean vehicles in both directions are prohibited from passing by crossing the lines. You may cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road, or when directed by traffic control or to avoid an immediate hazard, but not to pass another moving vehicle.

question: Defensive drivers typically:
options: a:Anticipate what others might do and prepare to react.,b:Always assume no one will yield to them.,c:Expect other drivers to always do the right thing.
note: Defensive drivers stay alert and anticipate what other road users might do, including possible mistakes. They leave space, scan ahead, and are prepared to react safely instead of assuming others will always follow the rules.

question: Temporary signs in construction and maintenance areas have what colors?
options: a:Yellow background with blue writing.,b:Red background with green writing.,c:Orange background with black writing.
note: Construction and maintenance work zone signs are orange with black letters or symbols. These signs warn of changing road conditions, so you should slow down, stay alert, and be prepared for workers and equipment.

question: If another vehicle appears likely to hit you, you should:
options: a:Wave your arms.,b:Sound your horn to warn them.,c:Only use emergency lights.
note: If another vehicle may hit you, use your horn to warn the other driver and try to get their attention. At the same time, be ready to slow, stop, or steer away to reduce the chance or severity of a collision.

question: What general rule should you follow when driving in a construction zone?
options: a:Expect the unexpected and use extra caution.,b:Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.,c:Drive slightly faster to clear the zone quickly.
note: In construction zones you should always expect the unexpected, slow down, and use extra caution. Workers, equipment, lane shifts, and sudden stops are common, so you must be prepared to react safely and give workers plenty of space.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Wait for police before moving the vehicle even if it creates a hazard.,b:Never move your vehicle under any circumstances.,c:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway.,d:Leave the vehicle and wait in the middle of the road.
note: If your vehicle is drivable and no one is seriously injured, you should move it out of the traffic lane to the shoulder or a safe area. This helps prevent additional crashes and keeps traffic flowing, while you stay at the scene to exchange information and assist if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The posted maximum speed limit is the fastest you may legally drive under ideal conditions:
options: a:False,b:True,c:
note: The posted maximum speed limit is not always the fastest you may legally drive; it is the maximum allowed only when conditions are ideal. By law you must adjust your speed to road, traffic, and weather conditions, and drive slower whenever conditions are not ideal.

question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what is the correct action?
options: a:Drive slowly and pass them,b:Honk and proceed as normal.,c:Wait and let the pedestrians finish crossing.,d:Speed up to clear the crosswalk before they arrive.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk and wait until the intersection is clear before proceeding.

question: What does a yellow-and-black diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:Services such as gas or food.,b:Traffic laws and regulations.,c:Warning about conditions on or near the road ahead.,d:Directions to nearby cities and towns.
note: Yellow-and-black diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to special conditions or hazards ahead, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or changes in road width, so you can slow down and proceed with caution.

question: How often should drivers check their mirrors for traffic behind them?
options: a:About every 45 seconds.,b:About every 20 seconds.,c:About every 10 seconds.
note: Good drivers scan all around them, including behind, on a frequent and regular basis. A common guideline is to check your mirrors roughly every 6–8 seconds so you stay aware of vehicles approaching from the rear or in adjacent lanes. Among the choices given, checking about every 10 seconds is the closest to this safe practice and helps you react early to changing traffic conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is true about passing maneuvers?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and ensure there is no oncoming traffic.,b:Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.,c:When passing, wait until you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your original lane.,d:All of the above.
note: When passing, you must signal well before changing lanes (at least 100 feet in most areas), check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to clear your blind spot. After passing, do not move back into the lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. These steps keep you from cutting off other drivers and reduce the risk of a collision.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Coordination only,b:Alertness only,c:Both coordination and alertness
note: Alcohol and many drugs affect several critical driving abilities at the same time. They reduce coordination, slow your reactions, and lower your alertness and judgment. Because both coordination and alertness are impaired, driving after using alcohol or drugs is extremely dangerous even if you feel only “a little” affected.

question: An orange-colored road sign typically indicates:
options: a:The start of a no-passing zone.,b:Construction,c:A school zone is ahead.,d:A railroad crossing is ahead.
note: Orange road signs are used for temporary traffic control in work or incident areas. They warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency operations on or near the roadway so you can slow down, be prepared for workers or equipment, and follow any changed traffic patterns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians, even if the pedestrian ignores a traffic signal.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers must always do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, even if the pedestrian is acting unsafely. However, the law does not give pedestrians the right-of-way in every situation, such as when they enter the roadway against a “Don’t Walk” signal or suddenly step into traffic. You must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and whenever they are legally in the roadway, and you must use extra caution at all times to prevent a collision.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn continuously to get attention.,b:Pull off the road,c:Get out and flag down the first passing car.,d:Walk along the shoulder to find help immediately.
note: On an interstate, if you must stop in an emergency, pull completely off the roadway if possible, turn on your hazard lights, and stay in your vehicle if it is safe to do so. Walking along the shoulder or standing near moving traffic is very dangerous; wait for help inside the vehicle and call for assistance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should your vehicle end up?
options: a:In the left lane of the street you are entering.,b:In the right lane of the street.,c:In the center of the street.
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should turn into the lane closest to you that is going in your direction of travel. This is usually the left lane of the one-way street. Turning into the correct lane helps prevent conflicts with other vehicles and keeps traffic organized.

question: If you see one deer or moose cross the road, should you expect more?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Deer and moose often travel in groups or along the same path. If you see one animal cross, slow down and be prepared for others that may follow immediately behind or from the side. Staying alert and reducing speed in these areas greatly reduces your chance of a collision.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn they may:
options: a:Use the left lane or make a proper left-turn movement like a vehicle.,b:Cut through multiple lanes recklessly.,c:Always wait on the sidewalk.
note: Bicyclists generally have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. To make a left turn, a bicyclist may move into the appropriate left-turn lane and follow normal left-turn rules, or use other legal methods such as a two-stage turn where allowed. They should not cut recklessly across lanes or ride on the sidewalk unless local law permits it.

question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning in wet conditions is to:
options: a:Lower your speed.,b:Increase your speed to pass water quickly.,c:Use cruise control at a reduced speed.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water instead of gripping the road. The most effective way to reduce this risk is to slow down in wet conditions, especially where water may pool. Avoid sudden steering or braking, and do not use cruise control in heavy rain so you can respond quickly if your tires start to lose contact.

question: Which of the following does not promote safer night driving?
options: a:Rely solely on a flashlight to improve road vision.,b:Be aware that tinted windows reduce visibility in the dark.,c:Keep your windshield clean.
note: For safer night driving, you should keep your windshield clean and remember that tinted windows reduce visibility in the dark. You should never rely on a flashlight to see the road; your vehicle’s headlights and proper night‑driving techniques are what provide safe visibility.

question: The most common mistake drivers make when backing is failing to look both ways behind them.
options: a:False,b:True
note: When backing, many drivers make the mistake of not looking carefully in both directions behind the vehicle. Mirrors do not show everything; you must turn your head and look through the rear window while backing to be sure the path is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Remain in the left lane if you plan to turn left soon.,b:Stay in the left lane until the vehicle ahead signals you to move back.,c:Return to the right side of the roadway as soon as there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
note: On a two‑lane road, you may pass only when it is legal and safe. After passing, return to your lane as soon as there is a safe gap between you and the vehicle you passed, without cutting in too closely or lingering in the oncoming lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, you should position your vehicle:
options: a:To the left of the centerline into opposing traffic.,b:Near the centerline,c:On the right-hand side of the road.
note: When turning left from a two‑way street, position your vehicle in the lane closest to the centerline. This keeps you out of opposing traffic and sets you up to turn into the proper lane without cutting the corner or swinging wide.

question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only in front of the vehicle.,b:Only in back of your vehicle.,c:Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
note: A safe driver maintains a space cushion on all sides of the vehicle—front, rear, and both sides. This extra space gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake or if a hazard appears suddenly.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, what should you do?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed.,b:Speed up.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: Wet, snowy, or icy roads reduce traction, making it easier to skid. You should slow down and increase your following distance so you have more time and space to stop safely.

question: Is it legal to consume alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway?
options: a:No,b:Yes,c:You yes
note: Open container laws in all states make it illegal to drink alcohol or have an open alcoholic beverage in the passenger area of a vehicle on public roads. Neither the driver nor passengers may legally consume alcohol in a moving vehicle on a public highway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a stopped school bus displaying its stop arm, drivers should:
options: a:Assume children are done and pass slowly.,b:Honk before passing on the left,c:Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
note: When a school bus extends its stop arm and activates red lights, drivers in most situations must stop and remain stopped until the stop arm is retracted and the lights stop flashing. Children may cross unexpectedly, so you must not pass the bus during this time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into the farthest lane from your prior lane.,b:Into the rightmost lane regardless of position.,c:Into any lane you choose as long as it's clear.,d:Into the lane closest to your previous lane (the nearest lane).
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should turn into the nearest available lane going your direction, which is the lane closest to the lane you turned from. This keeps traffic organized and reduces the chance of collisions with vehicles in other lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Expect oncoming traffic and pedestrians to yield to you.,b:Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians in the crosswalk or roadway. Only turn when it is safe and the way is clear.

question: Signs that require drivers to obey an instruction are called what?
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Guide signs.,c:Regulatory signs.,d:Information signs.
note: Regulatory signs are the signs that tell you what you must do or must not do, such as STOP, speed limits, and NO TURN ON RED. These signs are legally enforceable, and failing to obey them can result in tickets or other penalties.

question: If your gas pedal becomes stuck, you should:
options: a:Turn off your headlights and continue driving.,b:Shift into neutral, then brake and steer to a safe place off the road.,c:Keep accelerating to escape danger.
note: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift the transmission into neutral to disconnect engine power from the wheels, and then apply the brakes to slow down while steering to a safe place off the road. Once stopped, turn off the engine and get help. Never turn the ignition to LOCK while moving, because it can lock the steering.

question: Excessive speed most often does what to driving behavior?
options: a:Does not increase the chance of a crash.,b:Increases your ability to react to a hazard.,c:Often leads to high-risk decision-making.
note: Driving too fast reduces the time you have to see and react to hazards and often leads drivers to follow too closely, make risky lane changes, or run lights. This high‑risk decision‑making greatly increases the chance and severity of crashes.

question: Which traffic signal indication requires you to come to a complete stop, yield, then proceed when clear?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A solid green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: you must come to a complete stop, yield to pedestrians and cross traffic, and then proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:
options: a:Overcorrect to regain control.,b:Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid.,c:Turn the wheel into oncoming traffic sharply.
note: When your vehicle begins to skid, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go, which is the same direction the rear of the vehicle is sliding. This helps you straighten the vehicle and regain control without overcorrecting.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:
options: a:Speed up to cross quickly before any gates lower.,b:Look and listen,c:Creep across without stopping if clear.,d:Drive around lowered gates if no train is visible.
note: Railroad crossings require extra caution. Slow down, look both ways, and listen for trains or warning signals. Be prepared to stop if a train is approaching or if gates or lights are activated. Never speed up to beat a train and never drive around lowered gates.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Keep driving normally.,b:Gradually slow down and pull off the roadway.,c:Slam on your brakes.
note: In a tire blowout, hold the steering wheel firmly, ease your foot off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Avoid slamming on the brakes, as that can cause loss of control. When your speed has dropped and the vehicle is stable, steer smoothly to the shoulder or a safe place off the road.

question: Is it wise to continually improve your driving and observation skills?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Continuously improving your driving and observation skills helps you spot hazards earlier, make better decisions, and reduce your risk of crashes. Safe drivers stay alert, practice defensive driving, and keep learning as traffic laws, vehicles, and road conditions change.

question: How should you check your blind spots when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Rely only on the inside rearview mirror.,b:Rely only on the outside rearview mirror.,c:Use your horn instead of looking.,d:Turn your head to glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.
note: Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle; areas not visible in your mirrors are called blind spots. Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and then quickly turn your head to glance over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to be sure the blind spot is clear.

question: When you see a person crossing with a white cane or guide dog, you should:
options: a:Stop until the person is well clear of your path.,b:Honk to alert them.,c:Carefully drive around them while they cross.
note: A person using a white cane or guide dog is visually impaired and has the right-of-way. You must stop and remain stopped until the pedestrian has completely crossed and is well clear of your vehicle. Do not honk or try to drive around them, as this can confuse or endanger the pedestrian.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn, which action is important?
options: a:Move into the left lane when it is safe and legal before reaching the intersection.,b:Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians and be prepared to yield.,c:Only use your rearview mirror to check behind you.
note: When preparing for a left turn, you must watch carefully for oncoming vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists, and be ready to yield to them. You should also signal, slow down, and move into the proper lane when it is safe, but constant observation of oncoming traffic and pedestrians is the key safety action.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a vehicle entering the interstate from an entrance ramp, what should you generally do?
options: a:Speed up to pass the merging vehicle.,b:Ignore them because you have the right-of-way.,c:Stop on the highway shoulder to let them in.,d:Make room by changing lanes or adjusting speed to allow them to merge.
note: On interstates, through traffic has the right-of-way, but safe driving practice is to help merging vehicles enter smoothly. When possible, change lanes away from the merging area or adjust your speed slightly so they have a safe gap to merge, while still maintaining control and obeying the speed limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into your driving lane?
options: a:After signaling for three seconds.,b:When the driver you passed signals you to return.,c:Immediately after completing the pass regardless of distance.,d:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your inside rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space ahead of that vehicle to return without cutting them off or forcing them to brake suddenly.

question: Do large vehicles have blind spots extending far behind them?
options: a:Only buses have large blind spots.,b:Only when they are towing a trailer.,c:False — large vehicles have smaller blind spots than cars.,d:True — large vehicles can have blind spots extending up to 200 feet behind them.
note: Large vehicles such as trucks and buses have large blind spots directly behind them that can extend a long distance, often up to 200 feet. If you follow too closely, the driver may not see you at all, so you should leave extra following distance and avoid lingering directly behind large vehicles.

question: What typically causes a vehicle to hydroplane?
options: a:Driving too fast for wet road conditions, causing tires to lose contact with the road.,b:Sudden braking on dry pavement.,c:Excessive stops during a trip.,d:A fully worn steering wheel.
note: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast for wet conditions and your tires ride up on a thin layer of water instead of gripping the road. This loss of contact reduces steering and braking control. Slowing down in rain and ensuring good tire tread greatly reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:
options: a:Drive at normal highway speeds when roads are wet.,b:Drive over puddles quickly to reduce time on water.,c:Use cruise control on wet roads.,d:Keep your tires properly maintained and reduce speed in wet conditions.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. The best prevention is to keep your tires properly inflated, have good tread, and slow down in wet conditions so your tires can channel water away. Avoid sudden steering or braking and reduce speed when roads are wet.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and the driver on your left arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.,b:You have the right-of-way.,c:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
note: At a four-way stop, when two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way. If the other driver is on your left, you are to their right, so you may proceed first after stopping and making sure it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light displays a red light and a green arrow for the same direction, can you turn in the arrow's direction?
options: a:True,b:False,c:Not enough information
note: A green arrow is a protected turn signal. When you have a green arrow, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow even if a steady red light is showing for that lane, but you must still yield to pedestrians and any traffic already in the intersection.

question: You should avoid using your horn:
options: a:When visibility ahead is limited.,b:If you might collide with another vehicle.,c:Near blind pedestrians.,d:To warn another driver who may not see you.
note: You should avoid using your horn around blind pedestrians because they rely heavily on sound to judge traffic. A sudden horn blast can be confusing or startling and make it harder for them to understand where vehicles are. Instead, slow down, be prepared to stop, and give them plenty of space.

question: If you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving it?
options: a:Not put much thought into it because all vehicles are the same.,b:Disregard defects to avoid embarrassing your friend.,c:Familiarize yourself with the vehicle's controls and correct any obvious defects before driving.
note: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, you should learn where and how the controls work—such as lights, turn signals, wipers, gear selector, parking brake, and seat and mirror adjustments—and make sure there are no obvious safety defects. Only drive the vehicle if it is in safe operating condition.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate highway, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop before entering the highway.,b:Select a safe gap and merge into the lane of traffic.,c:Merge across two lanes at once.
