note: On an interstate entrance ramp, use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge into a safe gap without stopping. Stopping on the ramp is dangerous because traffic behind you may not expect it and it makes merging harder.

question: When parking facing uphill on a road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels away from the edge of the road (to the left).,b:Keep the wheels facing straight ahead.,c:Turn the wheels so they point uphill.,d:Turn the wheels toward the edge of the road (to the right).
note: When parking uphill with no curb, turn the front wheels toward the right edge of the road. If the vehicle rolls, it will move away from the traffic lane and off the roadway instead of rolling into traffic.

question: What is the safest way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Speed up as you enter and slow down as you exit.,b:Maintain a constant speed throughout the curve.,c:Slow down as you enter and increase speed as you exit.
note: Before entering a curve, slow down so you can steer smoothly and keep traction. Once you are safely through the sharpest part of the curve and can see the road ahead, gently accelerate as you exit to return to normal speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it true that drivers are not required to yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Drivers must stop and yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks. You must also yield to pedestrians in unmarked crosswalks on your side of the roadway when there are no traffic-control signals.

question: A good driver should:
options: a:Focus only on the center of the road.,b:Stare only straight ahead.,c:Watch beside and ahead and check mirrors regularly.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan ahead, to the sides, and behind their vehicle. You should not stare straight ahead or focus only on the center of the road; instead, move your eyes regularly to check mirrors and the areas beside the road so you can spot hazards early.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition may you continue carefully through an intersection with a yellow light?
options: a:If the light turns red as you approach the intersection.,b:If a steady yellow light appears while you are already in the intersection,c:If an emergency vehicle is approaching from behind.,d:If pedestrians are crossing in front of you.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should continue through carefully and clear the intersection. If you have not yet entered, you must prepare to stop safely before the intersection unless it is unsafe to do so.

question: Is it lawful to drive at night using only your parking lights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Parking lights alone are not bright enough for safe night driving and do not make your vehicle clearly visible at normal driving speeds. Headlights are required between sunset and sunrise and any time visibility is poor, so it is unlawful and unsafe to drive at night using only parking lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Only where signs and pavement markings permit passing and you have enough space to do so safely.,b:Within intersections when no oncoming vehicles are visible.,c:On curves if you can see far ahead.,d:In all lanes of a multilane highway at any time.
note: Passing is only safe and legal where signs and pavement markings allow it and you have enough clear space to complete the pass without speeding or cutting off other drivers. Never pass in intersections, on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, or where your view is blocked.

question: If weather or lighting conditions require lights, which should you use?
options: a:Only parking lights.,b:Your low-beam headlights.,c:Your high-beam headlights.
note: In rain, fog, snow, or other reduced-visibility conditions, you should use low-beam headlights. High beams can reflect off moisture, fog, or snow in the air and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams help you see the road and help others see you without excessive glare.

question: In a vehicle with airbags, where should children age 12 and under ride?
options: a:On an adult's lap in the front seat.,b:In the front seat.,c:In the bed of a pickup truck.,d:In the back seat.
note: Airbags deploy with great force and can seriously injure young children. Children age 12 and under are safest when properly secured in the back seat, using an appropriate child safety seat or seat belt for their size and age, away from front airbags.

question: Before driving, you should remove snow, frost, and ice from which parts of your vehicle?
options: a:Only the windshield,b:Only the windshield and passenger window,c:All windows and mirrors
note: Before driving, clear snow, frost, and ice from all windows and mirrors so you can see in every direction. Limited visibility makes it harder to spot other vehicles, pedestrians, and hazards and can be considered unsafe or illegal in many states.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what should you do to check for traffic in your blind spot?
options: a:Rely on the rearview mirror.,b:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,c:Rely on the left side mirror.
note: Mirrors do not show areas in your blind spots. Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and then quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to be sure no vehicle is hidden beside you.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other traffic already in or entering the intersection.

question: Which combination provides the most effective protection in a crash?
options: a:An airbag alone.,b:Only a lap belt.,c:Both a properly worn lap-and-shoulder belt and a correctly functioning airbag.
note: The safest protection in a crash comes from using both a properly worn lap-and-shoulder belt and a working airbag. Airbags are designed to work with seat belts, not replace them, and you should always wear your belt even in vehicles with airbags.

question: You check your blind spots by:
options: a:Using the rearview mirror alone.,b:Only using side mirrors exclusively.,c:Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. To check them, briefly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move, in addition to using your mirrors and signals.

question: If another driver cuts you off, what is the safest reaction?
options: a:Flash your high beams at them.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Pull next to them and confront them.
note: If another driver cuts you off, the safest response is to stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and simply let them go. Slow slightly if needed to re‑establish a safe following distance and continue driving defensively. Reacting aggressively or confronting the other driver greatly increases the risk of a crash and road rage.

question: What are the colors of warning signs that indicate upcoming hazards?
options: a:Black on yellow background.,b:White on blue background.,c:Black on white background.
note: Warning signs that alert you to general hazards ahead are typically yellow with black symbols or lettering. Construction and maintenance warning signs are orange with black. These colors are standardized so drivers can quickly recognize potential dangers.

question: You may pass another vehicle when the dividing line is a ____ line.
options: a:Double solid yellow,b:Broken white,c:Solid yellow
note: You may pass another vehicle when there is a broken (dashed) line on your side of the road and it is safe to do so. Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and allow lane changes and passing when safe. Solid yellow lines generally prohibit passing across them.

question: How can you best avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Call a taxi only after you feel intoxicated.,b:Say 'No thanks,c:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.
note: The best way to avoid alcohol‑related crashes is to decide in advance that you will not drive if you drink. Plan a sober driver, use a taxi or rideshare, or avoid drinking when you must drive. Once you start drinking, your judgment is impaired and you may wrongly think you are still safe to drive.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:
options: a:May still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Have no right to turn and must proceed straight.,c:Retain the arrow's exclusive right-of-way.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn, meaning oncoming traffic is stopped. When the arrow goes out and a solid green light remains, you may still turn, but it becomes an unprotected turn. You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians and only turn when there is a safe gap.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:Railroad crossings.,c:School zones.
note: Crossbuck signs are white X-shaped signs that mark railroad crossings. They warn you that you are approaching train tracks and you must slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to yield or stop if a train is coming.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your turn or exit on a freeway, you should:
options: a:Make the turn quickly from your current lane.,b:Stop and back up on the freeway shoulder.,c:Continue driving until you reach the next exit or safe place to turn around.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway, you must never stop, swerve suddenly, or back up on the freeway or shoulder. Continue to the next exit or another safe place to turn around, then come back to your intended exit.

question: When you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, after setting the parking brake you should:
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Leave the wheels straight.
note: When parking facing uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will touch the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit represents what?
options: a:The suggested speed to travel under ideal conditions.,b:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel under dangerous conditions.,c:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel under ideal conditions.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum (and sometimes minimum) legal speed allowed under ideal conditions. You must reduce your speed below the posted limit when weather, traffic, or road conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

question: If you must park where vehicles are not usually parked, what should you ensure?
options: a:That you park five feet from the curb.,b:That your reverse lights are on while parked.,c:That your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.
note: If you must park where vehicles are not usually parked, make sure your vehicle can be clearly seen by drivers approaching from any direction. Use your hazard flashers if needed so your parked vehicle does not become a surprise hazard.

question: When must headlights be used?
options: a:Whenever visibility is reduced due to darkness, weather, or other conditions.,b:Between sunset and sunrise.,c:Only when the temperature drops below freezing.
note: Headlights must be used from sunset to sunrise and any time visibility is poor, such as in rain, fog, or snow. Using headlights helps other drivers see you and improves your own view of the road. Low beams should be used when following or approaching other vehicles to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: A bicyclist who disobeys traffic laws:
options: a:Must always ride on the sidewalk to avoid tickets.,b:Will always be warned but not ticketed.,c:Can be cited just like a motor vehicle driver.,d:Is exempt from traffic laws and cannot be ticketed.
note: Bicyclists on the roadway generally have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers of motor vehicles. They must obey traffic signals, signs, and lane markings, and they can be cited for violations such as running red lights or stop signs, just like drivers.

question: Stopping distances and crash severity tend to:
options: a:Decrease as a vehicle's speed increases.,b:Increase as vehicle speed increases.,c:Remain unchanged regardless of speed.
note: As speed increases, a vehicle needs more distance to stop because both reaction distance and braking distance grow with speed. Crashes at higher speeds also involve more force, which increases the severity of injuries and damage. This is why you should leave a larger following distance at higher speeds.

question: How close to a fire hydrant may you legally park?
options: a:No closer than 15 feet from the fire hydrant.,b:No closer than 10 feet from the fire hydrant.,c:No closer than five feet from the fire hydrant.
note: In many states, including those that follow common DMV guidelines, you may not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. This space must be kept clear so fire trucks can quickly connect hoses in an emergency. Always check local laws, but 15 feet is the standard distance used on most DMV exams.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate, what should you do on the entrance/acceleration lane?
options: a:Check traffic, accelerate to match the flow of traffic, and merge when safe.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large gap.,c:Reduce your speed to 25 mph before merging.
note: On an interstate entrance ramp, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of traffic, while checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling. Merge when there is a safe gap. Stopping on the ramp is dangerous because other drivers do not expect a stopped vehicle there.

question: What are potential effects of worn or bald tires?
options: a:They improve fuel economy.,b:They make hydroplaning less likely.,c:They can increase your stopping distance and make turning more difficult.
note: Tires with worn or bald tread cannot grip the road well. This increases your stopping distance, makes it harder to steer and turn, and greatly raises the risk of skidding or hydroplaning on wet roads.

question: When driving in extremely thick fog with very poor visibility, the safest action is to:
options: a:Pull off the roadway, stop, and use emergency flashers until visibility improves.,b:Proceed very slowly (under 10 mph) along the road.,c:Turn on high beams to see farther ahead.,d:Drive in the lane closest to the shoulder.
note: In extremely thick fog where you can barely see, it is safest to get completely off the roadway, turn on your emergency flashers, and wait until visibility improves. Continuing to drive, even very slowly or with high beams, can be extremely dangerous because other drivers may not see you in time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a ''Yield'' sign you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to crossing or merging traffic that is close enough to be a hazard.,b:Yield only to vehicles approaching from the right.,c:Always stop even if the way is clear.
note: At a yield sign you must slow down and be prepared to stop. You must let crossing or merging traffic and pedestrians go first if they are close enough to be a hazard. You only proceed when it is safe and you will not interfere with other road users.

question: If you start feeling tired while driving, you should:
options: a:Drink an energy drink and keep going.,b:Stop and rest or switch drivers.,c:Open a window for fresh air.
note: If you become fatigued, stop and rest or switch drivers to avoid the dangers of drowsy driving.

question: Which road is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?
options: a:A busy residential street.,b:A shaded area of the road.,c:A hilly road.
note: In cold weather after snow or rain, shaded areas of the road freeze first and thaw last. These spots can stay icy even when the rest of the road looks clear, so you should slow down and be especially cautious when driving through shaded sections.

question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:
options: a:Always signal your intention, even if no other traffic is visible.,b:Signal only if another vehicle is present.,c:Only signal when driving at night.,d:Only signal when turning left.
note: Always use your turn signal whenever you turn, change lanes, or pull away from the curb, even if you do not see other traffic. Signaling is required by law and gives other road users time to react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.,b:Stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.,c:Drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to get out of the way.
note: When entering a street from a driveway or alley, you must stop before the sidewalk or edge of the roadway and yield to pedestrians and all approaching traffic. Only proceed when it is safe and you will not force others to slow or change direction suddenly.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left.,b:Turn your wheels to the right.,c:Keep your wheels straight ahead.
note: When parking facing downhill on a two-way street, turn your front wheels toward the curb or road edge. If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will hit the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: Why should you allow extra space in front of a large truck?
options: a:So other drivers can merge in front of you.,b:Because trucks take longer to stop than passenger vehicles travelling at the same speed.,c:Becuase trucks always drive slower.,d:To give the truck driver room to change lanes quickly.
note: Large trucks are heavier and need a much longer distance to stop than passenger cars at the same speed. Leaving extra space in front of a truck gives the truck driver room to slow or stop safely and reduces your risk of being rear-ended.

question: Using cruise control on snowy or icy roads is:
options: a:Not safe and should be avoided.,b:Allowed if you have reduced your speed.,c:Recommended to maintain constant speed.
note: On snowy or icy roads, you should not use cruise control. Slippery surfaces require constant speed and steering adjustments, and cruise control can cause the wheels to spin or the vehicle to accelerate when traction is poor, leading to loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a flashing yellow traffic signal, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your speed to clear the intersection quickly.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop every time.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down, look for other traffic, and proceed through the intersection only when it is safe. It is a warning, not a stop signal, so you do not need to come to a complete stop unless needed for safety.

question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights, what should you do?
options: a:Briefly glance toward the right side of the road or edge of the lane.,b:Focus on the centerline until the car passes.,c:Flash your high beams to warn the other driver.
note: When oncoming headlights cause glare, briefly look toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road. This helps you stay in your lane using the road edge as a guide while avoiding being blinded by the bright lights.

question: A lack of sleep impairs driving ability in a way similar to which of the following?
options: a:The effect that amphetamines have.,b:The effect that anger has.,c:The effect that alcohol has.
note: Being very tired slows your reactions, reduces your alertness, and harms your judgment in a way similar to alcohol. Driving while drowsy can be as dangerous as driving after drinking, even if you have not consumed any alcohol.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Passing is allowed only on the right.,b:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Lanes move in the same direction only.,d:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and allows passing on the left when there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe. You must still check carefully and only pass when you have enough clear distance.

question: Which best describes defensive driving?
options: a:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,b:Getting ahead of poor drivers to avoid them.,c:Following the vehicle ahead at a close distance.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning for potential hazards, predicting what other road users might do, and adjusting your speed, position, and communication to avoid collisions before they happen.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Speed up to get through wet areas quickly.,b:Use parking lights instead of headlights.,c:Drive at reduced speeds on wet roads and maintain proper tire pressure and tread.,d:Drive with cruise control on wet roads.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water instead of gripping the road. You reduce this risk by slowing down on wet roads and making sure your tires have proper pressure and good tread depth so they can channel water away.

question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:
options: a:Keep a steady pace and stay there.,b:Stay in the blind spot until it is convenient to move.,c:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Staying in a blind spot is dangerous because the driver may change lanes or turn into your path. Either move ahead or drop back so you are clearly visible in their mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Proceed but yield to any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection.,b:Stop if a police officer is nearby.,c:Treat it as a four-way stop.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A steady green light means you may go if the intersection is clear, but you must always yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles already in the intersection. Never speed up just to beat the light, and always be prepared for it to change.

question: What color are traffic control devices used in construction and maintenance areas?
options: a:Red.,b:Orange.,c:Yellow.
note: Orange is the standard color for construction and maintenance work zones. Signs, cones, barrels, and barriers in orange warn you to slow down, be alert for workers and equipment, and be prepared for lane shifts or sudden stops.

question: When stopping on snow or ice in a vehicle equipped with ABS, what should you do?
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,b:Pump the brakes.,c:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.
note: With ABS on snow or ice, press and hold the brake pedal firmly and let the system work. ABS automatically pumps the brakes to prevent wheel lockup, helping you maintain steering control. Do not pump the brakes yourself in a vehicle equipped with ABS.

question: To check blind spots when changing lanes, drivers should:
options: a:Rely only on the left outside mirror.,b:Use the horn instead of looking.,c:Only use the inside rearview mirror.,d:Look over the appropriate shoulder (left or right) in addition to mirror checks.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly look over the shoulder on the side you’re moving toward to be sure no vehicle is hidden in your blind spot.

question: Is failure to report an accident that caused property damage of $1,000 or more a criminal offense?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Accidents causing more than $1,000 in property damage (or any injuries) must be reported to law enforcement; failure to report can lead to criminal penalties.

question: What do large flashing arrow panels in work zones indicate?
options: a:Drivers may remain in their current lane.,b:Drivers should merge in the direction of the arrow.,c:The arrow points to something to look at.
note: Large flashing arrow panels in work zones warn that a lane is closed ahead and show which direction you must move. Slow down, check traffic, and merge safely in the direction the arrow points.

question: With oncoming traffic to your left and parked vehicles to your right, what steering course should you take?
options: a:Steer a middle course between the oncoming vehicles and the parked vehicles.,b:Steer closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.,c:Steer closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.,d:Swerve back and forth to avoid both.
note: When you have oncoming traffic on one side and parked vehicles on the other, position your vehicle in the middle of the lane space between them. This gives you the greatest clearance from both hazards and reduces the risk of sideswiping or a head‑on collision.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Stop and wait until it turns green.,d:Yield only to pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield and stop if necessary for other vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.

question: If there is an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, you should:
options: a:Pass the bicyclist before the oncoming car arrives.,b:Pull onto the shoulder immediately.,c:Let the oncoming car pass first,d:Drive between them splitting the difference.
note: When you face hazards on both sides, deal with them one at a time. If a car is coming toward you and a bicyclist is on your right, slow down and let the oncoming car pass first. Once the lane is clear, you can move over safely to give the bicyclist extra space. Never try to squeeze between them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb:
options: a:Is necessary only if other traffic is present.,b:Is necessary only during the maneuver,c:Is a good driving habit and is required by law.
note: You must always signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from the curb, even if you think no one else is around. The signal must be given in advance—typically at least 100 feet before the maneuver in many states—so other road users have time to react.

question: Under normal conditions, what minimum following distance should you maintain?
options: a:One second.,b:Two seconds.,c:Three seconds.
note: Under normal conditions, use at least a two‑second following distance. Pick a fixed object ahead; when the vehicle in front passes it, you should be able to count at least “one‑thousand‑one, one‑thousand‑two” before you reach the same point. Increase this gap in bad weather, at higher speeds, or when following large vehicles.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, you should:
options: a:Avoid driving in the truck's blind spots and do not linger on its right side.,b:Remain farther back than you would behind a passenger car.,c:Stay closer than you would behind a passenger car.
note: Large trucks need more time and distance to stop and have large blind spots directly behind and along their sides. You should stay farther back than you would behind a passenger car so you can see the road ahead and have more time to react. Never follow a truck more closely than you would a car, and avoid lingering alongside it, especially on the right side.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection with a steady yellow light and have NOT entered the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and proceed.,b:Enter the intersection and then stop,c:Speed up to beat the red light.,d:Come to a safe stop before entering the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection, you should slow down and stop if you can do so safely before the stop line or crosswalk. Only continue through if you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals are out due to a power outage, drivers should:
options: a:Turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping.,b:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop,c:Park and wait until power is restored.,d:Follow the same rules as for a flashing yellow light.
note: When a traffic signal is completely dark due to a power outage, you must treat the intersection like a four‑way stop. Come to a complete stop, then proceed in the order of arrival, yielding to any vehicles already in the intersection and to pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If driving next to a single broken white line, you may:
options: a:Never cross the line to pass.,b:Only cross to change lanes if you are in the left lane.,c:Cross the line to pass or change lanes when safe.
note: A single broken (dashed) white line separates lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal, after checking mirrors, blind spots, and signaling.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving, you should:
options: a:Stop in your lane and leave hazard lights off.,b:Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road as soon as safely possible.,c:Signal and move into the slow lane and continue driving.,d:Continue driving at reduced speed until you reach a service area.
note: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem, turn on your hazard lights and carefully move off the roadway to the right shoulder or a safe area as soon as you can do so safely. Getting out of the traffic lane and warning other drivers reduces the risk of a collision.

question: How are bicycles on the road regarded under traffic laws?
options: a:They must always yield the right-of-way to motor vehicles.,b:They are considered vehicles and have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.,c:They do not follow specific rules of the road.
note: Bicycles on the road are treated as vehicles. Bicyclists generally must obey the same traffic signals, signs, and right‑of‑way rules as drivers, and they are entitled to use the lane. Motorists must yield to them when required and share the road safely.

question: What do two solid yellow lines painted on the pavement signify?
options: a:Passing is allowed if you are at the top of a hill.,b:Passing is not allowed.,c:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.
note: Two solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean no passing from either direction. You may not cross them to pass another vehicle, though in many states you may carefully cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe.

question: What do your brake lights tell other drivers?
options: a:You have your emergency brake on.,b:You are making a turn.,c:You are slowing down or stopping.
note: Brake lights warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping. This gives them time to reduce speed and maintain a safe following distance, helping prevent rear-end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway, you should be driving:
options: a:Well below the speed limit.,b:At any slow speed to wait for a gap.,c:At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
note: When using a freeway on-ramp, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed at or near the speed of traffic so you can merge smoothly and safely. Do not exceed the posted speed limit, even if other traffic is speeding.

question: Backing up a vehicle is:
options: a:Always risky and requires extra caution.,b:Safe if no helper is present.,c:Only dangerous in large vehicles.,d:Not dangerous when aided by mirrors alone.
note: Backing up is always higher risk because your view is limited and it is harder to see pedestrians, children, and obstacles. Move slowly, check all mirrors, look over your shoulder, and use a helper when needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must stop at an intersection when you see which signal?
options: a:A flashing green light.,b:A flashing red light.,c:A steady yellow light.,d:A yellow arrow.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas, steer parallel to the road, slow down, and then ease back onto the pavement when safe.,b:Stop quickly.,c:Accelerate and steer back onto the road quickly.
note: If your right wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm, ease off the gas, and keep steering straight and parallel to the road. Slow down gradually, then when the road is clear and your speed is under control, gently steer back onto the pavement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are you required to signal any time you pull away from a curb?
options: a:Yes — you must signal whenever you pull away from a curb.,b:No — signaling is optional when leaving a curb.,c:Only if another vehicle is present.,d:Only on multi-lane streets.
note: You must always signal before pulling away from a curb so other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know you are about to move into traffic. Signaling is required even if you do not see other vehicles, because someone may be approaching that you have not noticed.

question: Distracted drivers are at greater risk of a crash when using which device?
options: a:Radio.,b:CD player.,c:Cell phone.
note: Using a cell phone while driving is one of the most dangerous distractions because it takes your eyes, mind, and often a hand away from driving. Even hands‑free calls reduce your attention to the road and greatly increase your crash risk, so you should avoid using a phone while driving whenever possible.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:Never.,b:Only when pulling to or from a curb.,c:When changing lanes or making any lateral move such as merging or turning.
note: Before changing lanes, merging, or making any sideways movement, you must quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Mirrors do not show the entire area next to and behind your vehicle, so a shoulder check helps you see vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles that might be hidden from your mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is required for safe interstate driving?
options: a:No special skills beyond local driving.,b:Only the ability to drive fast,c:Both the ability to safely drive at increased speeds and constant alertness.,d:Only constant alertness while driving slowly.
note: Safe interstate driving requires being comfortable at higher, steady speeds and staying constantly alert to traffic, signs, and road conditions. You must be able to adjust speed smoothly, maintain safe following distances, and scan far ahead because situations develop more quickly on high‑speed roads.

question: Many crashes are caused by:
options: a:Drivers yielding the right-of-way.,b:Drivers going too fast for conditions.,c:Drivers frequently checking mirrors and blind spots.
note: Driving too fast for conditions is a major cause of crashes. Even if you are below the posted speed limit, you must slow down when roads are wet, icy, congested, or visibility is poor. Adjusting your speed to match traffic, weather, and road conditions gives you more time and space to react safely.

question: When must you obey instructions from a school crossing guard?
options: a:Only during school hours.,b:Only if you see children present.,c:At all times.
note: You must obey a school crossing guard’s instructions whenever they are on duty directing traffic or pedestrians, regardless of the time of day or whether you see children. Their directions have the same legal authority as traffic control devices while they are performing their duties.

question: What is the meaning of a diamond-shaped traffic sign?
options: a:Regulatory — you must follow it.,b:Warning — special conditions or hazards ahead.,c:Stop required ahead.,d:Information — services ahead.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to special conditions or hazards ahead, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or work zones, so you can slow down and be prepared.

question: Continuous hard braking on ice and snow often:
options: a:Helps you stop faster.,b:Prevents the brakes from freezing.,c:Locks the front wheels and causes loss of steering.
note: On ice and snow, hard continuous braking can cause your wheels to lock, which makes you lose steering control and can lead to a skid. Instead, slow down early and brake gently; if you have ABS, press firmly and let the system work, and if you don’t, use light, repeated braking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed on both sides while driving in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the left lane regardless of traffic.,b:Remain in the center lane and maintain speed.,c:Speed up to prevent others from passing.,d:Move to the lane on your right if it is safe to do so.
note: On multi-lane highways, the right lane is for through driving, and left lanes are mainly for passing. If you are in the center lane and vehicles are passing you on both sides, you are likely going slower than the flow of traffic; when safe, move to the lane on your right so faster traffic can pass on the left.

question: Large trucks are likely to lose speed under which condition?
options: a:When driving down long hills.,b:When driving in long traffic jams.,c:When driving up long or steep hills.
note: Large trucks are very heavy, so they often slow down when climbing long or steep hills. Their engines must work harder against gravity, which reduces their speed. When approaching a hill behind a truck, be prepared for it to lose speed and give it extra space to avoid sudden braking.

question: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, when may vehicles behind the bus proceed?
options: a:When all students are off the bus.,b:When the children wave to you.,c:When the stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.
note: Motorists must remain stopped until the bus turns off its red lights, retracts the stop arm, and begins moving again.

question: A double yellow centerline painted down the road means passing is:
options: a:Not allowed from either direction.,b:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Allowed from both directions.
note: A solid double yellow centerline means traffic on both sides of the line must stay in their lane and is not allowed to pass. The lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and indicate that passing is unsafe due to limited visibility or other hazards.

question: Which color lines separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Red,b:Yellow,c:Black
note: Yellow lines are used to separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. Red and black are not used in the U.S. to separate opposing traffic lanes.

question: A leaking exhaust system can cause you to become:
options: a:To use more oil.,b:Drowsy while driving.,c:To need a tune-up sooner.
note: A leaking exhaust system can let carbon monoxide enter the vehicle’s interior. Carbon monoxide is colorless and odorless and can cause headache, dizziness, and drowsiness, which can lead to loss of consciousness and even death. This makes driving extremely dangerous.

question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug and also drink alcohol?
options: a:It can make you unfit to drive and increase impairment.,b:It will make you more alert.,c:There will likely be no effect.
note: Alcohol can interact with prescription and over‑the‑counter drugs to greatly increase impairment. The combination can make you very drowsy, slow your reactions, affect judgment, and make you unfit to drive, even if each substance alone might not seem very strong.

question: Which of the following will help someone sober up after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Drinking coffee and getting fresh air.,b:Nothing but the passage of time will reduce impairment.,c:Taking a cold shower and drinking tomato juice.
note: Only time reduces alcohol impairment. The liver can process only a limited amount of alcohol per hour, and no amount of coffee, fresh air, showers, or food will speed this up. A person may feel more awake, but their judgment, reaction time, and coordination remain impaired until enough time has passed.

question: When making a turn, what should you do with your speed?
options: a:Reduce your speed to maintain control of the vehicle.,b:Increase your speed to make a quicker turn.,c:Maintain highway speed.,d:Come to a complete stop every time before turning.
note: Before and during a turn, you should slow to a safe speed so you can stay in your lane and maintain full control of the vehicle. Enter the turn at a controlled speed, then gently accelerate as you complete it. Turning too fast can cause skidding, drifting out of your lane, or losing control.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, the best course of action is to:
options: a:Turn up the radio volume to stay alert.,b:Stop driving and rest.,c:Drink coffee and continue driving.,d:Open a window and keep driving.
note: If you feel tired while driving, the safest action is to stop driving and rest. Fatigue slows reaction time and harms judgment much like alcohol. Tricks such as loud music, open windows, or caffeine may briefly make you feel more awake but do not restore safe driving ability when you are truly drowsy.

question: Must drivers stop when a school bus is using its flashing red lights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, drivers in the same direction must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the arm is withdrawn. On a divided highway with a physical median or barrier, oncoming traffic usually does not have to stop, but should use extra caution and be prepared for children near the roadway.

question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means what?
options: a:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,b:Passing is permitted from both directions.,c:Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.
note: A dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side of the dashed line. Drivers on the side of the solid yellow line must not cross it to pass. Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, so this rule controls which direction may legally pass.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how should your following distance compare to that behind a passenger vehicle?
options: a:No more than one car length behind the truck.,b:Closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.,c:Farther behind the truck than you would when following a passenger vehicle.
note: When following large trucks, you should leave more space than you would behind a passenger car. Trucks take longer to stop and have large blind spots directly behind them. A greater following distance gives you more time to react and helps keep you visible in the truck’s mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, what should a driver do?
options: a:Yield to traffic already in the intersection and to vehicles on your right if you arrive at the same time.,b:Slow, look carefully in all directions, and be prepared to yield; proceed when safe.,c:Maintain your speed and proceed without checking.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), you are not required to stop every time, but you must slow down, scan left and right, and be prepared to yield. Yield to any vehicle already in the intersection and to vehicles on your right if you arrive at the same time. Proceed only when it is clear and safe.

question: How does increasing your vehicle's speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It decreases your field of vision as speed increases.,b:It increases your field of vision.,c:It makes it easier to see cross traffic.,d:It has no effect.
note: As your speed increases, your side vision (peripheral vision) narrows and you see less to the sides of the road. This reduced field of vision makes it easier to miss hazards such as pedestrians, cyclists, or cross traffic, so higher speeds require extra attention and longer following distances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: With a solid yellow line on one side and a broken yellow on your side, when may you pass?
options: a:Only on expressways.,b:You may pass if the way ahead is clear.,c:Only in an emergency.
note: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. When the broken yellow line is on your side and the solid line is on the other side, you may cross the broken line to pass if the lane is clear and there is no oncoming traffic. Never pass if your side has the solid yellow line.

question: Before changing lanes, what is the correct sequence of checks and signals?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder, then change lanes when safe.,b:Signal only if you see a vehicle nearby.,c:Check mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, signal, and then change lanes when safe.
note: Before changing lanes, first check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, then quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot in the direction of the lane change. If it is clear, signal to let others know your intention, and then change lanes smoothly when safe.

question: Which statement about passing motorcycles is true?
options: a:Motorcycles with two riders are always more stable than with one.,b:You must move completely into the adjacent lane when passing a motorcycle.,c:You can pass a motorcycle without changing lanes.,d:Other vehicles may follow motorcycles closely.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like cars. When you pass a motorcycle, you must move completely into the adjacent lane and pass as you would another vehicle, leaving plenty of space. Never try to squeeze by in the same lane or follow a motorcycle too closely, because they can stop and maneuver more quickly than larger vehicles.

question: Where is it appropriate to use high beam headlights?
options: a:Where pedestrians may be present and no other vehicles are near.,b:Only on familiar roads.,c:In construction areas where no nearby vehicles are present.
note: High beam headlights should be used when you need extra visibility and there are no oncoming vehicles or vehicles close ahead of you, such as on dark rural roads or where pedestrians may be present along the roadside. You must dim your high beams when you are within about 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or about 300 feet when following another vehicle, so you do not blind other drivers.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around or under a moving railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Only if your vehicle can clear it without damage.,b:If you look both ways first and see no trains.,c:No—never drive around or under a lowering or lowered gate.
note: It is never acceptable to drive around, under, or through a lowering or lowered railroad crossing gate. Trains are much faster and closer than they may appear, and they cannot stop quickly. You must wait until the lights stop flashing, bells stop ringing, and the gates are fully raised before crossing the tracks.

question: If a child appears likely to run into the street in front of your vehicle, what should you do immediately?
options: a:Flash your headlights.,b:Sound a sharp blast of your horn and be ready to brake.,c:Start to prepare to slow down.
note: If a child looks like they may run into the street, you should immediately sound a sharp blast of your horn to get their attention and warn them of danger, while also being ready to brake hard. Children are unpredictable and may not see or hear your vehicle, so giving a clear audible warning and slowing or stopping is critical to prevent a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these statements about changing lanes is correct?
options: a:Vehicles with two outside mirrors do not have blind spots.,b:Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.,c:You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder for lane changes to the right or left.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots, even if it has multiple mirrors. Before changing lanes, always signal, check your mirrors, and then look over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter. This quick head check lets you see the blind spot that mirrors cannot cover and helps you avoid vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles that may be alongside you.

question: Large vehicles generally have:
options: a:Smaller blind spots due to higher seating.,b:No blind spots at all.,c:Larger blind spots than smaller vehicles.
note: Bigger vehicles like trucks and buses have larger blind spots, especially close to their rear and sides.

question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days for what reason?
options: a:To keep your engine warm.,b:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,c:So others can see your vehicle.
note: If weather conditions reduce visibility, turning on your low beam headlights makes your vehicle easier for others to see; in Maine, if wipers are required, headlights must be on.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To change lanes safely, what sequence should you use?
options: a:Signal, then move,b:Use turn indicator only,c:Signal, check mirrors, check blind spot, then change lanes
note: To change lanes safely, first turn on your signal to show others what you plan to do, then check your mirrors and quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only move into the new lane when you are sure it is clear and safe.

question: Are drivers always required to stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road?
options: a:Drivers only need to slow down for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road.,b:FALSE – you do not always have to stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road.,c:TRUE – on a two-lane road, drivers in both directions must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm.
note: On a two-lane road, drivers in both directions must stop when a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, because children may be crossing the road from either side.

question: What does an ''End school zone'' sign indicate?
options: a:The beginning of a reduced speed zone.,b:The speed limit is 20 mph at all times.,c:The end of a reduced school speed zone.
note: An 'End school zone' sign marks the end of the reduced school speed zone; observe posted speed limits outside the zone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a railroad crossing without electric warning devices, you should:
options: a:Drive through without stopping if no train is visible.,b:Slow down, look, and be prepared to stop before crossing.,c:Speed up and cross quickly.
note: At a railroad crossing without gates or flashing lights, you must slow down, look and listen carefully for trains, and be prepared to stop. Only proceed when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to fully clear the tracks. Never speed up to beat a train.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver's left arm extended upward indicates they plan to:
options: a:Stop.,b:Turn left.,c:Turn right.
note: A driver’s left arm extended straight out indicates a left turn. A left arm bent upward at the elbow (hand pointing up) is the signal for a right turn. A left arm bent downward is the signal for slowing or stopping.

question: Before backing out of your driveway and with children nearby you should:
options: a:Rev your engine to warn them.,b:Walk to the rear of your vehicle to ensure the way is clear.,c:Sound your horn only.
note: When children are nearby, always walk behind your vehicle to check for them or any obstacles before backing. Mirrors and cameras can miss small children, so physically looking behind the vehicle is the safest practice.

question: What do double solid yellow lane markings indicate?
options: a:Both lanes may pass.,b:Neither lane may pass.,c:The lane to the right may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that passing is not allowed for vehicles in either direction. You may cross them only when turning left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than:
options: a:The posted maximum speed limit only.,b:What feels comfortable for you.,c:What is reasonable and prudent given conditions
note: You must always drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for current conditions, even if that means driving below the posted speed limit. Factors include weather, traffic, road surface, and visibility, and you must also stay within the legal speed limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:
options: a:Assume the guard shouldn't be directing traffic.,b:Copy what other drivers do even if it contradicts the guard.,c:Follow the crossing guard's directions.
note: In a school zone, you must obey the crossing guard’s directions, even if they differ from traffic signals or what other drivers are doing. Crossing guards help protect children and manage traffic safely, so always follow their signals and proceed with extra caution.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line indicates:
options: a:Passing is not allowed in either direction.,b:Both directions may pass.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line but not from the lane next to the solid line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line and prohibited from the side with the solid line. Always pass only when you have enough clear distance and it is safe and legal to do so.

question: Which statement best completes the sentence: ''____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory''?
options: a:Alcohol does not,b:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can,c:Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can
note: Even small amounts of alcohol can reduce your concentration, slow your perception, and impair your judgment and memory. Impairment begins well before you reach the legal limit, which is why you should never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

question: A person using a white cane or a guide dog is most likely to be:
options: a:A person involved in a traffic study.,b:A deaf person.,c:A blind or visually impaired person.
note: A white cane or a guide dog identifies a pedestrian who is blind or visually impaired. Drivers must always yield the right‑of‑way, stop well before the crosswalk, and use extra caution to ensure these pedestrians can cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign, what sequence should you use to check for cross traffic before entering the intersection?
options: a:Move when the vehicle ahead moves only after you have checked for cross traffic.,b:Look left, then right, then left again before entering the intersection.,c:Check your rearview mirror for tailgaters, then scan left and right for cross traffic.
note: At a stop sign, after stopping completely, you should first look left, because that is where the nearest cross traffic comes from on a typical two‑way road. Then look right, then left again before entering the intersection. This left‑right‑left pattern helps you spot approaching vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists in time to avoid a collision.

question: What should you do before driving if you are taking any medicine?
options: a:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about how it may affect your driving.,b:Have someone follow you home, even if medication is fine.,c:Open your windows and drive slower.,d:Double the dose to speed up recovery.
note: Both prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines can make you drowsy, dizzy, or slow your reactions. Before driving, ask your doctor or pharmacist whether the medicine can affect your ability to drive safely, and follow their advice.

question: When changing lanes, you should look for a gap of about:
options: a:About four seconds,b:About one to two seconds,c:About three seconds,d:Less than one second
note: When changing lanes at typical highway speeds, you need a gap of about four seconds between you and vehicles in the new lane. A four‑second gap gives you time to signal, move over smoothly, and maintain a safe following distance in case traffic ahead slows or stops.

question: To safely pass a bicyclist you should:
options: a:Drive in the bicycle lane until you complete the pass.,b:Honk close to the bicyclist so they know you are there.,c:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible, leaving at least several feet of clearance.,d:Pass as quickly as possible even if you are very close to the bicyclist.
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and move over to give them plenty of space—at least three feet, and more when possible. Never drive in the bicycle lane to pass, and avoid honking close to the bicyclist because it can startle them and cause a loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, which of the following actions should you perform?
options: a:Signal and move into the next lane without checking mirrors or blind spots.,b:Check only your rearview and outside mirrors before moving.,c:Signal, check your mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.,d:Change lanes quickly without signaling if traffic seems light.
note: Before changing lanes, you should signal, check your mirrors, and then quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This over‑the‑shoulder check is essential because mirrors do not show vehicles in the blind spot next to your car.

question: Alcohol in any concentration is classified as:
options: a:A stimulant.,b:A depressant.,c:Neither of the above.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant. It slows brain and body functions, reducing judgment, coordination, and reaction time. Even small amounts of alcohol can impair driving ability and increase crash risk.

question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Stop,b:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,c:Yield to all traffic before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not need to stop, but you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with extra caution, being prepared to yield if necessary.

question: If a large vehicle is overtaking you, you should:
options: a:Maintain your speed or slow down slightly.,b:Speed up to prevent it from passing.,c:Immediately move into the left lane without signaling.
note: When a large vehicle is passing you, keep a steady speed or slow slightly so it can pass safely. Never speed up, because that increases risk and lengthens the time you are side‑by‑side in the blind spots of the larger vehicle.

question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may proceed in the arrow's direction if:
options: a:You first come to a complete stop.,b:You wait until the light changes to solid green.,c:You are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.
note: A green arrow is a protected turn signal that allows you to move only in the arrow’s direction, from the proper lane, after checking that the roadway is clear of vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,b:Stop only if other cars are approaching.,c:Come to a full stop, then proceed when it is safe to do so.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign: you must come to a complete stop, then yield to any traffic or pedestrians in or close to the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Distracted driving typically:
options: a:Is never dangerous.,b:Helps drivers respond faster.,c:Causes slower reactions to hazards.
note: Distractions such as phone use, eating, or adjusting controls take your attention away from driving and usually slow your reaction time, making it harder to notice and respond to hazards in time.

question: As you near the top of a hill, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Maintain a steady speed.,b:Speed up slightly.,c:Prepare to stop if necessary.
note: As you approach the top of a hill, you cannot see what is on the other side. There may be a stopped vehicle, an animal, a slow-moving bicycle, or debris in the road. You should reduce speed as needed and be prepared to stop suddenly if necessary.

question: A sign reading “Reduced speed, 35 mph” means:
options: a:The previous speed limit still applies until the next sign.,b:You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced zone.,c:The reduced 35 mph speed limit begins at that sign.,d:The reduced speed begins at the next sign.
note: A sign that says “Reduced speed, 35 mph” means the new 35 mph speed limit starts at the sign. You must have already slowed to that speed by the time you reach the sign, and you must not exceed 35 mph beyond that point unless another sign indicates a different limit.

question: Alcohol affects your driving by:
options: a:Improving driving skills while harming judgment.,b:Harming both driving skills and judgment.,c:Having no effect on either.
note: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces coordination, affects vision, and harms judgment. This combination makes it harder to control the vehicle and to make safe decisions, greatly increasing the risk of a crash.

question: Which headlight setting should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:No lights at all.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.,d:High beam headlights.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and create glare, which makes it harder to see. Low beams help you see the road and help other drivers see you without causing extra glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two drivers reach a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right.,b:Either driver may proceed without stopping.,c:The driver on the left.
note: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. You should wait and allow the vehicle on your right to go first, then proceed when it is your turn and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady yellow traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Ignore it because they have right-of-way.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection.,c:Slow to a stop unless already in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must prepare to stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection or too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, what checks should you perform first?
options: a:Honk your horn at least three times.,b:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.,c:Check your mirrors and blind spots.
note: Before passing, check your mirrors and quickly glance over your shoulder to check blind spots, then signal and move into the passing lane only when it is safe. Never rely on horn use or an arbitrary distance; you must have clear space and time to pass and return safely.

question: Airbags provide complete protection in a crash. Is this true or false?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Airbags are designed to work together with seat belts, mainly in moderate to severe frontal crashes. They do not protect you in all types of crashes and cannot keep you properly positioned by themselves, so you must always wear a seat belt for full protection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road, what must you judge before pulling out?
options: a:Flash your headlights as you pass.,b:Sound your horn as you pass.,c:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, you must be sure you have enough time and space to complete the pass safely. Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles and make sure the lane is clear far enough ahead before pulling out to pass.

question: Which of the following is a dangerous habit in work zones?
options: a:Tailgating another vehicle.,b:Failing to carefully watch for workers and moving equipment.,c:Both of the above.
note: Work zones require extra caution. Following too closely reduces your time to react to sudden stops, and not watching carefully for workers and equipment can lead to serious crashes. Both tailgating and inattention are dangerous in work zones.

question: Tailgating (following too closely) can:
options: a:Reduce collisions by preventing others from cutting in.,b:Improve traffic flow in congested areas.,c:Never result in a traffic citation.,d:Provoke and frustrate other drivers and can lead to citations.
note: Tailgating is unsafe and often illegal. Following too closely increases the risk of rear-end collisions, can anger or provoke other drivers, and can result in a traffic citation for following too closely. You should always leave enough space to stop safely if the vehicle ahead brakes suddenly.

question: What does an arrow painted in a traffic lane on the pavement require drivers to do?
options: a:Drivers must come to a complete stop before following the arrow.,b:Drivers in that lane may choose to ignore the arrow.,c:The arrow applies only when traffic signals are not functioning.,d:Drivers in that lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow.
note: Lane-use arrows painted on the pavement tell you what movement you must make from that lane, such as turning left, turning right, or going straight. When you are in a lane with a directional arrow, you are required to follow the arrow’s direction unless a traffic sign or signal clearly allows a different movement.

question: If a vehicle has airbags, what about seat belts?
options: a:Seat belts should still be worn.,b:Seat belts are unnecessary.,c:Seat belts only needed in the back seats.
note: Airbags are designed to work together with seat belts, not replace them. Seat belts keep you properly positioned so the airbag can protect you and reduce the chance of being thrown from the vehicle. Everyone should wear a seat belt, in both front and rear seats, even in vehicles equipped with airbags.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers allow for?
options: a:The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,b:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.
note: Large trucks and other heavy vehicles need more distance to stop because of their size and weight. When driving near trucks, avoid cutting in front of them, don’t brake suddenly, and leave extra space so the truck has enough room to slow or stop safely.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal require of a driver?
options: a:Come to a complete stop at the intersection.,b:Maintain your normal speed.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you must slow down and proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you should be prepared to yield and watch carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards in or entering the intersection.

question: Should you use high beams when driving in fog?
options: a:Use parking lights only.,b:Yes — high beams improve visibility.,c:Alternate high and low beams frequently.,d:No — use low beams in fog.
note: High beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility; low beams are the correct choice when driving in fog.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck, what should you do?
options: a:Obey a flagger’s instructions if present.,b:Turn your radio down to hear an approaching train.,c:Approach with caution, be prepared to stop, and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
note: At a railroad crossing controlled only by a crossbuck (no lights or gates), you must slow, look, and listen for trains in both directions and be prepared to stop. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely. If a flagger is present at any crossing, you must obey their instructions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a left-turn lane to turn, what should you do as you approach the intersection with oncoming traffic?
options: a:Turn your front wheels to the left while waiting to turn.,b:Signal about 100 feet before the turn and keep your front wheels straight until you begin the turn.,c:Move to the far left of your lane but stay within the lane markings.
note: When preparing for a left turn, signal in advance (about 100 feet in most areas) to alert other drivers, and keep your front wheels pointed straight while waiting. If another vehicle hits you from behind while your wheels are turned, your car could be pushed into oncoming traffic. Keeping the wheels straight helps prevent this and keeps you in your lane until you actually begin the turn.

question: If you see other drivers acting angrily, you should:
options: a:Put distance between yourself and them and avoid engaging.,b:Make eye contact to calm them down.,c:Respond with hand gestures.,d:Drive faster to get away immediately.
note: Physically and mentally distance yourself from angry drivers to reduce risk of conflict.

question: What should you remember when driving on wet pavement?
options: a:Wet roads always improve traction.,b:You can stop in the same distance as on dry roads.,c:Roads can be especially slippery right after rain begins.
note: Wet roads are most slippery when rain first mixes with oils on the pavement. Slow down, increase following distance, and be cautious of hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle when:
options: a:All of the above,b:Facing a red traffic signal.,c:Approaching an intersection with a stop sign.,d:Where a traffic officer orders you to stop.
note: You must come to a complete stop at a red traffic signal, at a stop sign, and any time a traffic officer directs you to stop. These are all mandatory stopping situations, so each listed condition requires you to stop your vehicle.

question: What is the only effective way to reduce your BAC?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Exercise.,c:Allow your body time to eliminate the alcohol.
note: Only time allows your body to process and eliminate alcohol. Coffee, exercise, cold showers, or other tricks may make you feel more awake, but they do not lower your blood alcohol concentration or make you safer to drive.

question: Drivers must keep a safe distance when near a cyclist.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Drivers must always give cyclists extra space and avoid driving too close to them. Keeping a safe distance when following or passing a bicyclist helps prevent sideswipe collisions and gives the cyclist room to avoid hazards.

question: In very heavy fog you should slow down and:
options: a:Turn on your low beam headlights.,b:Turn on high beams to see further.,c:Turn on emergency flashers only.
note: In heavy fog, slow down and use low beam headlights or fog lights. High beams reflect off the fog and can make it harder to see, while low beams help you see the road and help others see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a railroad crossing warning sign you should:
options: a:Look for ways around any lowered gates.,b:Try to drive faster than the train to clear the tracks.,c:Be prepared to stop if a train is near.
note: A railroad crossing warning sign means you are approaching train tracks. Slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching or if warning devices are activated.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down gradually and gently steer back onto the pavement when safe.,b:Stop on the edge of the road immediately.,c:Brake hard and sharply steer back onto the pavement.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, ease off the accelerator and slow down gradually while keeping the vehicle straight. Do not brake hard or jerk the wheel. Once you have reduced speed and checked for traffic, gently steer back onto the pavement.

question: Collisions are most likely to occur when:
options: a:All vehicles travel at about the same speed.,b:One vehicle is traveling significantly faster or slower than the flow of traffic.,c:One lane of traffic is traveling faster than other lanes.
note: Crashes are more likely when one vehicle is moving much faster or much slower than surrounding traffic, because it increases lane changes, surprises other drivers, and reduces the time others have to react. Traveling at a speed similar to the flow of traffic, while staying within the speed limit, is generally safer.

question: What does a pentagon-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:School zone or school crossing.,b:Stop sign.,c:Regulatory sign.
note: A pentagon-shaped sign is used for school zones and school crossings. It warns drivers to slow down, watch for children, and be prepared to stop for pedestrians in or near the roadway.

question: Where should your hands be placed on the steering wheel when driving normally?
options: a:At the 1 and 11 o'clock positions.,b:One hand at the top of the wheel.,c:At the 2 and 10 o'clock positions on the wheel.,d:At the 3 and 9 o'clock positions.
note: Most modern driver manuals recommend placing your hands at the 9 and 3 o'clock positions. This gives you better control of the vehicle and reduces the risk of injury from an airbag deployment compared with the older 10 and 2 o'clock recommendation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A U-turn is prohibited:
options: a:On a straight road with a clear 500-foot view.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:In a parking lot.
note: You must not make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot be seen by other drivers approaching from either direction. Limited visibility means oncoming traffic may not have enough time or distance to react, creating a serious collision risk.

question: Alcohol affects drivers by:
options: a:Slowing reaction time, impairing thinking, and giving false confidence.,b:Speeding reaction time up safely.,c:Improving coordination and vision.,d:Having no effect if you feel sober.
note: Alcohol slows your reactions, harms your judgment, and reduces coordination, even if you feel fine. It can also make you overconfident, so you take risks you normally would avoid. Because of this, any amount of alcohol can make driving unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct method for making a right turn?
options: a:Approach in the right lane and position your vehicle as close as practical to the right curb or edge before turning.,b:Approach in the right lane but move toward the middle of the street before turning.,c:Signal and slow down, keeping close to the right curb or edge before turning.,d:Speed up and turn without signaling.
note: To make a safe right turn, you should signal well in advance, slow down, and keep your vehicle as close as practical to the right curb or edge of the roadway before and during the turn. You should not swing wide toward the middle of the street, because that can confuse other drivers and increase the risk of a collision.

question: Having a driver license is considered a:
options: a:Right.,b:Requirement.,c:Privilege.
note: A driver license is a privilege, not a right. The state grants you permission to drive if you meet certain requirements, and that privilege can be suspended or revoked if you break traffic laws or drive unsafely.

question: If you see or hear an approaching emergency vehicle while driving on a divided multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Stop immediately in your lane, even if it may cause a rear-end collision.,b:Continue driving normally if there are other lanes open for the emergency vehicle.,c:Safely move to the right, slow down, and stop if necessary to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.,d:Speed up to get out of the way as quickly as possible.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren on, you must yield the right-of-way. On a divided multilane highway, safely move to the right side of your lane or roadway, slow down, and stop if necessary so the emergency vehicle has a clear path. Never stop suddenly in your lane if it would cause a rear-end collision, and never ignore an emergency vehicle just because it has other lanes available.

question: In which situations is it important to slow down?
options: a:At intersections or railroad crossings.,b:All of the above.,c:On narrow or winding roads.,d:When the road is wet or slippery.
note: You should slow down whenever conditions increase risk: at intersections and railroad crossings, on narrow or winding roads, on hills, and when the road is wet, icy, or otherwise slippery. Reduced speed gives you more time to react and a shorter stopping distance in these higher-risk situations.

question: Which of the following about blind spots is true?
options: a:They can be checked only with rearview mirrors.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:They are removed if you have one outside mirror on each side.
