note: Mirrors, even when properly adjusted, do not eliminate blind spots. You must still turn your head to check areas your mirrors cannot show. Large trucks have much larger blind spots, often called no‑zones, along the sides, front, and rear of the vehicle. Drivers should avoid lingering in these areas because the truck driver may not see them.

question: When are roads most likely to be very slippery after rain begins?
options: a:The day after it rains.,b:For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.,c:After it has been raining steadily for several hours.
note: Roads are especially slippery during the first 10–15 minutes of a rainstorm. Oil and residue on the road surface mix with the water and rise to the top, reducing traction. After it has rained steadily for a while, much of this oil is washed away and the road surface usually becomes less slippery, though you should still drive with caution.

question: Which of the following helps you drive more safely at night?
options: a:Drive only with parking lights on.,b:Ignore headlights and keep using high beams.,c:Increase your following distance to allow more reaction time.,d:Depend on interior lights to see controls.
note: At night, you cannot see as far ahead, so you need more time to react. Increasing your following distance gives you extra space to respond to hazards. You should also use your low beams when following or meeting other vehicles and make sure your headlights and windshield are clean for best visibility.

question: If someone is injured in an accident, what should you do?
options: a:Not move the injured unless necessary; keep them warm and provide first aid if qualified.,b:Move the injured immediately away from the scene at all costs.,c:Leave the injured where they are and drive to get help.
note: If someone is injured in a crash, do not move them unless there is immediate danger, such as fire or risk of another collision. Moving an injured person can worsen neck, back, or internal injuries. Keep the person warm, reassure them, provide first aid only if you are trained, and call 911 or emergency services right away.

question: To reduce headlight glare from oncoming vehicles at night, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:Straight ahead.,b:Over your shoulder.,c:Toward the right side of the road ahead.
note: When you are bothered by the glare of oncoming headlights at night, look toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road. This helps you avoid being blinded while still using the lane markings or road edge as a guide to stay in your lane.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?
options: a:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,b:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.,c:Any prescription is safe to use while driving.
note: Even legal medications can affect your driving. Many prescription and over‑the‑counter drugs can cause drowsiness, blurred vision, or slower reaction time. You must read labels and follow medical advice, and you may not drive if any drug impairs your ability to operate a vehicle safely.

question: A red flashing traffic light has the same meaning as a:
options: a:Stop sign.,b:Solid red light.,c:Yield sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe. It does not mean yield without stopping.

question: What is the best way to avoid dangerous situations while driving?
options: a:Turn off the radio and avoid scanning mirrors.,b:Always keep your eyes focused only straight ahead.,c:Constantly be aware of what is happening around your vehicle.
note: To avoid dangerous situations, you must constantly be aware of traffic and road conditions all around your vehicle. Regularly check your mirrors, scan ahead, and watch to the sides so you can spot hazards early and adjust your speed or position in time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From top to bottom, what is the proper order of lights on a vertical traffic signal?
options: a:Red on top, yellow in the middle, green on the bottom.,b:Red on top, green in the middle, yellow on the bottom.,c:Green on top, yellow in the middle, red on the bottom.
note: On a standard vertical traffic signal, the red light is at the top, the yellow (amber) light is in the middle, and the green light is at the bottom. Knowing this order helps you understand the signal even if the colors are hard to see.

question: On a dimly lit street at night, you should:
options: a:Use high beams to better see the road ahead.,b:Keep instrument panel lights very bright so others see you.,c:Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
note: At night on dimly lit streets, you must drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance you can see with your headlights. This ensures you have enough time to react to hazards that appear in the illuminated area ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,b:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:When you are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: After you pass another vehicle, stay in the left lane until you can clearly see both of the vehicle’s headlights in your inside rearview mirror. That tells you you’re far enough ahead to move back without cutting them off or forcing them to brake suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check for traffic when entering a freeway?
options: a:Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder in the direction of the merge.,b:Only use your rearview mirror.,c:Use your rearview and side mirrors without turning your head.
note: When entering a freeway, use your mirrors to judge traffic and always do a quick glance over your shoulder in the direction you’re merging. This shoulder check lets you see vehicles in your blind spot so you can choose a safe gap and merge smoothly.

question: In fog, you should use:
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers primarily.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back at you, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and reduce glare, improving your ability to see lane lines and other vehicles.

question: When traveling to an unfamiliar area, what should you do before you leave?
options: a:Start with a general idea and figure it out while driving.,b:Depend only on road signs to find your way.,c:Plan your route in advance.
note: Before driving to an unfamiliar area, plan your route using a map, GPS, or directions. Knowing your route ahead of time reduces last‑second lane changes, sudden turns, and distractions from trying to navigate while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: Drivers may pass on a two-lane road when there is a single solid yellow line on their side of the centerline.
options: a:True,b:False
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means passing is not allowed. You may only pass on a two‑lane road when the line on your side is broken, and only if you have enough clear distance ahead to pass safely.

question: When passing a bicyclist on a two-lane road without bike lanes, the safest method is to:
options: a:Slow down, wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass leaving sufficient space.,b:Pass quickly and close to the cyclist to minimize lane time.,c:Never pass until a traffic signal or stop sign.
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down, wait until there is no oncoming traffic, and then move over to give them plenty of space—at least 3 feet, and more at higher speeds. Do not squeeze by in the same lane; fully or mostly change lanes when safe so you don’t startle or endanger the cyclist.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches while you're on a one-way street, you must:
options: a:Turn on your hazard flashers and keep moving.,b:Keep driving until you reach the next block.,c:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, you must yield the right-of-way by moving toward the nearest edge of the road and stopping until it passes. On a one-way street, this means pulling to whichever curb or roadside is closer and stopping, as long as it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are on a one-way street; you may turn left onto another one-way street only if:
options: a:You increase your speed before the turn.,b:Traffic on that street moves to the left.,c:Traffic on that street moves to the right.
note: You may turn left from a one-way street onto another one-way street only when the traffic on the street you are turning onto flows to the left and there is no sign prohibiting the turn. Make the turn from the left lane into the left lane of the new street, and always obey any posted turn restrictions.

question: As blood alcohol increases, it generally:
options: a:Makes you feel less confident but speeds reactions.,b:Causes the body to metabolize alcohol faster.,c:Slows your reactions and increases errors.
note: As blood alcohol concentration rises, your reaction time slows, your judgment and coordination worsen, and you are more likely to make serious driving errors. Even small amounts of alcohol can impair driving ability, and higher levels greatly increase crash risk.

question: If your vehicle's wheels have run off the pavement edge, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn the wheels sharply to get back on immediately.,b:Accelerate and then swerve back onto the pavement.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Ease off the accelerator and slow down gradually. Once you have the car under control and traffic is clear, gently steer back onto the pavement; do not jerk the wheel or suddenly swerve.

question: What should you do if you become tired while driving?
options: a:Drink coffee and continue.,b:Open a window and drive on.,c:Stop to rest or change drivers.,d:Turn on bright lights to stay awake.
note: Resting or switching drivers is the best way to address driving fatigue.

question: If one of your tires blows out while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain your current speed and steer straight.,b:Brake hard immediately.,c:Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by easing off the gas pedal.,d:Immediately turn on your hazard lights and steer sharply to the shoulder.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle going straight. Do not slam on the brakes; that can cause you to lose control, especially at higher speeds. Instead, ease your foot off the gas pedal to slow down gradually. Once the vehicle is under control and your speed has dropped, signal, move to the shoulder, and brake gently to stop in a safe place.

question: If a pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of them.,b:Flash your lights to signal them to hurry.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,d:Stop and yield to the pedestrian if they are in or about to enter your lane.
note: When a pedestrian starts to cross in front of you, you must slow down and be prepared to stop, yielding the right-of-way. Drivers are required to use extra caution around pedestrians, especially children or anyone who may move unpredictably. Never speed up or try to intimidate a pedestrian with your vehicle.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When exiting an expressway only.,b:When behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.,c:Only when following a motorcycle.,d:Whenever visibility is reduced or you need more time to react, such as in bad weather, heavy traffic, or when being tailgated.
note: You should increase your following distance whenever conditions make it harder to see or stop in time. This includes following large vehicles that block your view, driving in bad weather, at higher speeds, in heavy traffic, when following motorcycles or bicycles, or when you are being tailgated. More space gives you extra time to react and stop safely.

question: To prevent "expressway hypnosis" on long trips you should:
options: a:Stare straight ahead to maintain focus.,b:Keep your eyes moving and vary speed occasionally.,c:Keep the interior very warm.,d:Take regular breaks, keep your eyes moving, and avoid staring at one spot for too long.
note: To prevent "expressway hypnosis," you should keep your eyes moving, regularly check your mirrors, scan far ahead, and take breaks to rest. Slightly varying your speed and position within your lane helps keep you mentally engaged. Staring straight ahead or making the car very warm can make you drowsy and reduce your alertness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights and siren, you must pull over and stop:
options: a:Regardless of its direction of approach.,b:Only if it is following you.,c:Only if it is approaching from the opposite direction.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you must immediately pull to the right edge of the road and stop, regardless of whether it is coming from ahead, behind, or from a side street. Stopping clears a path so the emergency vehicle can pass safely and quickly.

question: At a railroad crossing where you see no train, you must stop under which condition?
options: a:If a stop sign is posted, or warning devices (lights, gates) are active, or a flagger signals you to stop.,b:Only if crossing lights are flashing.,c:Only if a train is clearly visible.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing any time a stop sign is posted, the warning lights are flashing, the gates are lowered, a flagger tells you to stop, or a train is clearly approaching. Even if you do not see a train, you are legally required to obey all signs, signals, and flaggers at the crossing.

question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling 55 mph may take up to how many feet to stop?
options: a:About 50 feet.,b:Nearly 400 feet.,c:Approximately 125 feet.
note: Large trucks need much more distance to stop than passenger cars. A fully loaded tractor‑trailer traveling about 55 mph can require nearly 400 feet to come to a complete stop, which is more than the length of a football field. This is why you should avoid cutting in front of trucks or braking suddenly when a truck is close behind you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two drivers arrive at the same time to an open intersection, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left.,b:The driver on the right.,c:The driver who signals first.
note: At an open (uncontrolled) intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive much slower than the flow of traffic, what is the likely result?
options: a:You will demonstrate defensive driving techniques.,b:You may interfere with traffic and could receive a ticket.,c:You will improve traffic flow.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because it forces other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly. If you unnecessarily block or interfere with traffic by driving too slowly, you may receive a ticket. When conditions allow, drive at or near the posted speed limit and match the flow of traffic, without exceeding the legal limit.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection is equivalent to:
options: a:A yield sign.,b:A slow sign.,c:A flashing yellow light.,d:A stop sign.
note: A flashing red signal means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when it is safe and after yielding to any pedestrians or vehicles with the right‑of‑way.

question: If you are being tailgated and there is no right lane to move into, what should you do?
options: a:Brake hard to warn the tailgater.,b:Wait until the road ahead is clear and then reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to pass.,c:Ignore the tailgater and maintain speed at all costs.
note: When being tailgated and you cannot move right, keep a steady speed and increase your following distance ahead. When the road ahead is clear and it is safe, gradually slow down to encourage the tailgater to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this can cause a rear‑end collision.

question: Diamond-shaped traffic signs are used to:
options: a:Alert drivers to school zones specifically.,b:Indicate public recreation areas.,c:Warn of existing or possible hazards ahead.
note: Diamond‑shaped signs are warning signs. They alert drivers to existing or potential hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, merging traffic, or pedestrian crossings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who must yield?
options: a:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:Both may proceed together without yielding.,c:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.
note: A single broken (dashed) yellow line in the center of a two‑lane road indicates two‑way traffic and that passing is allowed in both directions when it is safe and legal to do so. You must still check for oncoming traffic and ensure you have enough space and time to pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking, how much space should you leave between your vehicle and the cars in front and behind?
options: a:One foot,b:Six inches,c:Two to three feet
note: When parallel parking you should leave at least two feet between your vehicle and the cars parked in front and behind you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you come to an intersection that is blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.,b:Stay out of the intersection until you can pass completely through.,c:Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it. If traffic is stopped and you cannot get all the way through, stay behind the stop line or crosswalk. Blocking the intersection can prevent cross traffic and emergency vehicles from moving and is illegal in many jurisdictions.

question: As daylight begins to fade, which lights should you use to help others see you?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:High beam headlights regardless of other traffic.,c:Low beam headlights.,d:Emergency flashers.
note: As daylight fades, turn on your low beam headlights so other drivers can see you and you can see the road clearly. High beams should only be used when there is no oncoming traffic and no vehicle directly ahead of you, because they can blind other drivers. Parking lights and emergency flashers are not a substitute for headlights while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Turn into any lane.,b:Turn into the second lane.,c:Turn into the first available lane.
note: When turning left from a two‑way street onto a one‑way street, you must turn into the first available legal lane on the one‑way street, usually the lane closest to you. Entering directly into a farther lane can be unsafe and may violate lane‑use rules, because you would be crossing over a lane that you are required to enter first.

question: If the solid white edge line on the right slants toward the left, it indicates:
options: a:You will be required to turn left ahead.,b:The road is narrowing ahead.,c:An intersection is just ahead.
note: A solid white edge line marks the right edge of the roadway. If this line slants or angles toward the left, it warns that the road is narrowing or the shoulder is ending ahead. You should reduce speed if needed and be prepared for less room to maneuver.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is using high beams and fails to dim them, you should look toward which part of the road?
options: a:The left side of the road.,b:The right side of the road.,c:Either side of the road.,d:The center of the road.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, the bright light can temporarily blind you. To protect your night vision and still stay oriented in your lane, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road, using the edge line as a guide, rather than looking directly into the oncoming headlights.

question: You should use your horn to warn others when:
options: a:Passing a bicyclist.,b:Traveling through an intersection.,c:You see a child who might run into the street.
note: The horn is a warning device, not something to use routinely. You should use it when you need to alert others to a potential collision, such as when a child or pedestrian might suddenly run into the street and may not see or hear your vehicle. Avoid using the horn unnecessarily, like just because you are passing or moving through a normal intersection.

question: Never use high beam headlights in fog because:
options: a:Vehicles behind will follow too closely.,b:Approaching vehicles won't see you.,c:The light will reflect back into your eyes.
note: In fog, high beam headlights shine into the water droplets and reflect back toward your eyes, creating glare and actually reducing how far you can see. Low beams, fog lights if equipped, and reduced speed are safer because they cut under the fog more effectively and cause less reflection.

question: If you become drowsy while driving, you should:
options: a:Try to fight the drowsiness and continue driving.,b:Open the windows and turn up the radio to stay awake.,c:Take caffeine pills and keep driving.,d:Pull off at the first safe location and take a break.
note: Drowsy driving is extremely dangerous because your reaction time and judgment are impaired, and you may even fall asleep at the wheel. If you feel sleepy, the safe choice is to pull off the road at the first safe place, such as a rest area or parking lot, and take a break, nap, or switch drivers. Tricks like opening windows, turning up the radio, or taking caffeine cannot reliably keep you alert.

question: What minimum following distance should you keep behind a motorcycle in normal conditions?
options: a:One second.,b:Three to four seconds.,c:Two seconds.
note: Motorcycles can stop and maneuver more quickly than many cars, and riders are more vulnerable in a collision. You should leave extra space so you have time to react if the motorcycle stops suddenly, swerves to avoid a hazard, or falls. In normal conditions, maintain at least a three‑ to four‑second following distance behind a motorcycle, and increase this gap in poor weather or at higher speeds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down to create space in front so the other driver can complete the pass.,b:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,c:Maintain speed and ignore their attempt.
note: When another driver is passing you, help them do it safely. Slightly reduce your speed and maintain your lane so they have more space and time to pass and return to the lane. Never speed up to block a pass, as that increases risk of a collision.

question: What does 'distracted driving' mean?
options: a:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,b:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.,c:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
note: Distracted driving is anything that takes your attention away from driving—your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off the driving task. Examples include texting, eating, adjusting controls, or focusing on passengers instead of the road.

question: When a pedestrian uses a guide dog or white cane and is crossing, you must:
options: a:Tell them where to cross.,b:Always yield the right-of-way.,c:Only yield if at a corner.
note: Pedestrians who are blind or visually impaired and using a white cane or guide dog always have the right-of-way. You must stop or yield as needed, never honk or rush them, and allow them to cross safely at any crossing point.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it true you do not have to stop for a school bus with red lights flashing if it is on a private road?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm whenever the law requires, which in many states includes private roads, parking lots, and school property open to public traffic. Always stop when in doubt and proceed only when the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.

question: A railroad crossbuck sign should be treated the same as which traffic control?
options: a:A yield sign.,b:A stop sign always.,c:No control; you may proceed without slowing.
note: A railroad crossbuck is treated like a yield sign. Slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. You must yield the right-of-way to any approaching train and never proceed onto the tracks unless you are sure you can fully clear them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you change from one lane to another?
options: a:Quickly and often.,b:When a car is in your blind spot.,c:Gradually and carefully.
note: Lane changes should always be gradual and deliberate. Before moving over, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, signal in advance, and move smoothly only when there is enough space. Avoid sudden or frequent lane changes, which increase the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross double solid yellow centerlines to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Yes,b:Only to turn into a driveway or private entrance,c:No
note: Double solid yellow lines mean vehicles in both directions are prohibited from crossing the lines to pass. However, you may cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway or private road when it is safe. You must never use a lane with double solid yellow lines for passing other moving vehicles.

question: Blue traffic signs give information about what?
options: a:Mileage information like distances to locations.,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Motorist services such as rest areas
note: Blue traffic signs are service signs. They provide information about motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, hospitals, and lodging. They help drivers locate essential services while traveling.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross the centerline to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the yellow line next to your side is broken.,b:When the yellow line next to the opposite side of the road is broken.,c:If the vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.
note: You may cross the centerline to pass only when the yellow line next to your lane is broken and it is safe to do so. A broken yellow line on your side means passing is permitted if you have enough clear distance ahead; if the solid line is on your side, you must not pass.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving,b:Following other vehicles too closely,c:Excessive speed under conditions,d:All of the above
note: Inattentive driving, following too closely, and driving too fast for conditions are all major causes of crashes. Safe drivers stay focused on the road, maintain a safe following distance, and adjust speed for traffic, weather, and road conditions to reduce the risk of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, the speed limit outside a business or residential area is:
options: a:45 mph.,b:35 mph.,c:25 mph.
note: When no speed limit sign is posted, many states set a default limit for rural or non-residential roads. A common default on state roads outside business or residential areas is 45 mph, unless a different limit is posted. Always follow the posted sign if one is present, as it overrides the general rule.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers who are turning left must yield to which vehicles?
options: a:Overtaking cars.,b:Oncoming cars traveling straight ahead.,c:No one.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, as well as to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Only begin your left turn when there is a safe gap and you will not force oncoming drivers to slow or stop suddenly.

question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving ability?
options: a:Three drinks.,b:Two drinks.,c:One drink.
note: Even one alcoholic drink can begin to affect judgment, reaction time, and coordination. Because driving requires full attention and quick responses, any amount of alcohol can reduce your ability to drive safely, even if you do not feel drunk.

question: If the vehicle ahead has stopped at a crosswalk, what should you do?
options: a:Change lanes,b:Stop and proceed only when all pedestrians have crossed.,c:Cautiously pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.
note: If a vehicle has stopped at a crosswalk, assume it may be yielding to pedestrians you cannot see. You must not pass a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk. Stop as well, and proceed only after you are sure all pedestrians have completely crossed and the crosswalk is clear.

question: Which of these may cause distracted driving?
options: a:Talking or texting on a cell phone.,b:Eating,c:Changing a radio station or CD.,d:All of the above.
note: Distractions are anything that take your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving. Using a cell phone, eating, and adjusting the radio or music system all reduce your attention and increase crash risk. To drive safely, minimize all types of distractions inside the vehicle.

question: When should drivers use their turn signals?
options: a:When changing lanes, entering/exiting the freeway, or turning at intersections.,b:Only when turning at an intersection.,c:Only when changing lanes.
note: Use your turn signal every time you turn, change lanes, or enter/exit a freeway. Signaling lets other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians anticipate your movement and adjust safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you begin to pass another vehicle if you do not have space to return to your lane?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Never begin to pass unless you are sure you have enough clear space to complete the pass and return to your lane safely. You must not rely on other drivers to slow down or make room for you.

question: If a road is slippery, your following distance should be:
options: a:Greater than normal.,b:The same as usual.,c:Closer than normal.
note: On slippery roads, increase your following distance. Extra space gives you more time to react and a longer distance to brake gently without skidding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an unmarked stop sign (no crosswalk), where should you stop?
options: a:At the stop line; if none, before the crosswalk; if none, before entering the intersection.,b:At least one car length before the stop sign.,c:Only if other traffic is present.,d:In the middle of the intersection.
note: At a stop sign, stop at the stop line if there is one. If there is no stop line, stop before entering the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection so you can see traffic and pedestrians clearly and yield as required.

question: If a pedestrian is in the middle of the street when your signal turns green, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,c:Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.
note: At a green light you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk; wait for them to clear the roadway before proceeding.

question: You hear a siren but cannot immediately see the emergency vehicle. What should you do?
options: a:Keep driving until you see where the vehicle is.,b:Slow down and continue driving until you locate it.,c:Pull safely to the right side of the road and stop until you are sure it is not coming toward you.
note: When you hear a siren or air horn but cannot see the emergency vehicle, you must still yield the right-of-way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop. Staying stopped until you are sure the vehicle is not approaching your direction helps keep the path clear for emergency responders and prevents sudden, unsafe maneuvers if the vehicle appears suddenly.

question: Your vehicle's blind spot refers to an area:
options: a:Directly behind your vehicle only.,b:You see in your rearview mirror.,c:You cannot see without moving your head.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that are not visible in your mirrors. To check them, you must briefly turn your head and look over your shoulder. Relying only on mirrors can cause you to miss vehicles, bicycles, or motorcycles traveling alongside you, especially when changing lanes or merging.

question: When a school bus ahead is stopped to load or unload with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must:
options: a:Proceed if you think children are not present.,b:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,c:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,d:Slow down and pass while watching for children.
note: When a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. This rule protects children who may be crossing the road and can appear suddenly from in front of or behind the bus.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Double solid yellow centerlines indicate:
options: a:Passing is permitted if safe.,b:Passing is prohibited in both directions.,c:Traffic flows in the same direction on both sides.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that passing is not allowed for vehicles traveling in either direction. You may cross these lines only when making a permitted left turn into or out of a driveway or side road, but not to pass another vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, you should start the turn from:
options: a:Any lane if it looks clear.,b:The center lane only.,c:The lane closest to the left curb.
note: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, you should start from the lane closest to the left curb. This keeps your turn tight and predictable, reduces conflicts with other traffic, and aligns you properly with the correct lane on the street you are entering.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Flash your headlights to make them aware of you.,b:Always pass on the right side quickly.,c:Avoid driving alongside large vehicles and do not tailgate them.
note: Large trucks and buses have wide blind spots along both sides and directly behind them. If you drive right next to or close behind a large vehicle, the driver may not see you at all. To stay safe, avoid lingering alongside these vehicles, pass promptly and safely, and leave extra following distance instead of tailgating.

question: While backing up, what is the recommended way to see behind your vehicle?
options: a:Back up while looking forward.,b:Rely exclusively on your mirrors.,c:Open your door to check behind you.,d:Look over your shoulder and out the rear window rather than relying only on mirrors.
note: When backing up, you should turn your head and look directly out the rear window so you can clearly see what is behind you. Mirrors and cameras can help, but they do not show everything and should not be relied on alone. Always back up slowly while looking over your shoulder and checking your surroundings.

question: Parking in an access aisle next to a handicap spot is allowed when:
options: a:When you have a disability placard.,b:When other spaces are full.,c:Never.
note: Access aisles next to disabled parking spaces are reserved for wheelchair lifts and extra space for people with disabilities to enter and exit vehicles. These striped areas must always be kept clear, even if you have a disability placard or the lot is crowded. Parking there is illegal and subject to fines.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady yellow traffic signal means:
options: a:A steady red light will soon appear.,b:A flashing yellow will appear next.,c:The light is about to turn green.
note: A steady yellow traffic light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and prepare to stop before entering the intersection, unless you are so close that stopping suddenly would be unsafe. It is not a signal that the light will turn green next.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permissible to pass another vehicle?
options: a:In a curve or on a hill.,b:When your lane is next to a broken yellow line and it is safe to pass.,c:By using the shoulder of the highway.
note: You may pass another vehicle only where passing is allowed and conditions are safe. A broken yellow line next to your lane means you are permitted to pass if you have enough clear distance and no oncoming traffic. Never pass on hills, curves, or on the shoulder, where visibility and control are reduced.

question: If the rear of your vehicle starts skidding to the left, what action should you take?
options: a:Steer to the right.,b:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.,c:Steer to the left.
note: When the rear of your vehicle skids, you should ease off the accelerator and steer in the same direction the rear is skidding. If the rear slides left, you steer left. This aligns the front wheels with the direction of travel and helps you regain control without overcorrecting.

question: Why is driving at night more dangerous than daytime driving?
options: a:Headlights eliminate all visibility issues.,b:The road is always more slippery at night.,c:Your reaction time is slower at night regardless of visibility.,d:You cannot see as far ahead at night
note: At night, your headlights limit how far and how clearly you can see compared with daylight. Reduced visibility and glare from other vehicles’ lights make it harder to detect hazards in time, so driving at night is more dangerous even when you feel alert.

question: What do pentagonal (five-sided) signs indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:Speed limits.,c:School zones and school crossings.
note: Pentagonal (five-sided) signs are used for school zones and school crossings. When you see this shape, slow down, watch for children, and be prepared to stop for pedestrians in or near the roadway.

question: Because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see, you should:
options: a:Share a lane with a motorcycle.,b:Make constant visual checks and be alert.,c:Always slow down to a stop near them.
note: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are smaller and can be hidden in blind spots, so you must make frequent visual checks—use mirrors, check over your shoulder before changing lanes, and scan the road ahead. Never share a lane with a motorcycle; give them a full lane and extra space.

question: Does drinking coffee after consuming alcohol reduce your blood alcohol concentration?
options: a:Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.,b:Decreases blood alcohol concentration.,c:Cancels the effect of the alcohol.
note: Coffee does not lower your blood alcohol concentration. Only time allows your body to metabolize alcohol. Stimulants like caffeine may make you feel more awake, but they do not make you less impaired or safer to drive.

question: At a steady yellow traffic light, if you have not entered the intersection yet, you should:
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Proceed at the same speed.,c:Come to a safe stop before the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection, you are expected to slow down and stop if you can do so safely, rather than speeding up to get through.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle, you should:
options: a:Signal early enough so others know your intent.,b:Only signal just before changing lanes.,c:Signal after you have completed the pass.,d:Not signal at all if traffic is light.
note: Before passing or changing lanes, you must signal early enough to give other drivers time to see and react to your intentions. Signaling only at the last moment or after the maneuver does not give adequate warning and is unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following takes precedence over signs, signals, and pavement markings?
options: a:A police officer directing traffic.,b:A steady red light.,c:A stop sign.
note: When a police officer or authorized traffic officer is directing traffic, their hand signals and instructions override traffic lights, signs, and pavement markings. You must follow the officer’s directions even if they conflict with the normal controls.

question: If involved in an accident, what should a driver do at the scene?
options: a:Leave immediately if the other vehicle is blocking your path.,b:Stop their vehicle at or near the scene.,c:Stand in traffic lanes to direct cars.
note: If you are involved in a crash, you must stop at or as close to the scene as possible without blocking traffic more than necessary. Then check for injuries, call for help, and move vehicles out of traffic if it is safe to do so. Never leave the scene or stand in moving traffic lanes.

question: How can you avoid collisions caused by vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Change lanes without signaling.,b:Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.,c:Honk before changing lanes instead of checking.,d:Quickly turn your head to check the blind spot before changing lanes.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot cover. Before changing lanes, quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to be sure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

question: A curb painted red means:
options: a:Reserved for passenger drop-off.,b:Loading zone only.,c:No stopping, standing, or parking allowed.
note: A red curb means you may not stop, stand, or park there at any time, except when directed by law enforcement or to obey a traffic control device. It is not a loading zone or a passenger drop‑off area; it is a no‑stopping zone for general traffic.

question: Do solid or dashed white pavement markings indicate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:True,b:False
note: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction and also mark the right edge of the roadway. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. So solid or dashed white lines do not indicate opposing traffic.

question: What can happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:Both effects will be reduced.,b:No interaction will occur.,c:The effects of both may be increased.
note: When alcohol is combined with many prescription, over‑the‑counter, or illegal drugs, the effects of both substances can be intensified. This can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment more than either substance alone.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving on a busy street, what should you do first?
options: a:Shift to neutral, brake as needed, steer off the road to a safe area, then turn off the ignition.,b:Blow your horn repeatedly to warn other drivers.,c:Slam on the brakes hard to stop immediately.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep calm, shift to neutral to disconnect engine power from the wheels, then brake smoothly while steering to a safe place off the road. Once you are in control and out of traffic, turn off the ignition without locking the steering wheel. Do not slam on the brakes or turn the key off before you have control of the vehicle.

question: If you are parallel parked facing downhill, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Leave them straight ahead.,b:Turn them away from the curb.,c:Turn them toward the side of the road or curb.
note: When parking facing downhill, turn the front wheels toward the curb or road edge. If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will contact the curb or edge and help stop the vehicle from rolling into traffic.

question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:It has the same meaning as a circular red traffic light.,b:Drivers may turn in the direction of the arrow.,c:It is never used as a traffic signal.
note: A solid red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped in the direction of the arrow. You may not turn in that direction until the arrow changes to green or a permitted signal. This is the same requirement as a circular red light, but it applies specifically to the movement indicated by the arrow.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an approaching emergency vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down until it passes you.,b:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.,c:Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with siren and/or flashing lights, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping until it has passed. If you are in an intersection, clear the intersection first, then pull to the right and stop.

question: If stopped at a railroad crossing with multiple tracks you should:
options: a:Stop on the first track and then move forward,b:Cross as soon as one train passes.,c:Assume only one train will come through.,d:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before proceeding.
note: At a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, one train may hide another that is approaching on a different track. After one train passes, wait until you can clearly see down all tracks in both directions and are sure no other trains are coming before you proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are turning onto a street that has multiple lanes traveling in your direction, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into the lane marked with an arrow.,b:Into the middle lane.,c:Into the lane closest to your previous lane.
note: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your way, you must turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you were in before the turn. Complete the turn into that nearest lane first, then change lanes later when it is safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should drive below the posted speed limit when:
options: a:You see a police car,b:Entering a highway with other cars.,c:Road or weather conditions make normal speeds unsafe.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum allowed under ideal conditions. When rain, snow, fog, heavy traffic, or poor road conditions make normal speeds unsafe, you must slow down below the posted limit to a speed that is safe for current conditions.

question: Each time you pass another vehicle, what happens to your risk of collision?
options: a:There is no change in collision risk.,b:There is an increased chance of collision.,c:The chance of collision decreases.
note: Every time you pass another vehicle, your risk of a collision goes up. Passing puts you in the oncoming lane or in close proximity to other vehicles, reduces your escape options, and often involves higher speeds. Only pass when you are sure you have enough clear distance, good visibility, and it is legal and safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you approach a roundabout you should:
options: a:Maintain your current speed.,b:Increase your speed to merge quickly.,c:Decrease your speed and prepare to yield.
note: When approaching a roundabout, you must slow down and be prepared to yield to traffic already in the circle, as well as to pedestrians in crosswalks. Enter only when there is a safe gap, and travel at a low, controlled speed to maintain good control and reaction time.

question: If you encounter a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:
options: a:Avoid the puddle if possible.,b:Maintain the posted speed to drive through it.,c:Shift into neutral as you drive through the water.
note: If you see a deep puddle ahead, the safest choice is to avoid it if you can do so safely. Deep water can cause hydroplaning, hide potholes or debris, and damage your brakes or engine. If you must drive through water, go very slowly and test your brakes afterward to be sure they are working properly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does the absence of a sign or pavement marking forbidding passing mean it is safe to pass?
options: a:False,b:True
note: The absence of a sign or pavement marking banning passing does not mean it is automatically safe to pass. You must still ensure you have enough clear distance, good visibility, no oncoming traffic, and that road and weather conditions allow you to complete the pass safely and legally.

question: Is it legal to park in the handicap parking access aisle next to a marked stall?
options: a:Not given,b:True,c:False
note: It is illegal to park in the striped handicap access aisle next to an accessible parking stall. These areas must remain clear to provide space for wheelchair ramps and lifts so people with disabilities can safely enter and exit their vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it unsafe to pass other vehicles?
options: a:In open countryside.,b:On straight rural roads.,c:At intersections.
note: Passing is especially unsafe at intersections because vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians can enter from side streets or driveways and may be hidden from view. You should avoid passing near intersections, railroad crossings, and driveways or entrances where cross‑traffic may appear suddenly.

question: If you are upset, nervous, or crying before driving, what should you do?
options: a:Drive faster because you are more alert.,b:Drive no differently than usual.,c:Take the time to calm down and focus before starting to drive.
note: Strong emotions such as anger, fear, or sadness can distract you, slow your reaction time, and cause poor decisions. If you are upset or crying, wait until you have calmed down and can focus fully on driving before you start the car or continue your trip.

question: If dust or smoke makes it hard to see other vehicles, you should:
options: a:Use only emergency flashers and keep speed constant.,b:Drive more slowly and turn on your headlights.,c:Turn on your parking lights only.
note: Dust or smoke can greatly reduce visibility, so you should slow down and turn on your low‑beam headlights so you can see and be seen. Avoid using only emergency flashers or parking lights while moving, because other drivers may misjudge your speed or not see you clearly.

question: A broken (dashed) yellow line between two lanes indicates:
options: a:Traffic lanes go the same direction only.,b:Passing is permitted when safe.,c:Passing is prohibited.
note: A broken (dashed) yellow line in the center of a two‑way road means traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when it can be done safely. You must check for oncoming traffic, ensure there is enough clear distance to pass, and return to your lane before coming close to any oncoming vehicle.

question: In heavy fog you should:
options: a:Slow down and use low beam headlights.,b:Slow down and use high beam headlights.,c:Turn lights on and off to warn others.
note: In heavy fog, slow down and use low‑beam headlights so the light does not reflect back and blind you. High beams make it harder to see in fog, and flashing your lights on and off can confuse other drivers. If visibility becomes extremely poor, pull off the road to a safe place and wait for conditions to improve.

question: When you need to change lanes, what important steps should you take?
options: a:Flash headlights and change lanes without signaling.,b:Signal ahead of the lane change,c:Honk before changing lanes only.,d:Speed up and merge quickly.
note: Before changing lanes, always signal in advance, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check blind spots. Only move when there is enough space and it is safe to do so.

question: What does an orange-and-red triangular emblem on the back of a vehicle indicate?
options: a:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:There is shoulder work ahead.,c:A slow-moving vehicle (traveling 25 mph or less).
note: An orange-and-red triangular emblem on the back of a vehicle means it is a slow-moving vehicle, typically traveling 25 mph or less. Approach slowly, be prepared to slow down, and only pass when it is legal and safe.

question: After a stressful incident at work, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Play loud music to distract yourself.,b:Immediately start driving to get home quicker.,c:Take a few minutes to calm down before beginning to drive.,d:Drive fast on a highway to release stress.
note: Strong emotions like anger or stress can distract you and slow your reactions. Take a few minutes to calm down, breathe, and refocus before driving so you can give the road your full attention.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: During school hours, what is the speed limit in a school zone?
options: a:10 mph,b:15 mph,c:Follow the posted school zone speed limit shown on the signs.
note: School zone speed limits are set by state or local law and are clearly posted on signs. In many areas this is 25 mph, but in others it may be 15 mph or another value. Always follow the posted school zone speed limit during the specified times or when children are present, and drive with extra caution.

question: When involved in a collision, what should you do regarding the injured?
options: a:Move injured people as far from the road as possible regardless of injuries.,b:Assume injured people are fine and don't call for help.,c:Do not move seriously injured persons unless there's immediate danger.
note: Do not move someone who is seriously injured unless there is an immediate danger, such as fire or oncoming traffic, because moving them can worsen injuries, especially to the neck or spine. Call 911, keep them as still and comfortable as possible, and provide first aid only if you are trained and it is safe to do so.

question: You drive defensively when you:
options: a:Look only at the car in front of you while driving.,b:Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.,c:Put one car length between you and the car ahead.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road ahead, to the sides, and behind you so you can spot hazards early and react in time. Keeping your eyes moving helps you see changing traffic, pedestrians, and road conditions instead of fixating on just the vehicle in front.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best action?
options: a:Remain inside your vehicle and wait for help.,b:Leave the vehicle and walk for assistance.,c:Lie down inside the car and sleep.,d:Walk into the road to attract attention.
note: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, it is usually safest to stay inside your vehicle. Your car provides shelter and is easier for rescuers to see. Run the engine only periodically for heat, keep a window slightly open for fresh air, and make sure the exhaust pipe is clear of snow to prevent carbon monoxide buildup.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must obey directions given by which of the following people?
options: a:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.,b:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,c:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.
note: Flaggers at construction zones are authorized traffic-control persons. Their directions have the same legal force as traffic signals or signs, and you must obey them to keep workers and drivers safe through changing lane patterns and temporary hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway with two solid yellow lines dividing directions, you may:
options: a:Cross the lines only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:Cross the lines to pass slower traffic if no oncoming cars are visible.,c:Never cross under any circumstance including left turns.,d:Use the left lane for passing anytime traffic allows.
note: Two solid yellow lines between opposite directions of traffic mean no passing. You may not cross them to pass another vehicle, but you may carefully cross to make a left turn into or out of a driveway, alley, or private road when it is safe and not otherwise prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting a roundabout or traffic circle you should generally be in:
options: a:The left lane at all times.,b:The center lane and signal early.,c:The right lane unless signs or markings indicate otherwise.
note: In most roundabouts, you should be in the right lane when you are ready to exit, unless signs or lane markings direct you differently. Being in the correct lane and signaling your exit helps other drivers predict your path and reduces sudden lane changes inside the circle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the light is green but traffic ahead is blocking the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Enter the intersection and follow the vehicles ahead.,b:Remain out of the intersection until traffic ahead clears.,c:Turn left and find another route.
note: A green light does not give you the right to block an intersection. You may only enter if you can completely clear it without stopping. If traffic is stopped ahead and you would be stuck in the intersection, you must wait behind the stop line until there is enough space to get all the way through.

question: What does a red right-turn arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:You may turn after slowing and checking for traffic.,b:You may not turn in that direction until the signal turns green.,c:You may turn in that direction only after coming to a complete stop.
note: A solid red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped. You may not turn in the direction of the arrow until it changes to green or a green arrow appears, unless a specific sign allows a turn on red and local law permits it.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly and use the brakes lightly while slowing.,b:Apply the brake and hold it hard.,c:Immediately pull over at high speed.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly, stay straight, and ease your foot off the accelerator. Let the vehicle slow down gradually, then brake gently and pull off the road when you have control. Hard braking can cause loss of control.

question: Which of these commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Driving too fast for conditions or exceeding the posted limit.,b:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,c:Constantly scanning and staying focused.,d:Maintaining the speed of surrounding traffic within the limit.
note: Driving too fast for conditions or over the speed limit is a major cause of crashes. Higher speed reduces your time to react and increases stopping distance and crash severity, especially in bad weather, heavy traffic, or poor visibility.

question: When does your vehicle's stopping distance increase?
options: a:On paved highways.,b:When driving at night.,c:On a wet or icy road.
note: Stopping distance increases whenever traction is reduced, such as on wet, icy, snowy, or loose surfaces. With less grip, your tires need more distance to slow and stop, so you must reduce speed and increase following distance.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by:
options: a:Only passengers on long trips.,b:The driver and all passengers in the vehicle.,c:Only the front-seat passengers.
note: Seat belts protect everyone in the vehicle, not just front-seat passengers or people on long trips. In a crash, unbelted occupants can be thrown around inside the car or ejected, and they can injure others by becoming projectiles. The safest practice is for the driver and every passenger to wear a seat belt on every trip.

question: When driving in fog you should use:
options: a:Your high-beam headlights.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Low-beam headlights (and fog lights if available).
note: In fog, you should use low-beam headlights, and fog lights if your vehicle has them. High beams shine light upward and can reflect off the water droplets in fog, creating glare and making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and improve your ability to see lane lines and the edge of the roadway.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:Motorcycles do not follow the same traffic laws as other vehicles.,b:Motorcycles always brake more slowly than cars.,c:Motorcycles can stop much more quickly than standard vehicles
note: Motorcycles are lighter and have powerful brakes, so they can often stop more quickly than larger vehicles. If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time or space to react if the motorcyclist brakes or swerves suddenly. Always leave extra following distance behind motorcycles to reduce the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Having one outside mirror eliminates blind spots.,b:Blind spots can be checked using only the rearview mirror.,c:Large trucks have much larger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
note: All vehicles have blind spots—areas you cannot see with your mirrors alone—so you must turn your head to check them. Large trucks and buses have much bigger blind spots on all sides, especially directly behind and along the right side. If you cannot see the truck driver’s mirrors, the driver likely cannot see you, so avoid lingering in these areas.

question: Compared with daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:No more or less dangerous.,b:Less dangerous.,c:More dangerous.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving in daylight because you can see less of the road ahead, it is harder to judge distance and speed, and glare from headlights can temporarily blind you. There is also a greater chance of encountering drowsy or impaired drivers. Reduce speed and increase following distance at night.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow signal indicate compared with a circular yellow light?
options: a:It has the same meaning; you must reduce speed and prepare for red.,b:It means you may turn freely without yielding.,c:It indicates lane closure ahead.,d:It signals a pedestrian crossing only.
note: A solid yellow arrow means your protected turn is ending. You should slow down and be prepared to stop, just as you would for a circular yellow light. If you are already in the intersection when it appears, you may complete the turn, but you should not enter the intersection expecting continued protected right‑of‑way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle that arrives second.,b:The vehicle approaching from the left.,c:The vehicle whose driver honks first.,d:The vehicle approaching from the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at about the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion when there are no signs or signals controlling the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, you must yield to:
options: a:No one.,b:Only vehicles turning right.,c:Oncoming traffic, pedestrians, and bicyclists in or entering the intersection.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles, pedestrians, and bicyclists who are in or entering the intersection or crosswalk. Oncoming traffic has the right‑of‑way unless you have a green arrow, and pedestrians in crosswalks always have priority when they have the walk signal or are lawfully crossing.

question: What is the only thing that reduces blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time.,b:Drinking coffee.,c:Eating fatty foods.,d:Exercising vigorously.
note: Only time lowers your blood alcohol concentration. Your body must metabolize the alcohol, and this process cannot be sped up by coffee, food, cold showers, or exercise. You may feel more awake, but you will still be impaired until enough time has passed.

question: An advisory or speed restriction sign attached to a curve usually:
options: a:Is blue with black lettering.,b:Is triangular in shape.,c:Shows a recommended speed for the curve and should be reduced further in wet or poor conditions.,d:May be disregarded if you feel comfortable at a higher speed.
note: Advisory speed signs on curves show a recommended maximum safe speed under ideal conditions. You should slow to at least that speed and reduce your speed even further in rain, snow, or other poor conditions, because traction and visibility are reduced.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams at night, you should:
options: a:Look directly at the headlights to signal them.,b:Look toward the left edge of your lane.,c:Look toward the right edge of your lane and use peripheral vision to watch the road.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, the bright light can temporarily blind you. To protect your night vision, look toward the right edge of your lane and use your peripheral vision to keep track of the oncoming vehicle and the road ahead. Do not stare directly into the headlights, as this increases glare and reduces your ability to see hazards.

question: After stopping for a train at a railroad crossing, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Look for a second train only.,b:Both watch for a second train and wait for the signal lights to stop flashing and gates to fully rise.,c:Wait for signal lights to stop flashing only.
note: After a train passes, another train may be approaching on the same or an adjacent track, so you must look and listen for additional trains. You should not proceed until you are sure all tracks are clear and all active warning devices—such as flashing lights and lowered gates—have fully stopped and gates are raised. Only then is it safe to cross.

question: When changing lanes, you should never:
options: a:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,b:Change lanes abruptly or without warning.,c:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.
note: Safe lane changes must be smooth and predictable. You should always signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving. What you must never do is change lanes abruptly or without warning, because sudden movements increase the risk of collisions with vehicles you may not see or that are also changing lanes.

question: True or false: Pedestrians in crosswalks and intersections always have the right-of-way.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks and in unmarked crosswalks at intersections, and must stop for pedestrians who are lawfully crossing. However, pedestrians do not literally have the right-of-way in every possible situation—for example, when crossing against a red signal or suddenly stepping into traffic. You must still do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, but the phrase “always have the right-of-way” is not correct in all controlled situations.

question: Are you required to obey directions given by a school crossing guard?
options: a:False,b:True
note: School crossing guards are authorized to control traffic to protect children and other pedestrians. Their directions have the same legal force as traffic control devices. You must slow down, be prepared to stop, and obey their signals or hand directions, even if they differ from normal traffic signals, to ensure everyone’s safety in school zones.

question: Which medications might negatively affect driving?
options: a:Only diet pills.,b:Any medication that can cause drowsiness or impair cognition.,c:Only headache medicines.
note: Medications that can cause drowsiness, slowed reaction time, blurred vision, or impaired thinking can make driving unsafe. This includes many prescription drugs, some over‑the‑counter cold or allergy medicines, sleep aids, and certain pain medications. Always read the label and ask your doctor or pharmacist whether it is safe to drive while taking a medication.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement is true about driving too slowly?
options: a:Driving too slowly is never unsafe.,b:Vehicle speed does not affect safety.,c:Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can be dangerous on some roads.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because it causes other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly and may lead to unsafe passing. You should generally travel with the flow of traffic while staying within the posted speed limit and adjusting for road and weather conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning left you must:
options: a:Swing to the right side of your lane before turning.,b:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,c:Sound your horn regardless of conditions.
note: Before turning left, you must yield the right‑of‑way to oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Wait until there is a safe gap in oncoming traffic and the crosswalk is clear before completing your turn.

question: What do regulatory signs tell drivers?
options: a:Warn of conditions ahead.,b:Only indicate speed limits but nothing else.,c:What drivers must or must not do in a specific area.,d:About nearby scenic or recreational sites.
note: Regulatory signs tell you about laws and rules you must follow, such as speed limits, lane use, turns, parking, and one‑way streets. They usually indicate what you must or must not do in that specific area, and you are legally required to obey them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through an intersection that has a stop sign but lacks a stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection every time.,b:Without stopping if no cross traffic is visible.,c:After slowing to check for cross traffic without stopping.,d:After coming to a complete stop before entering the intersection and ensuring it's safe.
note: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection, at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you have a clear view of approaching traffic. Proceed only when it is safe and after yielding to any vehicles or pedestrians with the right‑of‑way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street, where should you start your turn?
options: a:From the middle of the intersection.,b:From the left lane.,c:From the right lane.
note: On a one-way street, a left turn must be made from the leftmost lane because it keeps you closest to the center of the roadway and away from traffic on your right. Starting from the left lane reduces conflicts with vehicles going straight or turning right and follows standard lane-use rules.

question: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, you should:
options: a:Sit in your car and wait without signaling.,b:Sound your horn at passing drivers for help.,c:Use your four-way flashers and move off the road to a safe place.
note: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, first move as far off the roadway as safely possible, preferably onto the right shoulder. Then turn on your hazard flashers so other drivers can see that your vehicle is stopped. Staying visible and out of moving traffic greatly reduces the risk of a collision.

question: Slowing down to look at a crash or other unusual event typically:
options: a:Is recommended to get a better view.,b:Prevents rear-end collisions.,c:Causes traffic congestion and can increase crash risk.,d:Improves traffic flow.
note: Slowing down just to look at a crash or something unusual, called rubbernecking, disrupts the normal flow of traffic. This sudden slowing can cause congestion and surprise other drivers, increasing the chance of rear-end and secondary crashes. Keep your attention on the road ahead and maintain a safe, steady speed.

question: What is the primary purpose of barriers, drums, cones, and signs in work zones?
options: a:To inconvenience drivers.,b:To keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.,c:To make drivers angry about slow traffic.
note: In work zones, barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to separate traffic from workers and hazards, and to guide vehicles safely through or around the work area. Following these devices helps protect both drivers and road workers and reduces the chance of crashes in construction zones.

question: Why can driving at night be more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:It is more likely to be raining at night.,b:Cars overheat more quickly at night.,c:Visibility is reduced in the dark.
note: At night, your headlights provide much less light than daylight, so you cannot see as far or as clearly. This reduced visibility makes it harder to spot hazards and judge distances and speeds. To compensate, use proper headlights, keep your windshield clean, and reduce your speed so you have time to react.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, which direction should you turn the steering wheel?
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight.,b:In the opposite direction of the skid.,c:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. As the vehicle starts to straighten out, gently adjust the steering to keep control and avoid overcorrecting.

question: Which of the following should you do when driving at night?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
note: At night, you should increase your following distance so you have more time to react with reduced visibility. Use high beams only when appropriate and dim them for oncoming traffic, and avoid looking directly at other vehicles’ headlights to prevent glare.

question: When following a motorcycle, what should you do?
options: a:Be ready to use your horn.,b:Allow a larger following distance.,c:Drive more slowly than usual.
note: Motorcycles can stop and maneuver more quickly than larger vehicles, and they are harder to see. Leave at least a three- to four-second following distance so you have enough time to react if the motorcyclist slows, stops, or swerves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to exit the interstate, when should you begin reducing your speed?
options: a:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,b:As you approach the deceleration lane.,c:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,d:Only after exiting the ramp.
note: Stay at freeway speed until you reach the deceleration lane, then begin slowing down within that lane to match the posted speed for the exit ramp. Slowing on the main freeway can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: While driving through a work zone, you should:
options: a:Maintain your normal speed the whole way through the zone.,b:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.,c:Increase your speed to get through the zone as quickly as possible.
note: In work zones, reduce your speed, obey all posted signs, and be prepared to stop suddenly. Lanes may shift, equipment may enter the roadway, and workers may be close to traffic, so extra caution and lower speeds are essential.

question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Construction workers must yield to vehicles.,b:Pedestrians must always wait for vehicles to pass.,c:Pedestrians have the right-of-way and vehicles must yield.,d:Vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are in a marked or unmarked crosswalk. You must slow or stop as needed to let pedestrians cross safely, and never force them to hurry or step back for you.

question: Should you use high-beam headlights in fog, heavy rain, or snow?
options: a:No — use low beams in fog, snow, and heavy rain.,b:Yes — high beams improve visibility in precipitation.
note: High beams can reflect off fog, heavy rain, or snow and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. In these conditions, use low-beam headlights so you can see the road and be seen by others with less glare.

question: What is the legal blood alcohol concentration (BAC) limit for a person age 21 or older?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: In most U.S. states, it is illegal for drivers age 21 or older to operate a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher. Even lower levels can impair driving, but 0.08% is the typical legal limit for DUI for adults.

question: A 'Merging lanes' sign is intended to tell drivers to:
options: a:Be prepared to change lanes or allow other traffic to merge.,b:Come to a complete stop before merging.,c:Speed up to prevent merging traffic from entering.,d:Ignore other vehicles when merging.
note: A merging lanes sign warns that two traffic lanes will soon become one. You should be ready to adjust speed, change lanes if needed, and create space so vehicles can merge smoothly and safely.

question: Always signal when:
options: a:Only when other vehicles are nearby.,b:Only when turning at an intersection.,c:Always when changing lanes, turning, or entering/exiting traffic.
note: You must always signal before changing lanes so other drivers know your intentions and can adjust safely. You should also signal before turning, entering or leaving a parking space, and when pulling into or out of traffic from a curb, driveway, or alley.
