question: Which foot should you use for both braking and accelerating?
options: a:Alternate feet depending on speed.,b:Use your left foot for braking.,c:Use your right foot for both acceleration and braking.,d:Always use both feet simultaneously.
note: Use your right foot for both the accelerator and the brake. This helps prevent accidentally pressing both pedals at once and gives you better control when switching between speeding up and slowing down.

question: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:
options: a:Only increased vehicle noise.,b:Excessive oil use.,c:Carbon monoxide poisoning.
note: A leaky exhaust system can let carbon monoxide enter the passenger area. Carbon monoxide is colorless and odorless and can quickly cause sickness, unconsciousness, or death, so exhaust leaks must be repaired immediately.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended you must:
options: a:Turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.,b:Only lock the doors.,c:Leave the engine running if warm.,d:Just set the parking brake.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended, stop the engine, lock it, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

question: If the rear of your vehicle starts to skid left, how should you steer?
options: a:Do not turn the steering wheel at all.,b:Turn the steering wheel sharply to the right.,c:Turn the steering wheel to the left (in the direction of the skid).
note: If the rear of your vehicle skids, you should ease off the accelerator, avoid hard braking, and steer in the direction the rear is sliding. If the rear moves left, steer left. This helps realign the vehicle and regain traction and control.

question: You should yield to a pedestrian:
options: a:Only when pedestrian signals favor them.,b:At all times if needed to avoid striking them.,c:Only if they are in a marked crosswalk.
note: You must always be prepared to yield to pedestrians to avoid hitting them, even if they are crossing illegally or against a signal. Drivers have a duty to use care and do whatever is reasonably necessary to prevent a collision with a pedestrian.

question: What does a flashing yellow X lane-use signal mean?
options: a:You may use the indicated lane only to complete a left turn.,b:The lane is closed to all traffic.,c:The signal is about to change to a red X.,d:You must speed up to clear the lane.
note: A flashing yellow X over a lane means that lane is for left turns only. You may enter and use that lane only to make a left turn; it is not for through traffic or passing.

question: When is walking or standing on the traveled portion of an expressway permitted?
options: a:When your car has stalled.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:When you are trying to wave down another car.
note: You must never walk or stand on the traveled lanes of an expressway. If your vehicle becomes disabled, move it and yourself as far off the roadway as possible and call for help; do not remain or walk in the traffic lanes.

question: When roads are slippery, what adjustment should you make to your following distance?
options: a:Drive as you would on dry roads.,b:Use alternate routes.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: On slippery roads, your tires have less traction and it takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance so you have more time and space to react and brake smoothly.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving typically:
options: a:Are always aware of the risks.,b:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies, minds, or the vehicle.,c:Are better drivers because they are more careful.
note: Alcohol slows brain and body functions, harming judgment, vision, coordination, and reaction time. A driver who has been drinking does not have full control over themselves or the vehicle and is unsafe to drive.

question: If you are in a line of traffic crossing an unprotected railroad track, what must you ensure?
options: a:You have enough space to get completely across the tracks without stopping.,b:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.,c:You have the right-of-way and do not need to look for trains.
note: Never enter a railroad crossing unless there is enough room on the far side for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks. You must be able to cross completely without stopping on the tracks.

question: At night it is hardest to see:
options: a:Pedestrians,b:Road signs,c:Other motorists
note: Pedestrians are unlit, often wear dark clothing, and can appear suddenly from between parked cars or at poorly lit crossings. At night, headlights and streetlights make reflective road signs and other vehicles much easier to see than people on foot, so you must scan carefully for pedestrians.

question: Consistently looking far down the highway while driving helps you do what?
options: a:Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.,b:Reduce the need for last-minute braking or turning.,c:Helps you keep up with traffic.
note: Looking well ahead lets you see slow traffic, signals, and hazards early so you can ease off the gas or change lanes smoothly. This reduces sudden braking or swerving and gives you more time and space to react safely.

question: What is the safest approach to crossing a railroad track?
options: a:Look and listen for trains in both directions and obey all warning signals.,b:Listen only.,c:Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
note: At railroad crossings, you must both look and listen for trains in both directions and obey all warning devices. Never try to beat a train or cross when lights are flashing, gates are down, or you can hear or see a train approaching. Only proceed when you are sure the tracks are clear and you have enough space to fully cross without stopping on the tracks.

question: True or false: The faster your vehicle is moving, the longer it takes to stop after reacting to unexpected movements by other drivers.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Stopping distance has two parts: the distance you travel while reacting and the distance your vehicle needs to brake to a stop. Both increase as speed increases, so at higher speeds you travel much farther before you can stop, giving you less margin to avoid hazards.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:New drivers,b:Bad weather,c:Human error
note: Most crashes are caused by driver mistakes such as inattention, speeding, following too closely, or failing to yield. While weather and road conditions matter, human error is the primary factor in the majority of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you arrive at an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and drive through cautiously without stopping.,b:Come to a full stop,c:Turn right only.,d:Wait for a flashing green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing red light means you must treat the intersection like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield as required, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: At dawn, dusk, or in precipitation you can help others see you by turning on:
options: a:Your parking lights only,b:The instrument panel lights,c:Your headlights
note: Use headlights when visibility is reduced so other drivers can see your vehicle.

question: To increase visibility in rain or fog, drivers should use:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: In rain or fog, use low beam headlights. High beams can reflect off water droplets or fog and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams help you see the road and allow other drivers to see you more clearly.

question: A double solid yellow line down the center of the road means passing is:
options: a:Not allowed from either direction.,b:Allowed in one direction only.,c:Allowed from both directions.
note: A double solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means you must not pass from either direction. You may cross it only when making a left turn or entering/exiting a driveway or side road when it is safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it safer to cross as few lanes as possible when making a turn?
options: a:False,b:True
note: It is safer to cross as few lanes as possible when turning. Start from the correct lane and turn into the nearest legal lane in your direction of travel. This reduces your exposure to traffic and makes your path more predictable to other drivers.

question: To avoid last-minute braking and turning, you should look how far ahead of your vehicle?
options: a:One to three seconds,b:Five to seven seconds,c:10 to 15 seconds
note: You should scan the road about 10 to 15 seconds ahead so you can see hazards early and have time to brake or change lanes smoothly instead of making sudden last‑minute moves.

question: Why should you avoid following other cars too closely?
options: a:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.,b:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.,c:You may not see the road between the cars.
note: You must leave enough space so you can stop safely if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. Following too closely, or tailgating, greatly increases the risk of a rear‑end collision because you may not have enough time or distance to react and brake.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is heading toward you in your lane, what actions should you take?
options: a:Speed up and swerve into oncoming traffic.,b:Turn on your lights and flash them while braking and steering to the right.,c:Steer right, slow or stop, and use your horn and lights to warn the other driver.,d:Blow your horn.
note: If a vehicle is coming toward you in your lane, your first priority is to avoid a head‑on collision by moving to the right and slowing or stopping. Use your horn and lights to get the other driver’s attention, brake firmly, and steer to the right shoulder or off the road if needed. Never speed up or swerve into the oncoming lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When backing up, how should you control your speed?
options: a:Drive faster than usual.,b:Drive much more slowly than usual.
note: When backing, your view and control are reduced, so you must move no faster than a slow walking speed and check carefully in all directions to avoid hitting pedestrians, vehicles, or objects.

question: Which technique is most important to avoid crashes when roads are icy or snowy?
options: a:Reduce your speed and increase following distance.,b:Add extra weight to your vehicle to improve traction.,c:Get off the highways as quickly as possible.
note: On snow or ice, the most important crash‑prevention technique is to slow down and leave much more following distance. Slower speeds and extra space give you time to react and reduce the chance of skidding. Adding weight may slightly change traction but is not a primary safety method, and you do not need to leave highways unless conditions are impassable.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is a good general rule for passing other vehicles?
options: a:Pass on the right whenever possible.,b:Try to get to the front of slow traffic to see better.,c:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.
note: Driving with the flow of traffic within the speed limit and passing only when necessary is safer than frequently changing lanes. Every pass creates additional risk because you spend time in other drivers’ blind spots and may face oncoming traffic on two‑lane roads. Pass only when you have a clear need, good visibility, and enough space to complete the maneuver safely.

question: You should avoid driving beside large vehicles for extended periods because:
options: a:They have large blind spots on both sides.,b:They drive much slower than cars.,c:They always signal early when changing lanes.
note: Large trucks and buses have very large blind spots along both sides, especially on the right side and close alongside the cab and trailer. If you drive next to them for a long time, the driver may not see you and could change lanes into your vehicle. It is safer to either drop back or move ahead so you are clearly visible.

question: Construction zone signs are typically what shape and color?
options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange background and black lettering.,b:Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.,c:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
note: Work zone and construction signs are temporary warning signs. They are usually diamond‑shaped (sometimes rectangular) with an orange background and black letters or symbols. The orange color alerts drivers to road work, lane shifts, workers, or equipment ahead so they can slow down and proceed with extra caution.

question: On average, how quickly does the body eliminate alcohol?
options: a:Three alcoholic drinks per hour.,b:One standard alcoholic drink per hour.,c:Two alcoholic drinks per hour.
note: The body typically processes alcohol at about the rate of one standard drink per hour, but this can vary widely based on body size, sex, food in the stomach, health, and other factors. Nothing—coffee, cold showers, or exercise—can speed this up. Because you cannot reliably predict your own rate, the safest choice is not to drive after drinking.

question: A red-and-white triangular sign at an intersection indicates:
options: a:Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.,b:Always come to a full stop at the intersection.,c:Yield and be prepared to stop if necessary.
note: A red‑and‑white triangle sign is a yield sign. When you see it, you must slow down, look for traffic and pedestrians, and yield the right‑of‑way to cross traffic. Be prepared to stop if necessary, but you are not always required to come to a complete stop if the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A 'No stopping' sign means you may stop only for which reason?
options: a:To discharge passengers.,b:To unload packages.,c:To avoid conflict with other traffic.
note: A No Stopping sign means you may not stop your vehicle on that part of the roadway for any reason except when it is absolutely necessary to obey a traffic control device, follow a police officer’s directions, or avoid a conflict or collision with other traffic. You may not stop there just to load or unload passengers or goods.

question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:
options: a:Safe if you've had only a couple of drinks.,b:A minor safety issue.,c:Acceptable if you drive slowly.,d:A serious traffic safety problem.
note: Driving after drinking alcohol is a serious traffic safety problem because alcohol slows reaction time, impairs judgment, and reduces coordination. Even a small amount can affect driving ability and greatly increases the risk of a crash.

question: A double solid yellow centerline on a two-lane road indicates what?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.
note: A double solid yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means no passing is allowed for vehicles traveling in either direction. You may cross the lines only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe and not prohibited by other signs.

question: What is the most common color used for warning signs?
options: a:Red.,b:Yellow with black markings.,c:Green.
note: Most general warning signs are yellow with black symbols or lettering and are often diamond-shaped. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards, changes in road conditions, or special situations so drivers can slow down and proceed with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Excessive speed typically:
options: a:Increases the likelihood of serious injury or death.,b:Saves significant travel time.,c:Helps maneuver around obstacles safely.
note: Excessive speed increases both the chance of a crash and the severity of any injuries because it takes longer to stop and impacts are more forceful. Speeding usually saves little time but greatly increases risk to you and others on the road.

question: When must you stop for a school bus?
options: a:When the bus is parked on the shoulder with no one aboard.,b:When driving on a two-lane highway and the bus's red lights are flashing.,c:Whenever the bus approaches even if its lights are not flashing.
note: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm when you are approaching from either direction on a two‑lane road, or on most undivided roads. You do not stop if the bus is simply parked with no lights flashing and no children boarding or exiting.

question: When parked uphill with a curb, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels slightly to the right.,b:Turn the wheels sharply away from the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels sharply toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels sharply away from the curb. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will contact the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: Which of the following can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,b:Tranquilizers.,c:All of the above.
note: Many medicines and drugs can make you drowsy, slow your reactions, or affect your judgment. Cough syrups and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines, as well as tranquilizers, can all impair your ability to drive safely, even when taken as directed.

question: You are about to turn right and a person with a guide dog is at the corner ready to cross. You should:
options: a:Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before turning.,b:Tell the pedestrian when to cross.,c:Turn off your engine until they cross.,d:Edge around them slowly while they cross.
note: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes must be given the right-of-way; wait for them to cross.

question: Which factor significantly affects your ability to stop quickly?
options: a:Signal lights ahead.,b:The time of day.,c:Road conditions (such as wet, icy, or gravel surfaces).
note: Your stopping distance depends heavily on road conditions. Wet, icy, or gravel surfaces greatly increase the distance it takes to stop, so you must slow down and increase your following distance when traction is reduced.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, you may:
options: a:Cross the centerline to change lanes when safe.,b:Only drive within your lane at all times.,c:Change lanes only from the left lane.
note: A single broken white centerline separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling.

question: What should you keep in mind when driving on gravel or dirt roads?
options: a:Your tires grip the road better than on pavement.,b:Your tires have less traction than on pavement,c:Visibility is better than on pavement.
note: On gravel or dirt roads, the loose surface reduces traction compared to paved roads. Because your tires grip less, you should slow down, increase following distance, and steer and brake gently to avoid skidding.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of drug?
options: a:Antihistamine.,b:Stimulant.,c:Depressant.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant. It slows brain and body functions, reducing judgment, coordination, and reaction time, which makes driving unsafe even at relatively low blood alcohol levels.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, you should:
options: a:Blow your horn to warn approaching cars.,b:Pull out quickly to merge smoothly with traffic.,c:Yield to pedestrians and traffic already on the roadway.
note: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, you must stop if needed and yield the right‑of‑way to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway. Enter only when there is a safe gap in traffic.

question: When passing another vehicle, you should return to your lane only when:
options: a:Two seconds have passed since beginning the pass.,b:You can no longer see the vehicle in your side mirror.,c:You cross directly in front of the passed vehicle's hood.,d:The entire passed vehicle is visible in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your inside rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space and do not cut off the other driver.

question: When passing a large truck, what should a driver of a smaller vehicle be ready for?
options: a:Loud noises only.,b:Extra exhaust pollution.,c:Gusts of wind that can affect your steering.
note: Large trucks push a lot of air around them. As you pass, you may feel a strong gust that can pull or push your smaller vehicle sideways. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to make small corrections so you stay in your lane.

question: Which of the following can be a telltale sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Driving more slowly than the normal traffic flow.,b:Making quick and sudden stops.,c:Weaving between lanes.,d:Any of the above.
note: Impaired drivers often show several warning behaviors, including driving much slower than surrounding traffic, making quick or sudden stops without reason, and weaving between lanes. Any of these can be a telltale sign of a drunk driver, so you should increase your following distance and avoid driving close to them.

question: Why should you look farther ahead when driving on a freeway compared with a city street?
options: a:Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop your vehicle completely.,b:Because it helps you keep up with traffic.,c:To spot potential hazards early.
note: On freeways, speeds are higher and situations develop more quickly. Looking farther ahead gives you more time to see slow traffic, crashes, or merging vehicles early so you can adjust smoothly instead of braking or swerving at the last second.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a gap in traffic on a highway, what should you do?
options: a:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.,b:Speed up and force your way into the gap.,c:Check traffic behind, to the sides, and ahead, then adjust your speed to merge safely.
note: To enter a gap in highway traffic safely, you must check traffic all around you—behind, to the sides, and ahead—then adjust your speed so you can merge smoothly into the gap without forcing other drivers to brake hard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the best practice when merging onto a freeway?
options: a:Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.,b:Turn on hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.,c:Stop at the end of the on-ramp and wait for an opening.,d:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic and merge smoothly.
note: When merging onto a freeway, use the on‑ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, signal, and then merge into a safe gap. Entering traffic must yield to vehicles already on the freeway, so do not stop at the end of the ramp unless absolutely necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another car, you have enough space to return to your lane when:
options: a:You can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:The other driver signals you to return.,c:If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car.
note: You should not move back into your original lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed clearly in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have created enough space so that when you return to the lane, you will not cut off the other driver or force them to brake suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to reach the exit.,b:Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.,c:Continue driving and use the next exit.
note: If you miss your exit on the interstate, stay calm, keep going, and take the next exit. Never stop, back up on the highway, cut across lanes at the last second, or make a U‑turn on the interstate. Continuing to the next exit and re‑routing is the only safe and legal option.

question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed to be driven.,b:Potential driving speeds for the area,c:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic.
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum (and sometimes minimum) speed allowed under ideal conditions. You are not required to drive at the posted limit if conditions are poor; you must slow down for rain, fog, traffic, or other hazards, even if that means driving below the posted limit.

question: Is nighttime the safest time for cyclists to ride their bikes?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Nighttime is more dangerous for cyclists because visibility is reduced and drivers have a harder time seeing bicycles. Cyclists should use lights and reflectors and ride defensively, and drivers should be extra alert for bikes after dark.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a train is close enough to be dangerous, you must:
options: a:Slow and proceed with caution if you think you can beat it.,b:Cross at your own risk if no lights are flashing.,c:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
note: If a train is close enough to be dangerous, you must stop and wait until it has completely passed and you can see that the tracks are clear in both directions. Trains cannot stop quickly, and trying to beat a train is extremely dangerous and illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you have the legal right-of-way at an intersection, what is the safest action?
options: a:Assume others will yield to you.,b:Check for traffic.,c:Proceed immediately because you have the right-of-way.
note: Having the legal right-of-way never guarantees that other drivers will yield. The safest action is to slow if needed and check for traffic, pedestrians, and bicyclists before entering the intersection. You must be prepared to yield to avoid a collision, even when you are legally entitled to proceed.

question: You discover a defect that could affect safe operation of your vehicle. What should you do?
options: a:Delay repairs until it becomes severe.,b:Drive more slowly until you can afford to fix it.,c:Correct the defect as soon as possible.
note: Any defect that could affect the safe operation of your vehicle should be repaired as soon as possible and ideally before driving again. Driving with known safety defects, even at lower speeds, increases your risk of a crash and may be illegal if the vehicle is unsafe.

question: Guide (destination) signs are typically what color?
options: a:Green.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.
note: Guide or destination signs are typically green with white lettering. They provide information such as route directions, distances, and exits to help you navigate to cities, streets, and points of interest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When you cannot see any vehicle directly to your right.,b:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:When you have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.
note: After passing, you should not move back into your original lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space ahead of that vehicle to return safely without cutting them off.

question: After a minor collision with no injuries and little damage at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if possible.,b:Leave your vehicle where it stopped until police arrive.,c:Not move your vehicle at any cost.
note: After a minor collision with no injuries, if the vehicles are drivable and it is safe, you should move them out of the traffic lane. This helps prevent additional crashes, reduces congestion, and allows emergency responders better access if needed.

question: Which of the following is illegal for a passenger in a moving motor vehicle?
options: a:Have an opened alcohol container.,b:Sleep.,c:Use a cell phone.
note: Open container laws in most U.S. states make it illegal for anyone in a moving vehicle—driver or passenger—to possess or consume alcohol from an open container on a public road. Passengers may legally sleep or use a cell phone, but having an open alcoholic beverage is prohibited.

question: True or False: A motorist making a left turn must yield to oncoming bicyclists.
options: a:True,b:False
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic, including bicyclists approaching from the opposite direction. Bicycles are treated as vehicles and have the same right‑of‑way rules, so you must wait until it is safe before completing your turn.

question: Are most work zone signs orange in color?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Most temporary work zone and construction signs are orange with black symbols or lettering. The bright orange color and reflective material help alert drivers to road work, lane shifts, and workers ahead so they can slow down and proceed with caution.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes of traffic indicate?
options: a:Traffic moves in opposite directions.,b:Drivers may change lanes or pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Passing is prohibited from either direction.,d:You must stop before crossing it.
note: A single dashed white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling your intention.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a painted stop line at an intersection, you should stop:
options: a:On top of the stop line.,b:Past the stop line into the intersection.,c:Before the stop line.
note: At a painted stop line, you must bring your vehicle to a complete stop before the line. This keeps you out of the crosswalk area, protects pedestrians, and ensures you obey the intersection’s traffic control markings.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, you should:
options: a:Open all windows and drive faster.,b:Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.,c:Turn up the radio and drive on.,d:Increase your speed to finish sooner.
note: When drowsy, stop in a safe area and rest; driving tired is dangerous.

question: To be able to turn quickly and safely, where should your hands be on the steering wheel?
options: a:On the top and bottom of the wheel.,b:Next to each other on the top of the wheel.,c:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
note: To turn quickly and safely, your hands should be on opposite sides of the steering wheel, typically around the 9 and 3 o’clock positions. This gives you better leverage, control, and balance when steering, especially in emergencies. Avoid placing both hands at the top or one hand at the bottom, as that reduces control and can make sudden maneuvers unsafe.

question: Which statement about a work zone is correct?
options: a:You do not need to slow down when approaching a work zone.,b:Work zones are marked with black and white signs.,c:Work zones may be stationary or moving.
note: Work zones can be either stationary (such as a fixed construction area) or moving (such as line-painting or mowing operations). They are usually marked with orange signs, cones, and other devices. When approaching any work zone, you must slow down, obey posted work zone speed limits, and be prepared for sudden stops or workers and equipment near the roadway.

question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing and there is no traffic light?
options: a:The faster party must yield.,b:The driver must yield to the pedestrian.,c:The pedestrian must yield to the turning vehicle.,d:Whoever started moving last must yield.
note: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing the street at an intersection without a traffic light, the driver must yield. Pedestrians in a crosswalk—marked or unmarked at an intersection—have the right-of-way. The driver must slow or stop to let the pedestrian cross safely before completing the turn.

question: What message is displayed on a red octagonal sign?
options: a:One-way.,b:Stop.,c:Do not enter.
note: A red octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means STOP. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then proceed only when it is safe and after yielding to any pedestrians or other vehicles with the right-of-way.

question: To avoid hydroplaning in rainy conditions, you should:
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain steady speed.,b:Brake hard as soon as your car starts to skid.,c:Slow down and drive at a speed appropriate for wet roads.,d:Maintain your normal highway speed.
note: On wet roads, especially in heavy rain, you should slow down so your tires can maintain contact with the road surface and channel water out of the tread. Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water instead of the pavement, causing a loss of steering and braking control. Reducing speed and avoiding cruise control in the rain are key ways to prevent hydroplaning.

question: May you drive at night using only your parking lights instead of headlights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You must use your headlights when driving at night or whenever visibility is reduced (such as in rain, fog, or snow). Parking lights alone are not bright enough for safe driving and are not a legal substitute for headlights. Driving with only parking lights makes it harder for you to see the road and for others to see you, increasing the risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid yellow line next to your lane indicates:
options: a:Pass with extreme caution.,b:Passing from your direction is not permitted.,c:You should slow down.
note: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you may not pass vehicles ahead of you from your side of the road. The solid line marks a no‑passing zone for your direction of travel, usually because of limited visibility or other safety concerns. You must stay in your lane and only pass where passing is allowed and safe.

question: Where are trucks' blind spots typically located?
options: a:On the immediate left of the cab only.,b:On both sides near the cab and directly behind the truck.,c:Directly behind the body only.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots, often called “no‑zones,” along both sides of the truck (especially on the right), directly behind the trailer, and close in front of the cab. If you cannot see the truck driver’s face in the side mirror, the driver likely cannot see you. Avoid lingering in these areas and give trucks extra space when passing or following.

question: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, what should you do?
options: a:Call the police.,b:Determine if anyone is injured.,c:Stop.,d:All of the above.
note: If you are involved in a serious crash, you must stop immediately, check for injuries, and call 911 or the police when required by law. Do not leave the scene. If it is safe, move vehicles out of traffic to prevent another collision. Provide help within your ability, exchange information, and cooperate with law enforcement.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?
options: a:Only when changing lanes.,b:Only when you are slowing down.,c:Often
note: You should check your mirrors frequently so you always know what is happening behind and beside you. Regular mirror checks help you spot fast-approaching vehicles, lane changers, and potential hazards early, giving you more time to react safely.

question: When you see animals near the road while driving, you should:
options: a:Stop in the lane without warning other drivers.,b:Swerve suddenly into the next lane.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.,d:Speed up to scare them away.
note: When animals are near or on the road, slow down and be prepared to stop. Animals can move unpredictably or be followed by others, so proceeding cautiously reduces the chance of a collision and gives you and other drivers more time to react.

question: Only ____ can reduce BAC and alcohol's effects on the body.
options: a:Drinking coffee,b:Time,c:Eating fatty foods
note: Only time lowers your blood alcohol concentration. Your body must metabolize the alcohol; coffee, food, cold showers, or exercise do not make you sober faster and do not make it safe to drive.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Wait for a green light only.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop, but you should be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other vehicles if they are already in or entering the intersection.

question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, you should:
options: a:Tailgate slower drivers to express frustration.,b:Drive above the posted speed limit to avoid others.,c:Relax and focus on safe driving.
note: To avoid aggressive driving, give yourself plenty of time, stay calm, and focus on safety rather than speed or “winning” in traffic. Keeping a relaxed attitude helps you make better decisions and reduces the risk of road rage and dangerous maneuvers.

question: Should you use high beam headlights when driving in fog?
options: a:True,b:False
note: In fog, high beams reflect off the water droplets and create glare, making it harder to see. Use low-beam headlights or fog lights so the light stays lower on the road and improves your visibility without blinding you or other drivers.

question: Is the fatal accident rate higher for night driving compared with daytime driving?
options: a:False — daytime is more dangerous.,b:True — it is nearly three times greater at night.,c:Night and day rates are equal.,d:It depends only on traffic volume.
note: Night driving is more dangerous because visibility is reduced, depth perception and peripheral vision are worse, and drivers are more likely to be tired or impaired. Per mile driven, the fatal crash rate at night is significantly higher than during the day, so you should slow down and increase following distance after dark.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill next to a curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Keep the rear tires against the curb.,b:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,c:Turn your front wheels away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll back slightly and the front tire will rest against the curb, stopping the car from rolling into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If there is no marked crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane, how should you respond?
options: a:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.,b:Stop and allow the pedestrian to finish crossing.,c:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in the roadway, even if there is no marked crosswalk. Stop and let them finish crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If being passed in a no-passing zone, you should:
options: a:Slow down and allow the other driver to move back into the lane safely.,b:Pull off the road to let them pass, c:Speed up to prevent them from passing.
note: If another driver is passing you in a no-passing zone, do not speed up or block them. Maintain your lane and, if needed, ease off the accelerator so they can complete the pass and return to the lane safely, reducing the risk of a head-on collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as a driver on your left. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The driver on your left, because they were there first,b:You have the right of way — the driver to your left must yield to you,c:Whoever signals first proceeds first,d:The driver going straight always has priority
note: At a 4-way stop when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver to the RIGHT has the right of way. Since the other driver is to your LEFT, you are to their right — meaning you have the right of way and should proceed first.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass on a two-lane road, what should be your primary check?
options: a:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles.,b:Flash your headlights as you pass.,c:Sound your horn as you pass.,d:Assume oncoming traffic will slow down.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, your main concern is whether there is enough clear space ahead in the oncoming lane. Carefully judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles and only begin passing if you are sure you can complete the maneuver and return to your lane without forcing any other driver to slow or swerve.

question: On which road marking may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,b:You are on a hill or curve.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken center line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe. A solid line next to your lane means you must not pass, and you should never pass on hills, curves, or anywhere your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, you should move back into your original lane when:
options: a:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,b:You can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,d:The passing vehicle signals you to move over.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed (its headlights in the daytime or at night) in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead and do not cut off the other driver.

question: What do blue traffic signs generally indicate?
options: a:Regulatory requirements like speed limits.,b:Mileage distances to locations.,c:Construction and maintenance warnings.,d:Information on motorist services (rest areas, hospitals, food).
note: Blue traffic signs are service signs. They give information about motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals along the roadway.

question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic to merge safely?
options: a:Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.,b:Using only your rearview mirror.,c:Using your rearview and side mirrors without looking over your shoulder.
note: Before merging onto a freeway, use your mirrors and then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This helps you see vehicles that are not visible in your mirrors so you can choose a safe gap and merge smoothly.

question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do?
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn while being prepared to stop.,b:Flash your headlights.,c:Continue at the same speed.
note: If a child appears ready to run into the street, immediately cover the brake and be prepared to stop while giving a sharp blast of your horn to warn the child and others nearby. Use the horn to alert, but your primary responsibility is to slow or stop to avoid a collision.

question: What must you do when approaching a pedestrian who uses a guide dog or white cane?
options: a:Honk so they know to clear the way.,b:Swerve quickly around them.,c:Yield the right-of-way.
note: Stop and give the blind pedestrian the right-of-way; do not honk or attempt to steer around them abruptly.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of substance?
options: a:A depressant.,b:A stimulant.,c:An antihistamine.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant. It slows brain activity and impairs judgment, coordination, and reaction time, making it dangerous to drive after drinking.

question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood may affect which abilities?
options: a:Right-of-way privileges.,b:Judgment and physical coordination.,c:Knowledge.
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect your judgment and physical coordination, even if you do not feel drunk. Because driving requires quick decisions and precise control, even small amounts of alcohol can make driving unsafe.

question: When is using your horn appropriate?
options: a:When it may help prevent a collision.,b:When another driver makes a mistake.,c:When another vehicle is in your way and you want them to move.
note: Use your horn only to alert others to a potential collision or to warn of immediate danger. Do not use it to show anger, impatience, or to punish other drivers for mistakes.

question: What does a green arrow signal require you to do?
options: a:Proceed immediately without yielding.,b:Ignore any pedestrians in the intersection.,c:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,d:Yield to vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians in the intersection, then complete the turn.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected movement in the direction of the arrow, but you must still yield to any vehicles, bicyclists, or pedestrians already in the intersection before you complete your turn.

question: Why is winter driving more hazardous than other seasons?
options: a:There are increased hours of darkness.,b:Road conditions can be affected by freezing temperatures, ice, snow, and fog.,c:Both of the above.
note: Winter driving is more dangerous because there are more hours of darkness and road surfaces can become slippery or obscured by ice, snow, and fog. These conditions reduce traction and visibility, requiring slower speeds and greater following distances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What general attitude should a driver have about right-of-way rules?
options: a:Assume most drivers obey the right-of-way rules.,b:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.,c:Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.
note: Right-of-way laws say who should go first, but they do not guarantee that others will follow them. Safe drivers always stay ready to yield, even when they legally have the right-of-way, if yielding will prevent a collision.

question: If a tire blows out suddenly while you're driving, what steps should you take?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and exit the traffic lane slowly.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly to stop quickly.,c:Brake hard and steer immediately to the right edge.,d:Turn on your hazards and speed up to reach the shoulder faster.
note: When a tire blows out, the car may pull to one side. Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down. Once it is under control and speed has dropped, steer gradually off the road and brake gently if needed. Sudden hard braking or sharp steering can cause loss of control.

question: What is the only thing that can reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time,b:Eating foods high in fat,c:Drinking caffeine
note: Once alcohol is in your system, only time allows your body to metabolize it and lower your BAC. Food, coffee, cold showers, or exercise may make you feel more awake but do not speed up the elimination of alcohol.

question: When ridden on public roadways, bicycles are legally classified as:
options: a:Pedestrians.,b:Vehicles.,c:Hazards.,d:Motor vehicles.
note: Bicycles ridden on public roads are treated as vehicles. Cyclists must obey traffic signals, signs, lane markings, and right‑of‑way rules just like drivers of cars, including stopping at red lights and stop signs and riding in the same direction as traffic.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part seat belt, how should you wear it?
options: a:Use only the shoulder belt.,b:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,c:Use only the lap belt.
note: If your vehicle has both a lap belt and a shoulder belt, you must wear both. The lap belt should be low and snug across the hips, and the shoulder belt should cross the chest and shoulder, not the neck or under the arm. Using only one part greatly reduces protection in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn prohibited?
options: a:On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:In a parking lot.
note: You must not make a U‑turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot see far enough ahead to be sure it is safe. Limited visibility makes it hard to judge oncoming traffic and can lead to serious head‑on collisions.

question: Driving noticeably slower than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:Often a hazard because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.,b:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.,c:A good idea if the weather is bad, but you must not drive so slowly that you unnecessarily block or endanger other traffic.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because other drivers may not expect it and may make sudden or risky lane changes or passing maneuvers. You should generally travel at the speed of traffic (within the speed limit) and adjust your speed reasonably for conditions, such as bad weather, without becoming an unnecessary obstruction.

question: What qualifies as a driving distraction?
options: a:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: A driving distraction is anything that takes your attention away from the driving task—your eyes from the road, your mind from driving, or your hands from the wheel. Examples include texting, eating, adjusting controls, or focusing on passengers instead of traffic.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Both lanes may pass.,b:The lane to the right may pass.,c:Neither lane may pass.
note: A double solid yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross these lines only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you want to change lanes, which action should you never do?
options: a:Move into another lane while within an intersection.,b:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: You should not change lanes while you are in an intersection because traffic movements are more complex and other drivers may not expect a lane change there. Instead, change lanes before or after the intersection, and always check mirrors, blind spots, and signal first.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what should you do to re-enter safely?
options: a:Wait until it is safe to do so, then gradually re-enter the roadway.,b:Turn back onto the roadway immediately.,c:Stop.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and keep a firm grip on the wheel. When traffic allows, gently steer back onto the pavement at a shallow angle. Do not jerk the wheel or brake hard, as that can cause you to lose control.

question: Which headlights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: In rain, fog, snow, or sleet, use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and can create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams help you see the road and help other drivers see you without excessive glare.

question: Which driving skills are impaired by alcohol or drug use?
options: a:Alertness.,b:Coordination.,c:Both of the above.
note: Alcohol and many drugs slow your reaction time and make it harder to stay alert and coordinate steering, braking, and acceleration. Because both alertness and coordination are affected, your overall ability to drive safely is reduced.

question: What is the law regarding posters and signs on car windows?
options: a:Are a fun way to personalize your vehicle.,b:Are prohibited by state law if they obstruct a driver's view of the road.,c:Are allowed only if they do not contain offensive language.
note: State law prohibits placing signs or materials on vehicle windows that obstruct the driver's clear view of the roadway.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection tells you to:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,c:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop unless needed for other traffic, pedestrians, or to avoid a hazard.

question: How do you drive defensively?
options: a:Put one car length between you and the car ahead.,b:Look only at the car in front of you while driving.,c:Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road ahead, behind, and to the sides so you can spot potential hazards early. By keeping your eyes moving and checking mirrors, you have more time to react and avoid collisions.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what safety checks should you perform?
options: a:Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,b:Buckle your safety belt.,c:Both of the above.
note: Before starting the vehicle, you should always buckle your own seat belt and make sure all passengers are properly buckled. This simple habit greatly reduces the risk of injury in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian starts crossing after the \Don't Walk\" signal begins flashing and is in the middle of the street when your light turns green. What should you do?"
options: a:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,b:Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before proceeding.,c:Proceed since you have the green and the pedestrian is mid-street.,d:Honk to make the pedestrian hurry.
note: If a pedestrian is in the intersection when your light turns green, allow them to finish crossing before you proceed.

question: You should avoid using your horn when driving near:
options: a:Drivers whose visibility ahead is limited.,b:Blind pedestrians.,c:Vehicles about to collide with you.,d:Pedestrians in crosswalks at night.
note: You should not use your horn around blind pedestrians because they rely heavily on sound cues to understand traffic movement. A sudden horn blast can be confusing or frightening. Instead, slow down, yield, and pass only when it is clearly safe.

question: Reaction time is slower after which of the following?
options: a:Drinking alcohol.,b:Sleeping.,c:Working hard.
note: Alcohol slows your brain’s processing and your body’s reflexes, so it takes longer to notice hazards and react. Even small amounts of alcohol can increase reaction time and reduce your ability to drive safely.

question: Which factor listed affects how alcohol is absorbed into the body?
options: a:Height,b:Weight,c:Intelligence
note: Body weight is one of the main factors that affects how alcohol is absorbed and how strongly it affects you. In general, a smaller person will reach a higher blood alcohol concentration than a larger person after drinking the same amount.
